title: PAUDBLOD / LOADPADB - load pending-authorization IMS DB from sequential files
description:
##### Entry point
JCL **LOADPADB** (`app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl/LOADPADB.JCL`) STEP01 `EXEC PGM=DFSRRC00,PARM='BMP,PAUDBLOD,PSBPAUTB'`. Program **PAUDBLOD** (batch) entered via `PROCEDURE DIVISION USING IO-PCB-MASK PAUTBPCB` / `ENTRY 'DLITCBL' USING PAUTBPCB`.

##### Inputs
- **INFILE1** (SELECT INFILE1 ASSIGN TO INFILE1, sequential; DD DSN AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.FILEO) - INFIL1-REC X(100) = CIPAUSMY summary image.
- **INFILE2** (DD DSN AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.FILEO) - 206 bytes: ROOT-SEG-KEY S9(11) COMP-3 (6 bytes, account id) + CHILD-SEG-REC X(200) = CIPAUDTY detail image.
- PSB PSBPAUTB, PCB PAUTBPCB (PROCOPT=AP) on DBPAUTP0.

##### Processing flow
1. `1000-INITIALIZE`: dates; OPEN INPUT INFILE1 and INFILE2; status not spaces/'00' -> 9999-ABEND.
2. Loop `2000-READ-ROOT-SEG-FILE` until END-ROOT-SEG-FILE='Y': READ INFILE1; OK -> move to PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY, `2100-INSERT-ROOT-SEG`: `CBLTDLI ISRT PAUTBPCB PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY ROOT-UNQUAL-SSA`; spaces = inserted; 'II' (duplicate) = displayed, continue; other -> abend. Status '10' -> end. Any other file status: neither branch - loop re-reads (no abend).
3. Loop `3000-READ-CHILD-SEG-FILE` until END-CHILD-SEG-FILE='Y': READ INFILE2; OK and ROOT-SEG-KEY NUMERIC -> QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE = key, detail to PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS, `3100-INSERT-CHILD-SEG`: `CBLTDLI GU PAUTBPCB PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY ROOT-QUAL-SSA` (`PAUTSUM0(ACCNTID EQ <packed key>)`); spaces -> `3200-INSERT-IMS-CALL` (`ISRT PAUTBPCB PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS CHILD-UNQUAL-SSA`; spaces ok, 'II' duplicate displayed, other abend); GU status other than spaces/'II' (e.g. 'GE' parent missing) -> abend. Non-numeric key -> record skipped. '10' -> end.
4. `4000-FILE-CLOSE`: CLOSE both, display status. GOBACK.
5. `9999-ABEND`: RETURN-CODE 16, GOBACK.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  J[LOADPADB DFSRRC00 BMP,PAUDBLOD,PSBPAUTB] --> I[1000-INITIALIZE OPEN INFILE1 INFILE2]
  I --> R[2000-READ-ROOT-SEG-FILE READ INFILE1]
  R -->|OK| RI[2100 CBLTDLI ISRT PAUTSUM0] -->|ok / II| R
  RI -->|other| AB[9999-ABEND RC16]
  R -->|10 EOF| C[3000-READ-CHILD-SEG-FILE READ INFILE2]
  C -->|OK numeric key| GU[3100 CBLTDLI GU PAUTSUM0 ACCNTID EQ key]
  GU -->|ok| CI[3200 ISRT PAUTDTL1] -->|ok / II| C
  GU -->|not found etc| AB
  CI -->|other| AB
  C -->|10 EOF| CL[4000-FILE-CLOSE / GOBACK]
```

##### Data
Writes DBPAUTP0 PAUTSUM0 roots and PAUTDTL1 children (layouts CIPAUSMY / CIPAUDTY). Reads two sequential files above.

##### Outputs & side effects
Loaded IMS database; SYSOUT messages; RC 16 on fatal error. No checkpoints taken (single unit of work for BMP).

##### External calls
IMS `CBLTDLI` ISRT/GU. None other.

##### Migration notes
- Duplicate segments ('II') are tolerated, not counted as errors.
- Unexpected (non-00/non-10) READ status on either file causes a tight re-read loop rather than an abend.
- Child records with non-numeric packed key are skipped silently.
- No CHKP in a BMP load - large loads hold all locks/updates until end.
- Expected INFILE2 format (key+detail) differs from DBUNLDGS child GSAM output (detail only).
- Program DISPLAYs name 'IMSUNLOD' (WS-PGMNAME) not PAUDBLOD.
recommendation: Fully traced. Decide whether to keep tolerance of duplicates and silent skips.
note:
Consolidated document for app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/cbl/PAUDBLOD.CBL, app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl/LOADPADB.JCL; merged duplicates: sfind-ee137b17e1cc423ca168d74739707d5c.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Silent skip of orphan children**: in 3100 the abend check is nested inside `IF PAUT-PCB-STATUS = SPACES` (no END-IF; period ends both), so when the parent GU fails (e.g., 'GE') nothing is logged except the banner and the child is skipped without abend.
- Duplicates ('II') are tolerated for both roots and children.
- A persistent non-EOF read error loops forever (status re-read without abend).
- Root and child loads are two independent passes; children rely on roots already present.

title: COBTUPDT / MNTTRDB2 - batch maintenance of DB2 CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
description:
##### Entry point
JCL **MNTTRDB2** (`app/app-transaction-type-db2/jcl/MNTTRDB2.jcl`) STEP1 `EXEC PGM=IKJEFT01` with SYSTSIN `DSN SYSTEM(DAZ1)` / `RUN PROGRAM(COBTUPDT) PLAN(CARDDEMO)`. Program **COBTUPDT** (batch DB2, no linkage).

##### Inputs
DD **INPFILE** (`SELECT TR-RECORD ASSIGN TO INPFILE`, sequential, RECFM F; JCL DSN=INPFILE,DISP=SHR) read INTO WS-INPUT-REC:
| Col | Field | PIC | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | INPUT-REC-TYPE | X | A=add, U=update, D=delete, *=comment |
| 2-3 | INPUT-REC-NUMBER | X(2) | TR_TYPE |
| 4-53 | INPUT-REC-DESC | X(50) | TR_DESCRIPTION |

##### Processing flow
1. `0001-OPEN-FILES`: OPEN INPUT; DISPLAY OK/NOT OK (no stop on failure). Falls through to next paragraph.
2. `1001-READ-NEXT-RECORDS`: priming `1002-READ-RECORDS` (AT END LASTREC='Y'; DISPLAY 'PROCESSING' record), then loop `1003-TREAT-RECORD` + read until LASTREC='Y'; `2001-CLOSE-STOP`; STOP RUN.
3. `1003-TREAT-RECORD` EVALUATE INPUT-REC-TYPE: 'A' -> `10031-INSERT-DB` (`INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE (TR_TYPE, TR_DESCRIPTION) VALUES (:INPUT-REC-NUMBER, :INPUT-REC-DESC)`; SQLCODE 0 success msg; <0 error msg + 9999-ABEND; >0 nothing); 'U' -> `10032-UPDATE-DB` (`UPDATE ... SET TR_DESCRIPTION=:INPUT-REC-DESC WHERE TR_TYPE=:INPUT-REC-NUMBER`; 0 ok, +100 'No records found.' + 9999-ABEND, <0 error + abend); 'D' -> `10033-DELETE-DB` (`DELETE ... WHERE TR_TYPE=:INPUT-REC-NUMBER`; same handling); '*' -> DISPLAY 'IGNORING COMMENTED LINE'; other -> 'ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID' + 9999-ABEND.
4. `9999-ABEND`: DISPLAY WS-RETURN-MSG, RETURN-CODE=4, **returns and processing continues** with the next record.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  J[MNTTRDB2 IKJEFT01 DSN RUN COBTUPDT PLAN CARDDEMO] --> O[0001-OPEN-FILES INPFILE]
  O --> R[1002-READ-RECORDS]
  R -->|EOF| C[2001-CLOSE-STOP / STOP RUN]
  R --> T{1003-TREAT-RECORD type}
  T -->|A| I[10031 INSERT TRANSACTION_TYPE]
  T -->|U| U[10032 UPDATE]
  T -->|D| D[10033 DELETE]
  T -->|*| R
  T -->|other| AB[9999-ABEND RC=4 display]
  I & U & D -->|SQLCODE<0 or +100 U/D| AB
  I & U & D -->|0| R
  AB --> R
```

##### Data
DB2 table CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE (DDL TRNTYPE.ddl): TR_TYPE CHAR(2) NOT NULL PK, TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL. DCLGEN DCLTRTYP (DCL-TR-TYPE X(2), DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION varchar LEN S9(4) COMP + TEXT) is included but not used - host variables are the input-record fields.

##### Outputs & side effects
Rows inserted/updated/deleted; SYSOUT messages; final RC 4 if any record failed, else 0. Commit is implicit at successful program end under TSO DSN (no explicit COMMIT/ROLLBACK).

##### External calls
DB2 via precompiled EXEC SQL (plan CARDDEMO, subsystem DAZ1).

##### Migration notes
- Errors don't stop the run; failed records are skipped and RC=4 is sticky. No rollback - successful rows are committed alongside failures.
- Description inserted from fixed X(50): VARCHAR column receives 50 chars including trailing spaces.
- TR_TYPE is CHAR(2) with no numeric validation despite JCL comment saying numeric.
- Duplicate insert (SQLCODE -803) is just an error message; positive SQLCODEs on insert are ignored.
- OPEN failure only displays; subsequent READ on unopened file will fail at runtime.
recommendation: Fully traced.

title: COPAUS1C (CPVD) authorization detail view and fraud toggle
description:
##### Entry point
CICS pseudo-conversational program **COPAUS1C**, transaction **CPVD** (Pending Authorization Detail view and fraud tagging). It is reached by XCTL from COPAUS0C when the user enters 'S' on a row.

##### Inputs
- COMMAREA CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (COCOM01Y) plus `CDEMO-CPVD-INFO`. This has the same shape as COPAUS0C's CPVS-INFO, plus `CDEMO-CPVD-FRAUD-DATA X(100)`. Used fields:
  - CDEMO-ACCT-ID
  - CDEMO-CUST-ID
  - CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SELECTED: the 8-byte auth key, at the same offset as CPVS-PAU-SELECTED
- Map **COPAU1A** / mapset **COPAU01**: the screen is output only; the RECEIVE uses NOHANDLE.
- AID keys: ENTER, PF3, PF5, PF8, other.

##### Processing flow
1. **EIBCALEN=0**: TO-PROGRAM=COPAUS0C, then XCTL back (RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN sets FROM fields, context 0, PGM-ENTER).
2. Copy the COMMAREA and blank CPVD-FRAUD-DATA.
   - **First entry**: set REENTER, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, then SEND.
   - **Re-entry**: RECEIVE, then:
     - ENTER → PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
     - PF3 → XCTL COPAUS0C
     - PF5 → MARK-AUTH-FRAUD
     - PF8 → PROCESS-PF8-KEY
     - other → PROCESS-ENTER-KEY plus the invalid-key message
   - Then `RETURN TRANSID(CPVD) COMMAREA`.
3. **PROCESS-ENTER-KEY**: clear the map. If the account is numeric and an auth key is selected, READ-AUTH-RECORD:
   - SCHD PSBPAUTB
   - `GU PAUTSUM0 WHERE ACCNTID`
   - if OK, `GNP PAUTDTL1 WHERE PAUT9CTS = key`
   - then SYNCPOINT to release the PSB.
   - If no account or key is set, ERR-FLG is set and nothing is displayed.
   - Then POPULATE-AUTH-DETAILS.
4. **POPULATE-AUTH-DETAILS** (only when no error):
   - card number
   - date MM/DD/YY and time HH:MM:SS from the original request date/time
   - approved amount
   - AUTHRSPO = 'A' (green) when the response code is '00', else 'D' (red)
   - reason text: SEARCH ALL on table WS-DECLINE-REASON-TAB (see the reason list below), shown as 'code-DESC'. If the code is not found, '9999-ERROR' is shown.
   - processing code, POS mode, source, MCC
   - expiry formatted MM/YY from the expiry date
   - type, txn id, match status
   - fraud field: 'F-'/'R-' + report date when the fraud flag is F or R, else '-'
   - merchant name, id, city, state, zip
   - Decline reason table: 0000 APPROVED, 3100 INVALID CARD, 4100 INSUFFICNT FUND, 4200 CARD NOT ACTIVE, 4300 ACCOUNT CLOSED, 4400 EXCED DAILY LMT, 5100 CARD FRAUD, 5200 MERCHANT FRAUD, 5300 LOST CARD, 9000 UNKNOWN.
5. **MARK-AUTH-FRAUD (PF5)**: READ-AUTH-RECORD (the PSB stays scheduled). Toggle the fraud flag:
   - if PA-AUTH-FRAUD='F', set it to 'R' (action R, remove)
   - else set it to 'F' (action F, report).
   - Build WS-FRAUD-DATA (WS-FRD-ACCT-ID 9(11), WS-FRD-CUST-ID 9(9), the 200-byte detail record, action, update status, message X(50)).
   - `EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM(COPAUS2C) COMMAREA(WS-FRAUD-DATA) NOHANDLE`.
   - If RESP is NORMAL and the status is 'S', run UPDATE-AUTH-DETAILS: DLI REPL PAUTDTL1 from the returned record. This takes a SYNCPOINT and shows 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' or 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...'. If the REPL fails, roll back and show an error.
   - If the status is not 'S', show WS-FRD-ACT-MSG and SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK.
   - If the LINK fails, ROLLBACK.
   - Finally redisplay.
6. **PF8**: READ-AUTH-RECORD, then an unqualified GNP for the next (older) auth, then SYNCPOINT. If at the end: 'Already at the last Authorization...'. Otherwise the new key becomes the selected key and is displayed.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[COPAUS1C / CPVD] --> C{EIBCALEN=0?}
  C -->|yes| X0[XCTL COPAUS0C]
  C -->|no| K{EIBAID}
  K -->|ENTER/first/other| E[READ-AUTH-RECORD: SCHD, GU PAUTSUM0, GNP PAUTDTL1 by key]
  K -->|PF3| X0
  K -->|PF5| F[MARK-AUTH-FRAUD toggle F/R]
  F --> L[LINK COPAUS2C - DB2 AUTHFRDS insert/update]
  L -->|S| U[DLI REPL PAUTDTL1 + SYNCPOINT]
  L -->|fail| RB[SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK]
  K -->|PF8| N[READ-AUTH-RECORD + GNP next]
  E --> P[POPULATE-AUTH-DETAILS + SEND COPAU1A]
  U --> P
  RB --> P
  N --> P
  P --> RT[RETURN TRANSID CPVD]
```

##### Data
- IMS DBPAUTP0 via PSBPAUTB: PAUTSUM0 (GU) and PAUTDTL1 (GNP, REPL). Updated field: PA-AUTH-FRAUD. PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE is set by COPAUS2C to the current date.
- DB2 **CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS**, via COPAUS2C: an INSERT of the full auth row with AUTH_FRAUD = the action. On SQLCODE -803 (duplicate) it falls back to an UPDATE. See the AUTHFRDS DCLGEN flow.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Screen COPAU1A.
- On PF5: an IMS detail-segment update and a DB2 fraud row, committed together by CICS SYNCPOINT (a two-phase unit of work across IMS and DB2).

##### External calls
- **COPAUS2C** (LINK, outside this batch; read for this flow).
  - Input: WS-FRAUD-DATA.
  - Output: WS-FRD-UPDATE-STATUS ('S' or 'F'), WS-FRD-ACT-MSG ('ADD SUCCESS', 'UPDT SUCCESS', or ' SYSTEM ERROR DB2: CODE:nnn'), and the auth record with PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE set.
- CICS: XCTL, RETURN, SEND/RECEIVE, SYNCPOINT, SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK.
- IMS DL/I.

##### Migration notes
- The fraud action is a **toggle**: PF5 on a removed ('R') or blank auth marks it 'F'; PF5 on an 'F' auth sets it to 'R'.
- UPDATE-AUTH-DETAILS uses REPL after a GNP, not a GHNP or a hold call. The PSB has PROCOPT=AP; behavior under CICS DL/I depends on that.
- The REPL record is the copy returned by COPAUS2C, not the local one.
- `DISPLAY 'RPT DT: '` writes to the CICS job log.
- Error paths call SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN without exiting, so the screen may be sent twice.
- `CDEMO-CPVD-FRAUD-DATA` is blanked on every entry and never used otherwise.
- The SEARCH ALL requires the table to be sorted by code; it is.
- After PF8, the GNP is unqualified under the same root, so the chain stops at the end of the account's children (GE).
- 'Already at the last Authorization' leaves the old values on the screen because SEND-ERASE-NO is set.
recommendation: Fully documented from source.
note:
Consolidated document for app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/cbl/COPAUS1C.cbl; merged duplicates: sfind-bc5179dc733c4d6daf541ad7c22079ad.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Fraud toggle semantics: any value other than 'F' (including spaces and 'R') becomes 'F'.
- CDEMO-CPVD-* and CDEMO-CPVS-* overlay the same commarea bytes; the new stack must keep the selected key handoff.

End-to-end: COPAUS1C is XCTLed from COPAUS0C when an authorization is selected. Upstream findings: sfind-dc30b1d02e7d41f9b03fd81743cbaa83.

title: BMS screen contracts: COSGN00, COADM01, COCRDSL, COTRN02, COUSR02
description:
##### Entry point
The BMS mapset definitions in `app/bms` that belong to this batch. Each one is assembled into a physical map and a symbolic map copybook. The programs below send and receive each map:

| Mapset / map | Program | Transaction / purpose |
|---|---|---|
| COSGN00 / COSGN0A | COSGN00C | sign-on, transaction CC00 |
| COADM01 / COADM1A | COADM01C | admin menu, CA00 |
| COCRDSL / CCRDSLA | COCRDSLC | card detail view |
| COTRN02 / COTRN2A | COTRN02C | add transaction |
| COUSR02 / COUSR2A | COUSR02C | update user |

The online flows that use these maps are documented in the batches that cover those programs. This finding records only the screen contracts.

##### Inputs
The named fields in each map are listed below. In the symbolic map, each field has L (length), F/A (flag/attribute) and I/O (data) suffixes.

- **COSGN0A**
  - Header: TRNNAME, TITLE01, CURDATE, PGMNAME, TITLE02, CURTIME
  - APPLID, SYSID
  - **USERID**, **PASSWD** (input; the password is a dark/non-display field)
  - ERRMSG
- **COADM1A**
  - Header fields, as in COSGN0A
  - OPTN001–OPTN012 (menu option lines)
  - **OPTION** (input selection)
  - ERRMSG
- **CCRDSLA**
  - Header fields
  - **ACCTSID**, **CARDSID** (input keys)
  - CRDNAME, CRDSTCD, EXPMON, EXPYEAR
  - INFOMSG, ERRMSG, FKEYS
- **COTRN2A**
  - Header fields
  - Input fields: **ACTIDIN**, **CARDNIN**, TTYPCD, TCATCD, TRNSRC, TDESC, TRNAMT, TORIGDT, TPROCDT, MID, MNAME, MCITY, MZIP
  - **CONFIRM**
  - ERRMSG
- **COUSR2A**
  - Header fields
  - **USRIDIN**, FNAME, LNAME, PASSWD, USRTYPE
  - ERRMSG

##### Processing flow
These are static screen definitions, so they contain no logic. Each program uses its map in the usual pseudo-conversational cycle:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[Owning CICS program] -->|SEND MAP mapset| T[3270 terminal]
  T -->|ENTER/PFn| R[RECEIVE MAP into symbolic map xxxxI]
  R --> V[program edits fields]
  V --> P
```

##### Data
- The field positions, lengths and attributes are defined by the DFHMDF macros in each `.bms` file. Most maps declare `CTRL=(ALARM,FREEKB)`; COCRDSL declares `FREEKB`.
- The copybooks generated from these maps live in `app/cpy-bms`.

##### Outputs & side effects
The 3270 screen layouts.

##### External calls
None.

##### Migration notes
- Re-implement each field using the exact lengths and protection attributes in the DFHMDF definitions.
- PASSWD fields are non-display.
- Programs change attributes at run time (color, protect, cursor positioning through length −1), so the static definition alone is not enough to reproduce screen behavior.
- **Limitation:** I recorded only the field names for this summary. The exact POS/LENGTH values were not transcribed here; take them from the `.bms` source.
recommendation: Exact POS/LENGTH per field not transcribed; owning program flows are in other batches.

title: IMS pending-authorization DB unload (PAUDBUNL, DBUNLDGS, DBPAUTP0 HD unload job)
description:
##### Entry point
There are two IMS batch DL/I programs and one utility job. All of them unload the pending-authorization database DBPAUTP0.

1. **PAUDBUNL**: run by JCL `UNLDPADB.JCL`. It executes `DFSRRC00` with `PARM='DLI,PAUDBUNL,PAUTBUNL,...'`, and the linkage is `PAUTBPCB`.
2. **DBUNLDGS**: run by JCL `UNLDGSAM.JCL` with `PARM='DLI,DBUNLDGS,DLIGSAMP,...'`, and the linkage is `PAUTBPCB, PASFLPCB, PADFLPCB`.
3. **DBPAUTP0.jcl**: an IMS HD unload utility job that does not use any custom program.

##### Inputs
- IMS DBPAUTP0: HIDAM, DD `DDPAUTP0` (`OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDB`); primary index DBPAUTX0, DD `DDPAUTX0` (`OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDBX`).
- **PSBs**
  - PAUTBUNL: PCB PAUTBPCB, PROCOPT=GOTP, KEYLEN=14, SENSEG PAUTSUM0/PAUTDTL1.
  - DLIGSAMP: the same DB PCB, plus GSAM PCBs `PASFLDBD` and `PADFLDBD` with PROCOPT=LS, and CMPAT=NO.
- Segment layouts: CIPAUSMY (100 bytes) and CIPAUDTY (200 bytes). These are described in the COPAUA0C flow.
- **Index DBD DBPAUTX0**: INDEX/VSAM, segment PAUTINDX with a 6-byte INDXSEQ, which is the target of LCHILD PAUTSUM0 via ACCNTID.

##### Processing flow
Both programs follow the same steps:

1. `1000-INITIALIZE`: ACCEPT the date and day, and DISPLAY the start banner.
   - PAUDBUNL: OPEN OUTPUT OPFILE1 and OPFILE2. If a status is not '00', it DISPLAYs the error and runs 9999-ABEND.
   - DBUNLDGS: the OPENs are commented out, because output goes through GSAM PCBs.
2. `2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY` runs until WS-END-OF-ROOT-SEG='Y'. It does `CALL 'CBLTDLI' USING FUNC-GN PAUTBPCB PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY ROOT-UNQUAL-SSA` ('PAUTSUM0 ').
   - Status spaces: increment the counters, MOVE the summary to OPFIL1-REC, and set ROOT-SEG-KEY = PA-ACCT-ID. **Only if PA-ACCT-ID IS NUMERIC**:
     - PAUDBUNL: WRITE OPFIL1-REC.
     - DBUNLDGS: run `3100-INSERT-PARENT-SEG-GSAM`, which does `CBLTDLI ISRT PASFLPCB OPFIL1-REC`. A non-blank status → 9999-ABEND.
     - Then loop `3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL` until the end of the children.
   - Status 'GB': end of the database, so set the root end flag.
   - Any other status: DISPLAY the status and the key feedback, then 9999-ABEND.
3. `3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL`: `CBLTDLI GNP PAUTBPCB PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS CHILD-UNQUAL-SSA` ('PAUTDTL1 ').
   - Status spaces: MOVE the detail to CHILD-SEG-REC.
     - PAUDBUNL: WRITE OPFIL2-REC (ROOT-SEG-KEY + CHILD-SEG-REC).
     - DBUNLDGS: run `3200-INSERT-CHILD-SEG-GSAM` (ISRT PADFLPCB PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS). A non-blank status → abend.
   - 'GE': set the child end flag.
   - Other: DISPLAY, then abend.
4. `4000-FILE-CLOSE`:
   - PAUDBUNL: CLOSE both files. A non-'00' status only DISPLAYs; there is no abend.
   - DBUNLDGS: nothing to close.
5. `9999-ABEND`: DISPLAY, then `MOVE 16 TO RETURN-CODE` and GOBACK.

**DBPAUTP0.jcl**
- `STEPDEL`: IEFBR14 deletes `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.IMSDATA.DBPAUTP0`.
- `UNLOAD`: DFSRRC00 `PARM=(ULU,DFSURGU0,DBPAUTP0)` (HD Reorganization Unload). DFSURGU1 is the new unload dataset, DFSCTL is `SBPARM ACTIV=COND`, and the RECON datasets are allocated.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  J1[UNLDPADB.JCL DFSRRC00 DLI PAUDBUNL/PAUTBUNL] --> P1[PAUDBUNL 1000-INITIALIZE OPEN OUTFIL1/OUTFIL2]
  J2[UNLDGSAM.JCL DFSRRC00 DLI DBUNLDGS/DLIGSAMP] --> P2[DBUNLDGS 1000-INITIALIZE]
  P1 --> GN[2000 CBLTDLI GN PAUTSUM0]
  P2 --> GN
  GN -->|GB| CL[4000-FILE-CLOSE / GOBACK]
  GN -->|other| AB[9999-ABEND RC=16]
  GN -->|ok & acct numeric| WR[write root: OPFILE1 or ISRT PASFLPCB]
  WR --> GNP[3000 CBLTDLI GNP PAUTDTL1]
  GNP -->|ok| WC[write child: OPFILE2 or ISRT PADFLPCB]
  WC --> GNP
  GNP -->|GE| GN
  GNP -->|other| AB
  J3[DBPAUTP0.jcl STEPDEL IEFBR14] --> U[UNLOAD DFSRRC00 ULU DFSURGU0 -> DFSURGU1]
```

##### Data
- **Outputs written by PAUDBUNL**
  - OUTFIL1 → `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.FILEO`: OPFIL1-REC X(100), which is the raw PAUTSUM0 image.
  - OUTFIL2 → `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.FILEO`: OPFIL2-REC, made of ROOT-SEG-KEY S9(11) COMP-3 (6 bytes) followed by CHILD-SEG-REC X(200), for 206 bytes in total.
  - UNLDPADB first deletes these datasets in an IEFBR14 step that has DD1/DD2.
- **Outputs written by DBUNLDGS**
  - GSAM `PASFILOP` → `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.GSAM`: the 100-byte root record.
  - GSAM `PADFILOP` → `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.GSAM`: the 200-byte child record only, **without the root key**.
- **DBPAUTP0.jcl** writes the standard IMS unload format to `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.IMSDATA.DBPAUTP0`.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Sequential or GSAM unload files.
- SYSOUT DISPLAYs: a banner, plus 'CHILD SEG FLAG GE' for every root.
- RETURN-CODE 16 on error.
- The IMS database is read only (GOTP).

##### External calls
- `CBLTDLI`: GN, GNP, and ISRT to GSAM.
- DFSRRC00, the IMS region controller.
- DFSURGU0, the IMS utility.
- IEFBR14.

##### Migration notes
- Roots whose PA-ACCT-ID is not numeric are **silently skipped**, together with their children. They are still counted in WS-NO-SUMRY-READ.
- The child reads increment the *summary* counters: WS-NO-SUMRY-READ and WS-AUTH-SMRY-PROC-CNT. The counts are therefore not separable.
- The two variants differ as follows:
  - Child file layout: 206 bytes with the parent key in PAUDBUNL, versus 200 bytes with no parent key in DBUNLDGS. With DBUNLDGS, parent linkage is only implied by file order.
  - Close errors are not fatal in PAUDBUNL.
- 9999-ABEND only sets RC=16 and GOBACKs; it does not issue a real abend, so IMS does not back out. For a read-only PSB this is harmless.
- The GSAM PCBs in DLIGSAMP are LS (load). They need the GSAM DBDs PASFLDBD/PADFLDBD, which are not in the repo.
recommendation: GSAM DBDs PASFLDBD/PADFLDBD not in repo.
note:
Consolidated document for app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/cbl/PAUDBUNL.CBL, app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl/UNLDPADB.JCL; merged duplicates: sfind-464cf891f52248d8afecd729384b8bf3, sfind-d483081ea65a4a74ab3128d586c71680.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Output files are binary (packed decimal, halfword counts); the reload (PAUDBLOD, outside batch) expects this exact layout.
- GNP returning 'GB' (instead of 'GE') would be treated as an error and abend.
- STEP0 fails with a JCL error if the old datasets do not exist (DISP=OLD); abend path does not close files.
- 
No COND codes: STEP01 runs even if STEP0 fails? (STEP0 failure with DISP=OLD on missing dataset is a JCL allocation error that terminates the job). Space allocation is tiny (400-byte blocks) - large databases need more. Dataset names are environment-specific HLQs.

title: COTRTLI/CTRTLIA BMS map for transaction-type list
description:
##### Entry point
BMS mapset **COTRTLI**, map **CTRTLIA** (`app/app-transaction-type-db2/bms/COTRTLI.bms`). It is used by COTRTLIC (transaction CTLI).

##### Inputs
The map fields are:
- Header: TRNNAME, TITLE01, CURDATE, PGMNAME, TITLE02, CURTIME, PAGENO.
- Filters: **TRTYPE** (type code filter), **TRDESC** (description filter).
- Seven list rows, n = 1..7: **TRTSELn** (action, D or U), TRTTYPn (type code), **TRTYPDn** (description).
- A trailer row: TRTSELA, TRTTYPA, TRTDSCA.
- Messages: INFOMSG, ERRMSG.
- PF key labels: BUTNF02, BUTNF03, BUTNF07, BUTNF08, BUTNF10.

##### Processing flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[COTRTLIC 2600-SEND-SCREEN] -->|SEND MAP CTRTLIA MAPSET COTRTLI| T[terminal]
  T -->|RECEIVE MAP| L2[COTRTLIC 1100-RECEIVE-SCREEN]
```
COTRTLIC's 2200/2300/2400 paragraphs set the row protection and the PF-key labels at run time.

##### Data
The field definitions are the DFHMDF entries in the BMS file. The mapset is declared with `LANG=COBOL` and the map with `CTRL=(FREEKB)`.

##### Outputs & side effects
The screen layout for the transaction-type list.

##### External calls
None.

##### Migration notes
- The grid is fixed at 7 rows, matching WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES = 7 in COTRTLIC.
- I did not transcribe the exact POS/LENGTH values; take them from the source file.
recommendation: Exact field positions/lengths to be taken from source.

title: COTRTUPC (CTTU) transaction-type add/update/delete maintenance screen (DB2)
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program **COTRTUPC** (transaction **CTTU**) maintains a single transaction type: it views, adds, updates, and deletes one row at a time. It uses mapset **COTRTUP** and map **CTRTUPA**. It is reached by XCTL from COTRTLIC (PF2) or from the admin menu COADM01C. `EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND LABEL(ABEND-ROUTINE)` is in effect.

##### Inputs
- **COMMAREA**: CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA. That area holds:
  - The state flag **TTUP-CHANGE-ACTION**.
  - TTUP-OLD-DETAILS (type X(2), description X(50)).
  - TTUP-NEW-DETAILS.
- **Map**: input TRTYPCDI (type code); a description field.
- **AID keys**: ENTER, PF3, PF4 (delete), PF5 (save/create), PF12 (cancel).

**State values**

| Value | State |
|---|---|
| low/space | DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED |
| K | INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS |
| X | DETAILS-NOT-FOUND |
| S | SHOW-DETAILS |
| R | CREATE-NEW-RECORD |
| V | REVIEW-NEW-RECORD |
| 9 | CONFIRM-DELETE |
| 8 | START-DELETE |
| 7 | DELETE-DONE |
| 6 | DELETE-FAILED |
| E | CHANGES-NOT-OK |
| N | CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED |
| L | LOCK-ERROR |
| F | OKAYED-BUT-FAILED |
| C | OKAYED-AND-DONE |
| B | BACKED-OUT |

##### Processing flow
1. **Entry reset.** On a fresh entry the COMMAREA and state are reset and PGM-ENTER is set. A fresh entry is any of:
   - EIBCALEN=0.
   - Arrival from COADM01C without REENTER.
   - Arrival from COTRTLIC without REENTER.
2. **Key check.** `0001-CHECK-PFKEYS` decides which keys are valid in the current state:
   - PF3: always valid.
   - ENTER: valid unless the state is CONFIRM-DELETE.
   - PF4: valid in states S or 9.
   - PF5: valid in states N, X, or a delete state.
   - PF12: valid in states N, S, X, 9, or R.
   - Any other key sets WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED.
3. **Pre-dispatch reset.** These conditions reset the screen to the search prompt (PGM-ENTER and NOT-FETCHED):
   - PF12 in state S, R, or X.
   - State C, L/F, or B with blank old details.
   - Delete done or delete failed.
4. **Dispatch.**
   - **PF3**: SYNCPOINT, then XCTL to the caller (default COADM01C/CA00).
   - **First display**: send the empty screen and set REENTER.
   - **PF4 in state 9**: `9800-DELETE-PROCESSING` runs `DELETE FROM CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = old type`.
     - SQLCODE 0: state 7 (delete done), then SYNCPOINT.
     - SQLCODE −532: message "Please delete associated child records first:". The state is **not** changed to failed.
     - Any other code: state 6 (delete failed) with a message.
   - **PF4 in state S**: state 9, which asks the user to confirm the delete.
   - **PF5 in state X**: state R, which shows an empty description for a new record.
   - **PF5 in state N**: `9600-WRITE-PROCESSING` runs `UPDATE ... SET TR_DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE`.
     - SQLCODE 0: SYNCPOINT.
     - SQLCODE +100: `9700-INSERT-RECORD` runs INSERT (type, description); SYNCPOINT on 0, otherwise the "Error inserting" message.
     - SQLCODE −911: lock error, state L.
     - SQLCODE < 0: state F.
     - Otherwise: state C.
   - **PF12 in state N, 9, or S**: re-read the record (`2000-DECIDE-ACTION`).
   - **Invalid key**: redisplay.
   - **OTHER** (ENTER): `1000-PROCESS-INPUTS`, then `2000-DECIDE-ACTION`, then `3000-SEND-MAP`.
5. **`1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS`.**
   - **Type code**: `1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE` → `1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD`. The code is required, must be numeric (TEST-NUMVAL), and must not be zero. It is then normalized to 2 digits with zero fill.
   - **Description**: compare new and old (case-insensitive, after trimming). If it changed, it is required and must be alphanumeric only (`1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD`). If it passes, the state becomes N (needs PF5 confirmation).
6. **`2000-DECIDE-ACTION`.**
   - **NOT-FETCHED or PF12, with a valid key**: `9000-READ-TRANTYPE` → `9100-GET-TRANSACTION-TYPE` runs `SELECT TR_TYPE, TR_DESCRIPTION ... WHERE TR_TYPE = :key`.
     - SQLCODE 0: state S.
     - SQLCODE +100: "record not found", state X.
     - SQLCODE < 0: error message.
     - `9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA` keeps the old values.
   - **PF12 with an invalid key**: state 9 → "delete cancelled"; state N → "update cancelled", state B.
   - **State S with no edit errors**: state N.
   - **State B**: state E.
   - **State C**: state S.
   - **Any other state**: ABEND-ROUTINE with code '0001' and message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. ABEND-ROUTINE does SEND of the abend data, then CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999'). The code is overwritten to '9999' inside the routine.
7. **Return**: `COMMON-RETURN` issues `RETURN TRANSID(CTTU) COMMAREA`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[COTRTUPC / CTTU] --> P[0001-CHECK-PFKEYS]
  P --> E{EVALUATE AID+TTUP-CHANGE-ACTION}
  E -->|PF3| X[SYNCPOINT XCTL caller/COADM01C]
  E -->|first| SM[3000-SEND-MAP CTRTUPA]
  E -->|ENTER| IN[1000-PROCESS-INPUTS 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS]
  IN --> D[2000-DECIDE-ACTION]
  D -->|fetch| RD[9100 SELECT TRANSACTION_TYPE]
  E -->|PF4 S| C9[state 9 confirm delete]
  E -->|PF4 9| DL[9800 DELETE + SYNCPOINT]
  E -->|PF5 X| NR[state R new record]
  E -->|PF5 N| WR[9600 UPDATE]
  WR -->|+100| INS[9700 INSERT + SYNCPOINT]
  WR -->|0| SP[SYNCPOINT state C]
  RD --> SM
  C9 --> SM
  DL --> SM
  NR --> SM
  INS --> SM
  SP --> SM
  SM --> RT[RETURN TRANSID CTTU]
```

##### Data
- **CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE**, the same table as in COTRTLIC. Operations: SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE.

##### Outputs & side effects
- **Screen**: CTRTUPA.
- **DB2 changes**: each insert, update, or delete is committed immediately by SYNCPOINT.
- **CICS ABEND** '9999' on an unexpected state.

##### External calls
- **DB2**.
- **CICS**: XCTL, SYNCPOINT, SEND, RETURN, HANDLE ABEND, ABEND.

##### Migration notes
- **Upsert**: PF5 is an upsert. It tries UPDATE first and falls back to INSERT on +100. A row deleted by another user between read and save is therefore silently re-created.
- **Duplicate inserts**: the INSERT error path does not handle −803.
- **No optimistic locking**: the UPDATE does not compare the old description. DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE is never set anywhere, so that state branch is dead.
- **Stored description length**: the length is set from the untrimmed field (50), so the stored VARCHAR is space-padded to 50.
- **Abend code**: the '0001' set in 2000 is overwritten by '9999' in ABEND-ROUTINE.
- **Delete −532**: this path does not set TTUP-DELETE-FAILED, so the state stays at 8 (START-DELETE).
- **Unresolved**: the details of the screen-attribute paragraphs (3000–3400) were not traced line by line. They set field protection, colors, and the info message for each state.
recommendation: Screen attribute paragraphs 3000-3400 summarized, not traced line by line.
note: Duplicate of sfind-63f866033e6444b7bf2136d8f7c5ec6e (CTTU / COTRTUPC); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: COTRTLIC (CTLI) transaction-type list/filter/update/delete screen (DB2)
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program **COTRTLIC**, transaction **CTLI**. This is the admin screen that lists, filters, updates and deletes transaction types. BMS mapset **COTRTLI**, map **CTRTLIA**. Users reach it from the admin menu COADM01C (CA00).

##### Inputs
- **COMMAREA.** CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (COCOM01Y) followed by WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA. The program's own area holds:
  - type and description filters (WS-CA-TYPE-CD, WS-CA-TYPE-DESC)
  - paging values: WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE, WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE, WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM, and the next-page and last-page-shown flags
  - WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED
  - the 7 rows displayed: WS-CA-ROW-TR-CODE-OUT and WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT
  - delete/update requested flags
- **Map fields (COTRTLI.bms).**
  - Header: TRNNAME, TITLE01/02, CURDATE, CURTIME, PGMNAME, PAGENO.
  - Filters: TRTYPE (2-character type code) and TRDESC (description).
  - Rows 1–7: TRTSELn (action: 'D' = delete, 'U' = update), TRTTYPn (type) and TRTYPDn (description, editable when 'U' is selected).
  - Also TRTSELA, TRTTYPA, TRTDSCA, INFOMSG and ERRMSG.
  - Key labels: BUTNF02, BUTNF03, BUTNF07, BUTNF08, BUTNF10.
- **AID keys** (normalized by YYYY-STORE-PFKEY from CSSTRPFY): ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, PF10. Any other key is treated as ENTER. PF10 is honored only when a delete or update request is pending.

##### Processing flow
1. **First entry (EIBCALEN=0).** Initialize the COMMAREA, set the user type to admin and set first page. The same reset applies when the program is entered from another program, or on PF3 coming back from CTTU.
2. **Receive input.** When the previous screen was this program, `1000-RECEIVE-MAP` runs RECEIVE MAP, then `1200-EDIT-INPUTS`, which performs these edits:
   - `1210-EDIT-ARRAY` — if a filter changed, the selections are cleared. Otherwise it counts D and U selections. If more than one action is selected, the message "more than 1 action" is set and the rows are flagged. A value other than D, U or blank gives the "invalid action code" error. For a 'U' row, `1211-EDIT-ARRAY-DESC` checks whether the description changed (case-insensitive, compared after trimming). If it changed, the description must be non-blank and alphanumeric (`1240-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD`).
   - `1230-EDIT-DESC` — a non-blank description filter becomes the LIKE pattern `'%'||trim||'%'`.
   - `1220-EDIT-TYPECD` — a type filter that is blank, zeros or low-values means no filter. A non-numeric value gives the error "TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER". A filter change resets paging.
   - `1290-CROSS-EDITS` — when a filter is set, `9100-CHECK-FILTERS` runs SELECT COUNT(1) with the same predicate as the cursor. A count of 0 gives "No Records found for these filter conditions".
3. **PF3.** XCTL to the calling program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), or to COADM01C/CA00 when the caller is blank or is this program. A SYNCPOINT runs first.
4. **PF2.** XCTL to **COTRTUPC** (the add/edit screen, CTTU) with the COMMAREA.
5. **Priming query.** `9998-PRIMING-QUERY` (from CSDB2RPY) runs SELECT 1 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1. On failure the program sends a plain long-text error and returns.
6. **EVALUATE dispatch:**
   - **INPUT-ERROR** — redisplay the screen from the first code, without reading when a filter is invalid.
   - **PF7 on the first page** — re-read forward from the first code.
   - **PF3, or re-entry from another program** — reset state and read the first page.
   - **PF8 with a next page** — start from the last code, increment the screen number, and run `8000-READ-FORWARD`.
   - **PF7 when not on the first page** — decrement the screen number and run `8100-READ-BACKWARDS`.
   - **ENTER with deletes requested** — redisplay. Rows show as "pending delete", and the user confirms with PF10.
   - **PF10 with deletes requested** — `9300-DELETE-RECORD` runs `DELETE FROM CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE=:code`. Results:
     - 0: SYNCPOINT, deleted.
     - −532: "Please delete associated child records first:".
     - Other: "Delete failed with message:".
     - On success the state is reset after the send.
   - **ENTER with updates requested** — redisplay for confirmation.
   - **PF10 with updates requested** — `9200-UPDATE-RECORD` runs `UPDATE ... SET TR_DESCRIPTION=:desc WHERE TR_TYPE=:code`. Results:
     - 0: SYNCPOINT.
     - +100: "Record not found. Deleted by others ?".
     - −911: "Deadlock. Someone else updating ?".
     - < 0: "Update failed with".
     - The page is then re-read.
   - **OTHER** — read forward from the first code.
7. **Read forward (`8000-READ-FORWARD`).** OPEN cursor C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD:
   ```
   SELECT TR_TYPE, TR_DESCRIPTION FROM CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
   WHERE TR_TYPE >= :WS-START-KEY [AND TR_TYPE = filter] [AND TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE TRIM(pattern)]
   ORDER BY TR_TYPE
   ```
   It fetches up to 7 rows, then one more to set the next-page flag. Messages: "no more records" on PF8, and "no records found".
8. **Read backward (`8100-READ-BACKWARDS`).** Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD uses `TR_TYPE < :start ... ORDER BY TR_TYPE DESC` and fills rows 7 down to 1.
9. **Send the screen (`2000-SEND-MAP`).** Builds the screen (2100–2500) and sends it (2600). `COMMON-RETURN` then issues `RETURN TRANSID(CTLI) COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA)`.
10. **DB2 error text.** `9999-FORMAT-DB2-MESSAGE` calls **DSNTIAC** with DFHEIBLK, DFHCOMMAREA, SQLCA, the output buffer and LRECL 72, then builds "<action> SQLCODE:<code> <text>".

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[COTRTLIC / CTLI] --> I{EIBCALEN=0 or entered from other pgm?}
  I -->|yes| INIT[init commarea, first page]
  I -->|no| RCV[1000-RECEIVE-MAP + 1200-EDIT-INPUTS]
  RCV --> K{AID}
  INIT --> PQ
  K -->|PF3| X3[SYNCPOINT, XCTL caller or COADM01C]
  K -->|PF2| X2[XCTL COTRTUPC]
  K --> PQ[9998-PRIMING-QUERY SYSDUMMY1]
  PQ --> EV{EVALUATE}
  EV -->|PF8| RF[8000-READ-FORWARD C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD]
  EV -->|PF7| RB[8100-READ-BACKWARDS C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD]
  EV -->|PF10 delete| DEL[9300 DELETE TRANSACTION_TYPE + SYNCPOINT]
  EV -->|PF10 update| UPD[9200 UPDATE TRANSACTION_TYPE + SYNCPOINT]
  EV -->|ENTER/other| RF
  DEL --> SM
  UPD --> RF
  RF --> SM[2000-SEND-MAP CTRTLIA]
  RB --> SM
  SM --> RT[RETURN TRANSID CTLI]
```

##### Data
- **DB2 `CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE`** (ddl/TRNTYPE.ddl):
  - TR_TYPE CHAR(2) NOT NULL, the primary key.
  - TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL.
- **Unique index `CARDDEMO.XTRAN_TYPE`** on TR_TYPE ASC (ddl/XTRNTYPE.ddl).
- **Host variables** (DCLTRTYP): DCL-TR-TYPE X(2), and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION as a varchar made of LEN S9(4) COMP plus TEXT X(50).
- Rows referencing this table (TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY) cause the −532 error on delete.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Screen CTRTLIA.
- DB2 UPDATE and DELETE, each committed by SYNCPOINT.
- XCTL to COTRTUPC or to the caller/admin menu.

##### External calls
- DB2 (SQL).
- DSNTIAC, the DB2 message-formatting module.
- CICS RECEIVE/SEND MAP, XCTL, SYNCPOINT, RETURN.

##### Migration notes
- **WHEN with no actions.** `WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK07 AND CA-FIRST-PAGE` is coded twice in a row. That is harmless.
- **PF10 update path.** It has no `GO TO COMMON-RETURN` and instead falls through to the trailing IF INPUT-ERROR logic. The outcome is the same.
- **Update length.** The description length is set to the length of the *untrimmed* input field, so trailing spaces are stored up to the field width, while the text itself is trimmed.
- **Edit order.** The description filter is edited before the type filter. The type-filter error message wins only if it is set later.
- **Hidden DB2 round trip.** The filter-count query and the priming query each add a DB2 call per interaction.
- **Description filter quirks.** It is case-sensitive and uses LIKE with user text, so user-entered `%` and `_` act as wildcards.
- **Paging.** It is keyset-based, using the first and last codes on the page.
- **Multiple selections.** Only one row action is allowed, and I-SELECTED is the lowest-numbered selected row because the loop runs from row 7 down to 1.
recommendation: Fully documented from source.
note: Duplicate of sfind-b7f6f63479e947a99e806c535d386c5f (COTRTLIC (CICS tran CTLI)); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: MVSWAIT assembler timer wait called by COBSWAIT (WAITSTEP.jcl)
description:
##### Entry point
JCL `jcl/WAITSTEP.jcl` has a step `//WAIT EXEC PGM=COBSWAIT`. That COBOL batch program calls the assembler module **MVSWAIT** (`app/asm/MVSWAIT.asm`, `MVSWAIT START 0`) with `CALL 'MVSWAIT' USING MVSWAIT-TIME`.

##### Inputs
- SYSIN card: PARM-VALUE X(8). The program MOVEs it to MVSWAIT-TIME, which is PIC 9(8) COMP (a 4-byte binary fullword).
- The value is the wait interval in hundredths of a second, because STIMER BINTVL uses units of 0.01 s.
- Parameter list passed to MVSWAIT: R1 points to the address of the fullword.

##### Processing flow
1. COBSWAIT runs `ACCEPT PARM-VALUE FROM SYSIN`, then `MOVE` to the COMP field, then `CALL 'MVSWAIT'`, then `STOP RUN`.
2. MVSWAIT:
   1. `STM 14,12,12(13)` saves the caller's registers. This module has no save area of its own.
   2. `L 5,0(1)` and `L 1,0(5)` load the delay value. `ST 1,BINLBL` stores it.
   3. The macro `ASMWAIT BINLBL` (from `app/maclib/ASMWAIT.mac`) expands to `STIMER WAIT,BINTVL=BINLBL`, which suspends the task for the interval.
   4. `LM 14,12,12(13)` restores the registers. `MVI 12(13),X'FF'` flags the caller's save area as returned. `SR 15,15` sets RC=0. `BR 14` returns.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  J[WAITSTEP.jcl WAIT EXEC PGM=COBSWAIT] --> A[ACCEPT PARM-VALUE FROM SYSIN]
  A --> B[MOVE to MVSWAIT-TIME 9-8 COMP]
  B --> C[CALL MVSWAIT]
  C --> D[STM regs, load delay via R1]
  D --> E[ASMWAIT -> STIMER WAIT BINTVL]
  E --> F[LM regs, MVI X'FF', R15=0, BR 14]
  F --> G[STOP RUN]
```

##### Data
There are no files. The only data used are the SYSIN card and the 4-byte BINLBL work field, which is defined inside the CSECT. Because the program stores into its own CSECT, it is not reentrant.

##### Outputs & side effects
The job step waits for the requested interval. RC=0.

##### External calls
The z/OS `STIMER` supervisor service.

##### Migration notes
- Moving PARM X(8) to 9(8) COMP requires numeric text. Non-numeric or blank input gives undefined results.
- A value of 12000 means 120 s, because the unit is 1/100 s.
- MVSWAIT uses R15 as its base register without establishing a new save area, which is unusual.
- The comment on `MVI 12(13),X'FF'` questions whether the instruction is needed.
- A replacement can be a simple sleep(n/100 seconds).
recommendation: Fully documented from source.
note: Duplicate of sfind-85a67e80e37c461887d6d0a4616532cc (WAITSTEP job); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: COPAUS2C fraud record insert/update into DB2 CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program **COPAUS2C**, started by `EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('COPAUS2C') COMMAREA(WS-FRAUD-DATA)` from COPAUS1C when the user presses PF5 (mark or remove fraud). There is no transaction id; it is called only through LINK.

##### Inputs
DFHCOMMAREA, laid out in this order:

| Field | Picture |
|---|---|
| WS-ACCT-ID | 9(11) |
| WS-CUST-ID | 9(9) |
| WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD | X(200), holds the CIPAUDTY PAUTDTL1 image |
| WS-FRD-ACTION | X: 'F' = report fraud, 'R' = remove |
| WS-FRD-UPDATE-STATUS | X: 'S' = success, 'F' = failed |
| WS-FRD-ACT-MSG | X(50) |

##### Processing flow
1. ASKTIME and FORMATTIME produce MMDDYY with a separator (MM/DD/YY). This value is written to **PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE** inside the COMMAREA record, which is returned to the caller.
2. Build WS-AUTH-TS in the form `YY-MM-DD HH.MI.SSsss000`:
   - YY, MM and DD come from PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE (YYMMDD).
   - The time is 999999999 − PA-AUTH-TIME-9C, which reverses the inverted key and gives HHMMSSmmm.
3. Move the record fields into the DCLAUTHFRDS host variables:
   - MERCHANT-NAME is a VARCHAR whose length is always set to 22.
   - AUTH-FRAUD is set to the action.
4. Run `INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS (26 columns) VALUES (..., TIMESTAMP_FORMAT(:AUTH-TS,'YY-MM-DD HH24.MI.SSNNNNNN'), ..., CURRENT DATE, :ACCT-ID, :CUST-ID)`. The insert uses CURRENT DATE for FRAUD_RPT_DATE.
5. Check the result:
   - SQLCODE 0: status 'S', message 'ADD SUCCESS'.
   - SQLCODE −803 (duplicate key): run FRAUD-UPDATE, which is `UPDATE CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS SET AUTH_FRAUD=:AUTH-FRAUD, FRAUD_RPT_DATE=CURRENT DATE WHERE CARD_NUM=:CARD-NUM AND AUTH_TS=TIMESTAMP_FORMAT(...)`. If that returns 0: status 'S', message 'UPDT SUCCESS'. Otherwise: status 'F', message ' UPDT ERROR DB2: CODE:<sqlcode>, STATE: <sqlstate>'.
   - Any other SQLCODE: status 'F', message ' SYSTEM ERROR DB2: CODE:..., STATE:...'.
6. EXEC CICS RETURN.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[LINK from COPAUS1C MARK-AUTH-FRAUD] --> B[ASKTIME/FORMATTIME -> PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE]
  B --> C[Build WS-AUTH-TS from PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE + 999999999-PA-AUTH-TIME-9C]
  C --> D[INSERT CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS]
  D -->|SQLCODE 0| S[status S ADD SUCCESS]
  D -->|-803| U[FRAUD-UPDATE UPDATE AUTHFRDS by CARD_NUM+AUTH_TS]
  U -->|0| S2[status S UPDT SUCCESS]
  U -->|err| F2[status F UPDT ERROR DB2]
  D -->|other| F[status F SYSTEM ERROR DB2]
  S --> R[CICS RETURN]
  S2 --> R
  F --> R
  F2 --> R
```

##### Data
- **DB2 table CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS**, defined by DCLGEN `dcl/AUTHFRDS.dcl`. Columns, with the COBOL host variable for each:

| Column | Type | Host variable |
|---|---|---|
| CARD_NUM | CHAR(16) NOT NULL | X(16) |
| AUTH_TS | TIMESTAMP NOT NULL | X(26) |
| AUTH_TYPE | CHAR(4) | |
| CARD_EXPIRY_DATE | CHAR(4) | |
| MESSAGE_TYPE | CHAR(6) | |
| MESSAGE_SOURCE | CHAR(6) | |
| AUTH_ID_CODE | CHAR(6) | |
| AUTH_RESP_CODE | CHAR(2) | |
| AUTH_RESP_REASON | CHAR(4) | |
| PROCESSING_CODE | CHAR(6) | |
| TRANSACTION_AMT | DECIMAL(12,2) | S9(10)V99 COMP-3 |
| APPROVED_AMT | DECIMAL(12,2) | S9(10)V99 COMP-3 |
| MERCHANT_CATAGORY_CODE | CHAR(4) | |
| ACQR_COUNTRY_CODE | CHAR(3) | |
| POS_ENTRY_MODE | SMALLINT | S9(4) COMP |
| MERCHANT_ID | CHAR(15) | |
| MERCHANT_NAME | VARCHAR(22) | 49-level LEN + TEXT |
| MERCHANT_CITY | CHAR(13) | |
| MERCHANT_STATE | CHAR(2) | |
| MERCHANT_ZIP | CHAR(9) | |
| TRANSACTION_ID | CHAR(15) | |
| MATCH_STATUS | CHAR(1) | |
| AUTH_FRAUD | CHAR(1) | |
| FRAUD_RPT_DATE | DATE | X(10) |
| ACCT_ID | DECIMAL(11,0) | S9(11)V COMP-3 |
| CUST_ID | DECIMAL(9,0) | S9(9)V COMP-3 |

- The −803 handling implies a unique key on CARD_NUM plus AUTH_TS. The DDL for AUTHFRDS is not in this batch.

##### Outputs & side effects
- One DB2 row is inserted or updated. The work is not committed here; COPAUS1C commits or rolls back through CICS SYNCPOINT.
- The COMMAREA returns the status, the message, and the record with PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE updated.

##### External calls
- DB2: SQL INSERT and UPDATE.
- CICS: ASKTIME, FORMATTIME, RETURN.

##### Migration notes
- The timestamp has a 2-digit year (YY, read through 'YY' in TIMESTAMP_FORMAT). It is built from the *original request date/time*, not from the IMS key date. The microseconds are milliseconds followed by '000'.
- The UPDATE path changes only AUTH_FRAUD and FRAUD_RPT_DATE. The other columns keep the values from the first insert.
- MERCHANT_NAME is always stored with length 22, so trailing spaces are kept.
- POS_ENTRY_MODE 9(2) is moved into SMALLINT.
- If a numeric field contains non-numeric data, the program may abend with ASRA; there is no handler for this.
- PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE (X(8) MM/DD/YY) is set in the returned record whether or not the SQL succeeds.
recommendation: AUTHFRDS DDL (keys/indexes) not in this batch; unique key inferred from -803 handling.
note:
Consolidated document for app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/cbl/COPAUS2C.cbl; merged duplicates: sfind-aa92423117ff4e33b68d523d0e11e3ba.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- MERCHANT_NAME always stored with length 22 (trailing spaces kept).

End-to-end: COPAUS2C is EXEC CICS LINKed from COPAUS1C (WS-PGM-AUTH-FRAUD) on fraud mark/unmark; together COPAUS0C -> COPAUS1C -> COPAUS2C form the pending-authorization review flow. Upstream findings: sfind-cc42995660ad4a41817741c9156ff0d6.

title: COACCT01 MQ-triggered account inquiry service (ACCTDAT -> CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT)
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program **COACCT01** (`app/app-vsam-mq/cbl/COACCT01.cbl`). It is an MQ-triggered account inquiry service and starts with `1000-CONTROL`. It is started by the CICS MQ trigger monitor, and `EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(MQTM)` returns the trigger message.

##### Inputs
- **MQ request** read from the trigger's `MQTM-QNAME` into MQ-BUFFER (1000 bytes). It is copied to REQUEST-MSG-COPY:
  - WS-FUNC X(4): the function code. Only 'INQA' is supported.
  - WS-KEY 9(11): the account id.
  - WS-FILLER X(985).
- MQMD values saved per message: MsgId → SAVE-MSGID, CorrelId → SAVE-CORELID, ReplyToQ → SAVE-REPLY2Q.

##### Processing flow
1. `2100-OPEN-ERROR-QUEUE`: MQOPEN **CARD.DEMO.ERROR** with OUTPUT + PASS-ALL-CONTEXT + FAIL-IF-QUIESCING. If it fails, DISPLAY the error and go to 8000-TERMINATION.
2. CICS RETRIEVE MQTM. If the response is NORMAL: input queue = MQTM-QNAME, and the reply queue is hard-coded to **CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT**. Otherwise, build the error 'RESP: … END', run 9000-ERROR, then terminate.
3. `2300-OPEN-INPUT-QUEUE`: MQOPEN with INPUT-SHARED + SAVE-ALL-CONTEXT + FAIL-IF-QUIESCING. On success it sets the REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN flag (misnamed: the flag tracks the input queue). On failure it runs 9000-ERROR and terminates.
4. `2400-OPEN-OUTPUT-QUEUE`: MQOPEN of the reply queue with OUTPUT + PASS-ALL-CONTEXT. It sets RESP-QUEUE-OPEN.
5. `3000-GET-REQUEST`: MQGET with SYNCPOINT + FAIL-IF-QUIESCING + CONVERT + WAIT, a wait interval of 5000 ms, and buffer length 1000.
   - On success: save the MQMD values, copy the request, run `4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY`, and increment MQ-MSG-COUNT.
   - Reason NO-MSG-AVAILABLE: set NO-MORE-MSGS.
   - Any other failure: run 9000-ERROR and terminate.
6. Loop `4000-MAIN-PROCESS` until NO-MORE-MSGS. Each pass issues `EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT`, which commits the previous get and put, then runs 3000-GET-REQUEST again.
7. `4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY`:
   - If WS-FUNC='INQA' and WS-KEY > 0: CICS READ **ACCTDAT** with RIDFLD = the key as X(11).
     - NORMAL: copy the account fields into WS-ACCT-RESPONSE, then run `4100-PUT-REPLY`.
     - NOTFND: reply 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : <key>'.
     - Any other response: 9000-ERROR ('ERROR WHILE READING ACCTFILE'), then terminate.
   - Otherwise: reply 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : <key>FUNCTION : <func>'.
8. `4100-PUT-REPLY`: MQPUT to the reply queue with a 1000-byte buffer. MsgId and CorrelId are copied from the request, the format is STRING, and the CCSID is the queue manager's. PMO = SYNCPOINT + DEFAULT-CONTEXT. A failed put runs 9000-ERROR and terminates.
9. `9000-ERROR`: MQPUT the MQ-ERR-DISPLAY text (1000 bytes) to CARD.DEMO.ERROR under syncpoint. If that put fails, DISPLAY the error and terminate.
10. `8000-TERMINATION`: MQCLOSE each queue that is open (input, reply, error), then `EXEC CICS RETURN`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[1000-CONTROL] --> B[2100-OPEN-ERROR-QUEUE CARD.DEMO.ERROR]
  B --> C[CICS RETRIEVE MQTM]
  C -->|ok| D[2300 open input MQTM-QNAME / 2400 open CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT]
  C -->|fail| E[9000-ERROR -> 8000-TERMINATION]
  D --> G[3000-GET-REQUEST MQGET syncpoint wait 5s]
  G -->|msg| P[4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY]
  P -->|INQA & key>0| R[CICS READ ACCTDAT]
  R -->|NORMAL| PUT[4100-PUT-REPLY MQPUT account data]
  R -->|NOTFND| PUT
  R -->|other| E
  P -->|else| PUT
  PUT --> M[4000-MAIN-PROCESS SYNCPOINT]
  M --> G
  G -->|no msg| T[8000-TERMINATION MQCLOSE x3, CICS RETURN]
```

##### Data
- **ACCTDAT** (VSAM KSDS, copybook CVACT01Y, 300 bytes). It is read only and keyed by ACCT-ID 9(11).
- Fields copied into the reply WS-ACCT-RESPONSE: ACCT-ID, ACTIVE-STATUS, CURR-BAL S9(10)V99, CREDIT-LIMIT, CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT, OPEN-DATE, EXPIRAION-DATE, REISSUE-DATE, CURR-CYC-CREDIT, CURR-CYC-DEBIT, GROUP-ID.
- The reply is fixed text. Each value is preceded by a label filler, for example WS-ACCT-LBL X(13) followed by the 11-digit id, and WS-STATUS-LBL X(17) followed by the status. The amounts are display-format S9(10)V99, so the sign is overpunched in the last digit and there is no decimal point.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Reply messages on CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT. The request's ReplyToQ is saved but **ignored**.
- Error text on CARD.DEMO.ERROR.
- No file updates.

##### External calls
- IBM MQ MQOPEN, MQGET, MQPUT and MQCLOSE, using IBM copybooks CMQGMOV, CMQPMOV, CMQMDV, CMQODV, CMQV and CMQTML.
- CICS RETRIEVE, READ, SYNCPOINT and RETURN.

##### Migration notes
- The reply queue is hard-coded rather than taken from ReplyToQ. The reply copies both MsgId and CorrelId from the request; the usual pattern is to set CorrelId to the request MsgId.
- Gets and puts are under syncpoint, so they are committed together at the next loop SYNCPOINT. The final message is committed implicitly when the task ends normally at RETURN. A terminating error goes to RETURN, which still commits normally because no ROLLBACK is issued.
- The buffer is always 1000 bytes, so replies are padded with spaces.
- WS-KEY is 9(11) moved from text with no numeric validation. Non-numeric data compares unpredictably against ZEROES.
- 5000-CLOSE-INPUT-QUEUE and 5100-CLOSE-OUTPUT-QUEUE perform 8000-TERMINATION recursively when MQCLOSE fails. That can loop, because the open flags are never reset.
- The OPEN calls use QMGR-HANDLE-CONN while GET and PUT use MQ-HCONN. Both are 0, the default CICS connection.
recommendation: Reply label literal texts not transcribed.
note:
Consolidated document for app/app-vsam-mq/cbl/COACCT01.cbl; merged duplicates: sfind-d818870bb558402d90bb84d319eb740e.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Numeric fields in the reply are zoned decimal with implied 2 decimals and trailing sign overpunch (no decimal point), e.g. balance 0000000123{ style; consumers must decode EBCDIC overpunch.
- RETRIEVE error message bug: `MOVE WS-CICS-RESP2-CD TO WS-CICS-RESP2-CD` so RESP2 display is always 0; MQ-ERROR-PARA only set on that path.
- MQCLOSE failures PERFORM 8000-TERMINATION recursively, which retries the same close - potential infinite recursion if a close keeps failing.

title: COPAUA0C (CP00) MQ-triggered card authorization decision and IMS posting
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program **COPAUA0C** (transaction **CP00**, `WS-CICS-TRANID`), an MQ-triggered authorization decision engine. It is started by the CICS MQ trigger monitor: `1000-INITIALIZE` issues `EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(MQTM)`. When RESP=NORMAL, `MQTM-QNAME` becomes the request queue name and `MQTM-TRIGGERDATA` is saved in `WS-TRIGGER-DATA` (it is never used after that). The LINKAGE `DFHCOMMAREA` (X(4096)) is declared but not used.

##### Inputs
- **MQ request message**: read by `MQGET` from the queue named in `MQTM-QNAME` into `W01-GET-BUFFER` X(500). Only the first `W01-DATALEN` bytes are used. The body is **comma-delimited ASCII text**. `UNSTRING ... DELIMITED BY ','` splits it, in this order, into `PENDING-AUTH-REQUEST` (copybook CCPAURQY):
  1. PA-RQ-AUTH-DATE X(6)
  2. PA-RQ-AUTH-TIME X(6)
  3. PA-RQ-CARD-NUM X(16)
  4. PA-RQ-AUTH-TYPE X(4)
  5. PA-RQ-CARD-EXPIRY-DATE X(4)
  6. PA-RQ-MESSAGE-TYPE X(6)
  7. PA-RQ-MESSAGE-SOURCE X(6)
  8. PA-RQ-PROCESSING-CODE 9(6)
  9. amount → `WS-TRANSACTION-AMT-AN` X(13), then `FUNCTION NUMVAL` → PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-AMT (`+9(10).99`) and WS-TRANSACTION-AMT S9(10)V99
  10. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-CATAGORY-CODE X(4)
  11. PA-RQ-ACQR-COUNTRY-CODE X(3)
  12. PA-RQ-POS-ENTRY-MODE 9(2)
  13. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-ID X(15)
  14. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-NAME X(22)
  15. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-CITY X(13)
  16. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-STATE X(2)
  17. PA-RQ-MERCHANT-ZIP X(9)
  18. PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-ID X(15)
- **MQMD of the request**: `MQMD-CORRELID` is saved in WS-SAVE-CORRELID, and `MQMD-REPLYTOQ` is saved in WS-REPLY-QNAME.
- Get options: `MQGMO-NO-SYNCPOINT + MQGMO-WAIT + MQGMO-CONVERT + MQGMO-FAIL-IF-QUIESCING`, wait interval 5000 ms. MsgId and CorrelId are reset to NONE before each get, so any message matches. Format is MQFMT-STRING.

##### Processing flow
1. `1000-INITIALIZE`: RETRIEVE the trigger message. Set the wait interval to 5000. Run `1100-OPEN-REQUEST-QUEUE`: MQOPEN with `MQOO-INPUT-SHARED`. If it fails, log M001 as critical, which ends the task. Then run `3100-READ-REQUEST-MQ` to get the first message.
2. `2000-MAIN-PROCESS` loops `UNTIL NO-MORE-MSG-AVAILABLE OR WS-LOOP-END`. Each pass does the following:
   - `2100-EXTRACT-REQUEST-MSG` (parse the message, as in Inputs).
   - `5000-PROCESS-AUTH`:
     - Set APPROVE-AUTH. Run `1200-SCHEDULE-PSB`: `EXEC DLI SCHD PSB(PSBPAUTB) NODHABEND`. If the status is TC (already scheduled), do TERM and then SCHD again. If the status is not OK (spaces/FW), log I001 as critical.
     - Pre-set CARD-FOUND-XREF and FOUND-ACCT-IN-MSTR.
     - `5100-READ-XREF-RECORD`: CICS READ of file **CCXREF**, key = card number (16). Outcomes:
       - NORMAL: card found.
       - NOTFND: set CARD-NFOUND-XREF and NFOUND-ACCT-IN-MSTR, and log A001 as a warning.
       - Any other response: log C001 as critical.
     - Only if the card was found:
       - `5200-READ-ACCT-RECORD`: READ **ACCTDAT**, key = XREF-ACCT-ID as X(11). NOTFND logs A002 (warning); any other error logs C002 (critical).
       - `5300-READ-CUST-RECORD`: READ **CUSTDAT**, key = XREF-CUST-ID X(9). NOTFND logs A003 (warning); any other error logs C003 (critical).
       - `5500-READ-AUTH-SUMMRY`: `EXEC DLI GU SEGMENT(PAUTSUM0) WHERE(ACCNTID = PA-ACCT-ID)`. OK means the summary was found. GE means not found. Any other status logs I002 (critical).
       - `5600-READ-PROFILE-DATA` (an empty CONTINUE stub).
     - `6000-MAKE-DECISION` (see the rules below).
     - `7100-SEND-RESPONSE`.
     - If the card was found, `8000-WRITE-AUTH-TO-DB`, which runs `8400-UPDATE-SUMMARY` then `8500-INSERT-AUTH`.
   - `ADD 1 TO WS-MSG-PROCESSED`, then `EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT`, which commits both the IMS and VSAM work. Then set IMS-PSB-NOT-SCHD.
   - If WS-MSG-PROCESSED > 500 (`WS-REQSTS-PROCESS-LIMIT`), set WS-LOOP-END. Otherwise run `3100-READ-REQUEST-MQ`. When the MQGET reason is `MQRC-NO-MSG-AVAILABLE`, the loop ends normally. Any other MQGET failure logs M003 (critical, recorded with subsystem 'C').
3. `9000-TERMINATE`: `EXEC DLI TERM` if the PSB is scheduled, then `9100-CLOSE-REQUEST-QUEUE` (MQCLOSE; a failure logs M005 as a warning). Then `EXEC CICS RETURN`.

**Decision rules (`6000-MAKE-DECISION`)**
- Copy the card number and transaction id into the reply. The reply auth id code is set to **PA-RQ-AUTH-TIME**.
- If the auth summary was found: available = PA-CREDIT-LIMIT − PA-CREDIT-BALANCE. If the transaction amount > available, the auth is DECLINED with reason INSUFFICIENT-FUND.
- Else, if the account was found: available = ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT − ACCT-CURR-BAL. The same comparison is applied.
- Else (card or account not found): DECLINED.
- If declined: response code **'05'** and approved amount 0. If approved: response code **'00'** and approved amount = the requested amount.
- The reason defaults to '0000'. When declined, it is set by the first matching condition, in this order:
  - card, account or customer not found → '3100'
  - INSUFFICIENT-FUND → '4100'
  - CARD-NOT-ACTIVE → '4200'
  - ACCOUNT-CLOSED → '4300'
  - CARD-FRAUD → '5100'
  - MERCHANT-FRAUD → '5200'
  - otherwise → '9000'
- The reply is built with STRING into W02-PUT-BUFFER X(200), using `WITH POINTER WS-RESP-LENGTH`. Its CSV layout is: `card,txnid,authid,respcode,reason,approvedAmt(-zzzzzzzzz9.99),` (note the trailing comma).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[CICS RETRIEVE MQTM - trigger] --> B[1100-OPEN-REQUEST-QUEUE MQOPEN]
  B --> C[3100-READ-REQUEST-MQ MQGET wait 5s]
  C -->|no msg| T[9000-TERMINATE DLI TERM + MQCLOSE]
  C -->|msg| D[2100-EXTRACT-REQUEST-MSG UNSTRING CSV]
  D --> E[1200-SCHEDULE-PSB PSBPAUTB]
  E --> F[5100 READ CCXREF by card]
  F -->|found| G[5200 READ ACCTDAT / 5300 READ CUSTDAT / 5500 DLI GU PAUTSUM0]
  F -->|not found| H
  G --> H[6000-MAKE-DECISION]
  H --> I[7100-SEND-RESPONSE MQPUT1 to ReplyToQ]
  I --> J{card found?}
  J -->|yes| K[8400 REPL/ISRT PAUTSUM0 + 8500 ISRT PAUTDTL1]
  J -->|no| L
  K --> L[SYNCPOINT, count++]
  L -->|count>500| T
  L -->|else| C
  T --> R[CICS RETURN]
```

##### Data
- **CCXREF** (VSAM KSDS, CVACT03Y, 50 bytes): XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) key, XREF-CUST-ID 9(9), XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11), filler X(14). Read only.
- **ACCTDAT** (CVACT01Y, 300 bytes): ACCT-ID 9(11) key, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X, ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99, followed by dates and other fields. Read only.
- **CUSTDAT** (CVCUS01Y): read only. Only the found/not-found result is used.
- **IMS DBPAUTP0** (HIDAM, PSB PSBPAUTB PROCOPT=AP; secondary index DBPAUTX0 on ACCNTID):
  - Root **PAUTSUM0** (100 bytes, CIPAUSMY):
    - PA-ACCT-ID S9(11) COMP-3 (6 bytes; key ACCNTID)
    - PA-CUST-ID 9(9)
    - PA-AUTH-STATUS X
    - PA-ACCOUNT-STATUS X(2)×5
    - PA-CREDIT-LIMIT, PA-CASH-LIMIT, PA-CREDIT-BALANCE, PA-CASH-BALANCE: each S9(9)V99 COMP-3
    - PA-APPROVED-AUTH-CNT and PA-DECLINED-AUTH-CNT: each S9(4) COMP
    - PA-APPROVED-AUTH-AMT and PA-DECLINED-AUTH-AMT: each S9(9)V99 COMP-3
    - FILLER X(34)
  - Child **PAUTDTL1** (200 bytes, CIPAUDTY):
    - Key PAUT9CTS (8 bytes) = PA-AUTH-DATE-9C S9(5) COMP-3 + PA-AUTH-TIME-9C S9(9) COMP-3
    - The request fields
    - PA-AUTH-ID-CODE X(6)
    - PA-AUTH-RESP-CODE X(2)
    - PA-AUTH-RESP-REASON X(4)
    - PA-TRANSACTION-AMT and PA-APPROVED-AMT: each S9(10)V99 COMP-3
    - PA-MATCH-STATUS X: P = pending, D = declined, E = expired, M = matched
    - PA-AUTH-FRAUD X: F or R
    - PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE X(8)
    - FILLER X(17)
- **Writes**
  - `8400-UPDATE-SUMMARY`: if no summary existed, INITIALIZE it (numeric fields set to zero) and set the account id and customer id from the xref. In all cases, copy ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT → PA-CREDIT-LIMIT and ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT → PA-CASH-LIMIT.
    - Approved: approved count +1, approved amount += approved amount, PA-CREDIT-BALANCE += approved amount, and **PA-CASH-BALANCE set to 0**.
    - Declined: declined count +1, and PA-DECLINED-AUTH-AMT += PA-TRANSACTION-AMT.
    - Then DLI **REPL** if the summary was found, or **ISRT** if it was not. A non-OK status logs I003 (critical).
  - `8500-INSERT-AUTH`: ASKTIME/FORMATTIME to get YYDDD, TIME and milliseconds. Then:
    - PA-AUTH-DATE-9C = 99999 − YYDDD
    - PA-AUTH-TIME-9C = 999999999 − (HHMMSS×1000 + ms)
    - These inverted keys make the newest record sort first.
    - Copy the request and reply fields into the detail record. Match status = 'P' if approved, else 'D'. Fraud flag and fraud date = spaces.
    - `ISRT PAUTSUM0 WHERE(ACCNTID=PA-ACCT-ID) / PAUTDTL1`. A non-OK status logs I004 (critical).
- **TD queue CSSL**: ERROR-LOG-RECORD (CCPAUERY, 136 bytes):
  - ERR-DATE X(6) (YYMMDD) and ERR-TIME X(6)
  - ERR-APPLICATION = 'CP00', ERR-PROGRAM = 'COPAUA0C'
  - ERR-LOCATION X(4)
  - ERR-LEVEL: L/I/W/C
  - ERR-SUBSYSTEM: A/C/I/D/M/F
  - ERR-CODE-1 X(9), ERR-CODE-2 X(9)
  - ERR-MESSAGE X(50), ERR-EVENT-KEY X(20)

##### Outputs & side effects
- One MQ reply per request, sent with **MQPUT1** to the request's ReplyToQ. MQMD settings:
  - MSGTYPE = REPLY
  - CORRELID = the request CorrelId
  - MSGID = NONE
  - not persistent
  - **EXPIRY = 50** (in tenths of a second, so 5 s)
  - FORMAT = STRING
  - PMO = NO-SYNCPOINT + DEFAULT-CONTEXT
  - Buffer length = WS-RESP-LENGTH
  - A failed put logs M004 (critical).
- IMS summary update and detail insert, committed at the per-message SYNCPOINT.
- Error records written to TD queue CSSL. When a logged error is ERR-CRITICAL, `9990-END-ROUTINE` runs: DLI TERM, MQCLOSE, then CICS RETURN. This ends the task without SYNCPOINT, so CICS backs out the uncommitted unit of work at task end.

##### External calls
- **IBM MQ**:
  - MQOPEN (connection handle 0 = default CICS connection)
  - MQGET
  - MQPUT1 (a separate W02-HCONN-REPLY, also 0)
  - MQCLOSE
  - Copybooks CMQODV, CMQMDV, CMQV, CMQTML, CMQPMOV, CMQGMOV (IBM-supplied, not in the repo).
- **IMS DL/I through CICS**: SCHD/TERM PSBPAUTB; GU, REPL and ISRT on DBPAUTP0.
- **CICS**: READ (CCXREF/ACCTDAT/CUSTDAT), ASKTIME, FORMATTIME, WRITEQ TD, SYNCPOINT, RETURN.

##### Migration notes
- **Responses go out before the DB write and are not under syncpoint** (MQPUT1 with NO-SYNCPOINT). If the IMS write later fails (critical error, so the task ends and backs out), the requester has already received the approval.
- MQGET is also NO-SYNCPOINT, so a request whose processing abends is lost; it is not re-queued.
- The PSB is re-scheduled for every message. The SYNCPOINT releases the PSB, and the code sets the flag to NOT-SCHD.
- Limit check: `WS-MSG-PROCESSED > 500` means up to **501** messages are processed per trigger.
- Declined auths still update the summary's credit limits. Approved auths reset **PA-CASH-BALANCE to 0** on every approval.
- Available credit comes from the IMS summary when one exists, not from the VSAM balance. ACCTDAT is used only when no summary exists.
- The flags CARD-NOT-ACTIVE, ACCOUNT-CLOSED, CARD-FRAUD and MERCHANT-FRAUD are **never set** anywhere, so reasons 4200/4300/5100/5200 cannot occur (dead). Reason 9000 also cannot occur. ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS and card expiry are not checked. A customer not found does not cause a decline by itself: NFOUND-CUST only affects the reason code, and only when the auth is already declined.
- If the account is not found but the card is, NFOUND-ACCT is set, so the auth is declined with '3100'. The summary update still runs, using whatever ACCOUNT-RECORD contains (stale/uninitialized credit limits). This is a quirk.
- The auth id code is the request's auth time, not a generated value.
- WS-RESP-LENGTH is initialised to 1 and never reset between messages. STRING WITH POINTER therefore keeps appending, and the reply length grows across messages in the same task. When it exceeds 200, STRING overflows; with no ON OVERFLOW clause the buffer is left truncated. **This is a likely latent defect.** Replies after the first may carry data from earlier messages.
- NUMVAL is used on the amount text, so invalid text gives undefined or zero results; there is no validation. The UNSTRING has no field-count check.
- The time keys are inverted (99999−YYDDD, 999999999−time) so that a GNP returns the newest first. YYDDD has a 2-digit year, so ordering breaks across a century boundary. Two requests in the same millisecond give a duplicate key (II), which logs I004 as critical.
- M003 (MQGET failure) is recorded with subsystem 'C' (CICS), not 'M'.
recommendation: Confirm intended behavior of non-reset WS-RESP-LENGTH and the unused decline-reason flags (4200/4300/5100/5200) with the business owner.
note: Duplicate of sfind-ed8806e1e84244d6b802febe5cca0c30 (COPAUA0C (CICS tran CP00)); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: COPAUS0C (CPVS) pending authorization summary list screen
description:
##### Entry point
CICS pseudo-conversational program **COPAUS0C**, transaction **CPVS** (Pending Authorization Summary list). It is reached by XCTL from the menu (COMEN01C) or from COPAUS1C (PF3). It can also be started directly with no COMMAREA.

##### Inputs
- COMMAREA `CARDDEMO-COMMAREA` (COCOM01Y) plus the extension `CDEMO-CPVS-INFO`:
  - PAU-SEL-FLG X(1)
  - PAU-SELECTED X(8) (the selected auth key)
  - PAUKEY-PREV-PG X(8) OCCURS 20 (key of the first row of each page)
  - PAUKEY-LAST X(8)
  - PAGE-NUM S9(4) COMP
  - NEXT-PAGE-FLG X
  - AUTH-KEYS X(8) OCCURS 5 (keys of the 5 rows on the current page)
- BMS map **COPAU0A**/mapset **COPAU00**:
  - Input: ACCTIDI (account id), SEL0001I–SEL0005I (selection)
  - Output: header fields; customer fields CUSTIDO, CNAMEO, ADDR001O/002O, PHONE1O; CREDLIMO, CASHLIMO, APPRCNTO, DECLCNTO, CREDBALO, CASHBALO, APPRAMTO, DECLAMTO; and rows 01–05: TRNIDnn, PDATEnn, PTIMEnn, PTYPEnn, PAPRVnn, PSTATnn, PAMT00n
- AID keys: ENTER, PF3, PF7, PF8.

##### Processing flow
1. **EIBCALEN=0**: initialize the COMMAREA, set REENTER, and send a blank screen.
2. **First entry** (not REENTER): set REENTER. If CDEMO-ACCT-ID is numeric, use it as the account; otherwise blank it. Then run GATHER-DETAILS and send with ERASE.
3. **Re-entry**: RECEIVE the map, then branch on EIBAID:
   - **ENTER** → PROCESS-ENTER-KEY:
     - Account blank → "Please enter Acct Id...". Account not numeric → "Acct Id must be Numeric ...".
     - Otherwise store the account in WS-ACCT-ID and CDEMO-ACCT-ID. Take the first non-blank SELnnnnI (in order 1–5) as the selection flag; its stored AUTH-KEYS(n) becomes PAU-SELECTED.
     - If the flag is 'S' or 's': set TO-PROGRAM=COPAUS1C, FROM-TRANID=CPVS, FROM-PROGRAM=COPAUS0C, set PGM-ENTER, and XCTL to COPAUS1C with the COMMAREA. Any other flag value → "Invalid selection. Valid value is S".
     - Then GATHER-DETAILS (only reached when there was no XCTL).
   - **PF3** → TO-PROGRAM=COMEN01C; RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN. This defaults to COSGN00C if blank, sets FROM fields and context 0, and XCTLs.
   - **PF7** (previous page): if PAGE-NUM > 1, decrement it, restart from PAUKEY-PREV-PG(page), and page forward. Otherwise "You are already at the top of the page...".
   - **PF8** (next page): restart from PAUKEY-LAST, if set. Then, if NEXT-PAGE-YES, page forward; otherwise "You are already at the bottom of the page...".
   - **Any other key** → CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY.
4. **GATHER-DETAILS**: PAGE-NUM=0. If an account is set:
   - GATHER-ACCOUNT-DETAILS:
     - READ **CXACAIX** (card xref by account AIX, key X(11)). On success it sets CDEMO-CUST-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM.
     - READ **ACCTDAT** by XREF-ACCT-ID.
     - READ **CUSTDAT** by XREF-CUST-ID.
     - NOTFND or another error on any read: build a message ('Account:… not found in XREF file. Resp:… Reas:…' and similar) and SEND the screen immediately. Processing then continues.
     - Format the name ("first M last") and address (line1,line2 / line3,state,zip5), phone, and credit/cash limits.
   - GET-AUTH-SUMMARY: SCHEDULE-PSB PSBPAUTB, then `DLI GU PAUTSUM0 WHERE ACCNTID = CDEMO-ACCT-ID`. If found, display the approved and declined counts and amounts and the credit and cash balances. Otherwise display zeros.
   - INITIALIZE-AUTH-DATA: clear the 5 rows and set the SEL fields to protected (DFHBMPRO).
   - If the summary was found, PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD.
5. **PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD**:
   - Loop up to 5 rows. On PF7 the first row uses REPOSITION-AUTHORIZATIONS (`GNP PAUTDTL1 WHERE PAUT9CTS = saved key`). All other rows use GET-AUTHORIZATIONS (unqualified `GNP PAUTDTL1`). GE/GB = end of list.
   - POPULATE-AUTH-LIST fills row n with:
     - txn id
     - date MM/DD/YY, taken from PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE YYMMDD
     - time HH:MM:SS
     - type
     - A/D: 'A' if response code '00'
     - match status
     - approved amount
     - SEL unprotected (DFHBMUNP)
     - The key is saved in AUTH-KEYS(n).
   - After the first row (when WS-IDX becomes 2), PAGE-NUM+1 and that key is stored in PREV-PG(page). After 5 rows, one more GNP sets NEXT-PAGE-YES or NEXT-PAGE-NO.
6. **SEND-PAULST-SCREEN**: if a PSB is scheduled, SYNCPOINT to release it. Fill the header (titles, tran CPVS, program, date MM/DD/YY, time). SEND with or without ERASE. Finally `RETURN TRANSID(CPVS) COMMAREA`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[COPAUS0C / CPVS] --> C{EIBCALEN=0?}
  C -->|yes| B[send blank COPAU0A]
  C -->|no| R{REENTER?}
  R -->|no| G[GATHER-DETAILS]
  R -->|yes| K{EIBAID}
  K -->|ENTER| E[PROCESS-ENTER-KEY validate acct + SEL]
  E -->|SEL=S| X[XCTL COPAUS1C]
  E --> G
  K -->|PF3| M[XCTL COMEN01C]
  K -->|PF7| P7[PREV-PG key -> GU summary -> REPOSITION GNP]
  K -->|PF8| P8[PAUKEY-LAST -> GU summary -> REPOSITION GNP]
  G --> A1[READ CXACAIX / ACCTDAT / CUSTDAT]
  A1 --> A2[DLI SCHD PSBPAUTB + GU PAUTSUM0]
  A2 --> PF[PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD GNP PAUTDTL1 x5]
  P7 --> PF
  P8 --> PF
  PF --> SND[SYNCPOINT, SEND MAP, RETURN TRANSID CPVS]
```

##### Data
- Read only:
  - CXACAIX: CVACT03Y xref by account AIX
  - ACCTDAT: CVACT01Y
  - CUSTDAT: CVCUS01Y
  - IMS DBPAUTP0 via PSBPAUTB: PAUTSUM0 root (GU) and PAUTDTL1 children (GNP)
- See the COPAUA0C flow for the segment layouts. The auth key is the 8-byte PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY (inverted date/time COMP-3), so GNP returns the newest auth first.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Screen COPAU0A.
- COMMAREA paging state.
- XCTL to COPAUS1C (detail view) or COMEN01C (menu).
- SYNCPOINT before each SEND, which only releases the PSB because nothing is updated.

##### External calls
- CICS: READ, RECEIVE/SEND MAP, XCTL, RETURN, SYNCPOINT.
- IMS DL/I: SCHD/TERM, GU, GNP.

##### Migration notes
- The error paths call SEND-PAULST-SCREEN in the middle of processing **without returning**. Processing continues and the screen may be sent twice in one task.
- The account read errors set WS-ERR-FLG only for "OTHER" responses. NOTFND does not set it, so the summary GU still runs.
- PF7/PF8 call GET-AUTH-SUMMARY, which also uses CDEMO-ACCT-ID. In PF8, after REPOSITION, the loop's first row uses the unqualified GNP, so the page starts *after* the last key. In PF7, row 1 is the repositioned key itself.
- PREV-PG has 20 entries with no bounds check. Paging past page 20 overwrites storage.
- The first-row capture happens when WS-IDX=2 (that is, after row 1 is populated). GATHER-DETAILS resets PAGE-NUM to 0.
- PF7 always sets NEXT-PAGE-YES.
- The amount display uses edit mask `-zzzzzzz9.99`, so values above 99,999,999.99 are truncated.
- The date is displayed from PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE, assumed to be YYMMDD (taken as supplied in the request, not validated).
- The selection check only looks at the first non-blank SEL field.
- PF3 sets TO-PROGRAM=COMEN01C. The 'COSGN00C' default is therefore unreachable from PF3.
recommendation: Fully documented from source.
note: Duplicate of sfind-dc30b1d02e7d41f9b03fd81743cbaa83 (COPAUS0C (CICS tran CPVS)); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: INTRDRJ2 - second-level copy of FTP backup file (submitted by INTRDRJ1)
