title: INTCALC / CBACT04C - monthly interest calculation, interest transaction generation and account balance update
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `INTCALC` (app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl), single step `STEP15 EXEC PGM=CBACT04C,PARM='2022071800'` loaded from `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB`. Scheduled in Control-M folder `MONTHLY-InterestCalculation`: CLOSEFIL -> INTCALC -> COMBTRAN -> WAITSTEP -> OPENFIL (app/scheduler/CardDemo.controlm). CICS files must be closed first because ACCTFILE is opened I-O.

##### Inputs
- PARM: `EXTERNAL-PARMS` = `PARM-LENGTH S9(4) COMP` + `PARM-DATE X(10)`. JCL hardcodes `2022071800` (it is used only as the first 10 chars of generated TRAN-IDs, not as a business date).
- DD `TCATBALF` -> `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.VSAM.KSDS` (SELECT TCATBAL-FILE, INDEXED, SEQUENTIAL, key FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY). Layout CVTRA01Y (50 bytes): TRANCAT-ACCT-ID 9(11) | TRANCAT-TYPE-CD X(2) | TRANCAT-CD 9(4) | TRAN-CAT-BAL S9(9)V99 zoned (11) | FILLER X(22). Key = first 17 bytes.
- DD `XREFFILE` -> `CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS` and `XREFFIL1` -> `CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH` (alternate key path; SELECT XREF-FILE RANDOM, RECORD KEY FD-XREF-CARD-NUM, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY FD-XREF-ACCT-ID). Layout CVACT03Y (50): XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) | XREF-CUST-ID 9(9) | XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) | FILLER X(14).
- DD `ACCTFILE` -> `ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS` (RANDOM, opened I-O). Layout CVACT01Y (300): ACCT-ID 9(11) | ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X | ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 | ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 | ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 | ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) | ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) | ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) | ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT S9(10)V99 | ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT S9(10)V99 | ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) | ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) | FILLER X(178).
- DD `DISCGRP` -> `DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS` (RANDOM). Layout CVTRA02Y (50): DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) | DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD X(2) | DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD 9(4) | DIS-INT-RATE S9(4)V99 | FILLER X(28).

##### Processing flow
1. Open TCATBALF INPUT, XREFFILE INPUT, DISCGRP INPUT, ACCTFILE I-O, TRANSACT OUTPUT (paragraphs 0000..0400). Any status other than '00' -> DISPLAY message, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM (CEE3ABD code 999).
2. Loop `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'`: 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT reads next TCATBAL record sequentially (status '10' -> EOF flag; other non-'00' -> abend). Each record is DISPLAYed and counted (WS-RECORD-COUNT).
3. Account break: if TRANCAT-ACCT-ID differs from WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM: if not the first record, 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT for the previous account; reset WS-TOTAL-INT to 0; remember new account; 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA (random READ ACCTFILE by ACCT-ID; INVALID KEY displays 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND' then, because status <> '00', abends); 1110-GET-XREF-DATA (READ XREF-FILE KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID via AIX; not found -> abend). Only the first xref row for the account is used.
4. For every record: build DISCGRP key = ACCT-GROUP-ID + TRANCAT-TYPE-CD + TRANCAT-CD; 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE. Status '00' ok; '23' (not found) -> move 'DEFAULT' to group id and 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE re-reads (must return '00' else abend); any other status -> abend.
5. If DIS-INT-RATE <> 0: 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST: `WS-MONTHLY-INT = (TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200` (no ROUNDED -> truncated to 2 decimals), add to WS-TOTAL-INT, then 1300-B-WRITE-TX; then 1400-COMPUTE-FEES (empty stub, EXIT only). Rate 0 -> no interest, no transaction.
6. 1300-B-WRITE-TX builds TRAN-RECORD (CVTRA05Y): TRAN-ID = PARM-DATE(10) || WS-TRANID-SUFFIX 9(6) (suffix incremented per transaction, starts 000001); TRAN-TYPE-CD '01'; TRAN-CAT-CD 5 (from literal '05'); TRAN-SOURCE 'System'; TRAN-DESC = 'Int. for a/c ' || ACCT-ID; TRAN-AMT = WS-MONTHLY-INT; merchant id 0, name/city/zip spaces; TRAN-CARD-NUM = XREF-CARD-NUM; ORIG-TS and PROC-TS = current timestamp 'YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000' (Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP). WRITE to TRANSACT; non-'00' -> abend.
7. 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT: ACCT-CURR-BAL += WS-TOTAL-INT; ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT = 0; ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT = 0; REWRITE account; non-'00' -> abend.
8. Close all 5 files (9000..9400, abend on error), DISPLAY end, GOBACK.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[INTCALC STEP15 CBACT04C PARM 2022071800] --> B[Open TCATBALF XREFFILE DISCGRP ACCTFILE-IO TRANSACT-OUT]
  B --> C{1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT EOF?}
  C -- yes --> Z[Close files GOBACK - last account NOT rewritten]
  C -- no --> D{TRANCAT-ACCT-ID new account?}
  D -- yes, not first --> E[1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT prev acct: bal+=total int, cyc credit/debit=0, REWRITE]
  D -- yes, first --> F
  E --> F[1100-GET-ACCT-DATA + 1110-GET-XREF-DATA via AIX]
  D -- no --> G
  F --> G[1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE DISCGRP key group+type+cat]
  G -- status 23 --> H[1200-A read group DEFAULT]
  G -- 00 --> I{DIS-INT-RATE = 0?}
  H --> I
  I -- no --> J[1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST bal*rate/1200; 1300-B-WRITE-TX to SYSTRAN; 1400 fees stub]
  I -- yes --> C
  J --> C
```

##### Data
- Read: TCATBALF KSDS (sequential), CARDXREF via AIX path, ACCTDATA KSDS, DISCGRP KSDS.
- Updated: ACCTDATA (REWRITE: ACCT-CURR-BAL, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT).
- Written: DD `TRANSACT` -> new GDG generation `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.SYSTRAN(+1)`, DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE), RECFM=F, LRECL=350. Record CVTRA05Y (350): TRAN-ID X(16) | TRAN-TYPE-CD X(2) | TRAN-CAT-CD 9(4) | TRAN-SOURCE X(10) | TRAN-DESC X(100) | TRAN-AMT S9(9)V99 | TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(9) | MERCHANT-NAME X(50) | MERCHANT-CITY X(50) | MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) | TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) | TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) | TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) | FILLER X(20).

##### Outputs & side effects
SYSTRAN(+1) file of interest transactions (consumed downstream by COMBTRAN per scheduler, not traced here); account master balance updates; SYSOUT DISPLAY of every TCATBAL record and error messages. Abend U999 on any I/O error (GDG deleted on abnormal end per DISP; ACCTDATA rewrites already done are NOT rolled back).

##### External calls
- `CEE3ABD` (LE abend service) with ABCODE=999, TIMING=0.
- No other CALLs.

##### Migration notes
- **Last account never updated**: the `ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` branch inside the loop requires END-OF-FILE='Y' at loop top, but `PERFORM UNTIL` (test-before) exits first, so the branch is dead. The final account's interest is written to SYSTRAN but never added to ACCT-CURR-BAL and its cycle totals are not zeroed. Decide whether to replicate.
- Cycle credit/debit are zeroed only for accounts that have TCATBAL rows (and not the last one).
- Interest is truncated, not rounded; negative category balances yield negative interest transactions.
- Division by 1200 = annual % rate / 12 months.
- Fallback to group 'DEFAULT' (padded to X(10)) keeps type/cat from the original key; missing DEFAULT row abends.
- TRAN-ID uniqueness depends only on PARM + 6-digit counter; the hardcoded PARM means reruns generate identical IDs.
- TRAN-CAT-CD receives literal '05' -> numeric 0005.
- Open-error message for DISCGRP wrongly says 'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE'.
- XREF lookup by account uses the alternate index (DD XREFFIL1 is the AIX path DD COBOL derives for the alternate key); non-unique account -> first card returned.
- 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS formats status as 4 digits; for '9x' statuses the second byte is shown as binary value.
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm with business whether the dead final-account update (last account never rewritten) is a defect to fix or behavior to preserve, and whether PARM should become a real run date.

Consolidated document for app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl, app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl; merged duplicates: sfind-6440b88600f84439a59fee8a522cc43b, sfind-3bc5185f1ef745a69cd35f3e5cfc1fab.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Cycle credit/debit are zeroed for EVERY account that has at least one TCATBAL record, even if rate=0 (no interest) - 1050 runs regardless.
- Default-group fallback is triggered only by status '23'; the DEFAULT key keeps the original type/category codes.
- `WS-MONTHLY-INT` arithmetic has no ROUNDED: truncation to 2 decimals; rate is annual percent (`/1200`). Negative category balances yield negative interest.
- Transaction ID = 10-char PARM date + 6-digit counter; rerunning with the same PARM produces the same IDs (duplicates when merged). Counter wraps after 999,999.
- The xref is read by account alternate key: with multiple cards per account the first card on the AIX is used.
- Fees are a stub; nothing is charged.


End-to-end: INTCALC is submitted by run_interest_calc.sh and run_full_batch.sh after posting, and scheduled in the Control-M MONTHLY interest folder; followed by TRANBKP -> COMBTRAN -> TRANIDX; together they form the month-end interest cycle. title: READCARD / CBACT02C - sequential dump of card master to SYSOUT
description:
##### Entry point
Job `READCARD`, `STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C` (triggered after READACCT in CA-7).

##### Inputs
DD CARDFILE -> `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDATA.VSAM.KSDS`, 150-byte CVACT02Y: CARD-NUM X(16) | CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) | CARD-CVV-CD 9(3) | CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) | CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) | CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X | FILLER X(59).

##### Processing flow
Open INPUT (abend on error) -> loop READ next; '00' -> DISPLAY CARD-RECORD once; '10' -> EOF; other -> DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', status, abend 999 -> close -> GOBACK.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[READCARD CBACT02C] --> B[OPEN CARDFILE]
  B --> C{READ next}
  C -- 00 --> D[DISPLAY CARD-RECORD] --> C
  C -- 10 --> E[CLOSE GOBACK]
  C -- other --> F[CEE3ABD 999]
```

##### Data
Read-only card master.

##### Outputs & side effects
SYSOUT listing only (includes CVV values).

##### External calls
CEE3ABD.

##### Migration notes
Utility/diagnostic; near-identical to CBACT03C/CBCUS01C (see READXREF/READCUST) except CBACT02C displays each record once.
recommendation: Fully documented.
note: Duplicate of sfind-092c678c69e54131a412533b8c2f303f (READCARD / CBACT02C and READCUST / CBCUS01C VSAM dump utilit); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: DUSRSECJ - build user security KSDS (USRSEC) from in-stream seed users
description:
##### Entry point
Job `DUSRSECJ` (setup).

##### Inputs
In-stream SYSUT1: 10 records, 80-byte CSUSR01Y layout: SEC-USR-ID X(8) | SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) | SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) | SEC-USR-PWD X(8) | SEC-USR-TYPE X(1) | FILLER X(23). IDs ADMIN001-ADMIN005 (type 'A') and USER0001-USER0005 (type 'U'); all passwords are the same 8-character literal [REDACTED] stored in plaintext.

##### Processing flow
1. PREDEL IEFBR14 deletes `USRSEC.PS` (MOD,DELETE,DELETE).
2. STEP01 IEBGENER copies SYSUT1 to `USRSEC.PS` NEW,CATLG FB LRECL 80, UNIT=SYSAD TRK(10,5); SYSIN DUMMY.
3. STEP02 IDCAMS: DELETE USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS; SET MAXCC=0; DEFINE CLUSTER KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80) REUSE INDEXED TRACKS(45,15) FREESPACE(10,15) CISZ(8192), DATA .DAT, INDEX .IDX.
4. STEP03 IDCAMS REPRO INFILE(IN=USRSEC.PS) OUTFILE(OUT=KSDS).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[DUSRSECJ] --> B[PREDEL IEFBR14 USRSEC.PS]
  B --> C[STEP01 IEBGENER instream to USRSEC.PS]
  C --> D[STEP02 DELETE/DEFINE USRSEC KSDS key 8]
  D --> E[STEP03 REPRO PS to KSDS]
```

##### Data
Writes USRSEC.PS and USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS (CICS file USRSEC, opened by OPENFIL; used by sign-on).

##### Outputs & side effects
Replaces all users.

##### External calls
IEFBR14, IEBGENER, IDCAMS.

##### Migration notes
Plaintext passwords in JCL and data - migration should hash/secure. Records already in ascending key order (ADMIN < USER) as required by REPRO. No COND. Trailing '//' null statement ends the job before the version comment.
recommendation: Fully documented; move seed credentials out of source in the target.
note:
End-to-end: DUSRSECJ is submitted by remote_refresh.sh/run_full_batch.sh; builds USRSEC read by COSGN00C sign-on and the COUSR0xC admin screens. Upstream findings: sfind-89eccdc975c54f8c8f058e029a06ca5f, sfind-574c7fefe140460688d7131108eb4d55.

title: TCATBALF - (re)load transaction category balance KSDS from flat file

JCL job `TCATBALF`; in CA-7 it is triggered by TRANCATG (CardDemo.ca7, SCHID 032).

2. STEP10 DEFINE CLUSTER TCATBALF.VSAM.KSDS CYL(1 5) VOL AWSHJ1 KEYS(17 0) RECORDSIZE(50 50) SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) ERASE INDEXED.

  B --> C[STEP10 DEFINE key 17 rec 50]

Writes TCATBALF.VSAM.KSDS, which CBTRN02C (POSTTRAN) updates and CBACT04C (INTCALC) reads; PRTCATBL unloads it.

Asynchronous; SDSF RC does not confirm the file opened. Region name hardcoded. DISCGRP and TCATBALF are not reopened here (presumably not CICS files). Counterpart CLOSEFIL is outside this batch.

title: TRANIDX - define and build TRANSACT alternate index and path on processed timestamp
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `TRANIDX`, run on demand (e.g. after TRANBKP, which deletes the AIX but does not recreate it).

##### Inputs
Existing `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS`.

##### Processing flow
1. STEP20 IDCAMS: DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX NAME(TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) RELATE(TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) KEYS(26 304) NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE RECORDSIZE(350,350) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) CYLINDERS(5,1), DATA .AIX.DATA, INDEX .AIX.INDEX.
2. STEP25 IDCAMS: DEFINE PATH NAME(TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH) PATHENTRY(TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX).
3. STEP30 IDCAMS: BLDINDEX INDATASET(KSDS) OUTDATASET(AIX).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TRANIDX] --> B[STEP20 DEFINE AIX KEYS 26 304]
  B --> C[STEP25 DEFINE PATH]
  C --> D[STEP30 BLDINDEX]
```

##### Data
Creates TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX (+DATA/INDEX) and .AIX.PATH; reads the base KSDS. AIX key = TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) at offset 304.

##### Outputs & side effects
Alternate index for timestamp-ordered access (CICS file CXACAIX).

##### External calls
IDCAMS only.

##### Migration notes
Identical to TRANFILE STEP20-30 but with no preceding DELETE and no CICS close/open: if the AIX already exists, STEP20 fails (duplicate catalog entry) and, with no COND, STEP25/STEP30 still run. CICS files must be closed/reopened separately.
recommendation: Fully documented.

End-to-end: TRANIDX is the last data step of run_posting.sh, run_interest_calc.sh and run_full_batch.sh, rebuilding the TRANSACT processed-timestamp AIX after POSTTRAN/COMBTRAN. JCL job `TRANFILE` (initial load / rebuild of the transaction master). Not found in the Control-M folders; run on demand.

##### Inputs
`AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT` (350-byte CVTRA06Y-format records, must be in ascending TRAN-ID order with unique keys for REPRO into KSDS). SDSF ISFIN in-stream commands.

##### Processing flow
1. CLCIFIL `EXEC PGM=SDSF`: ISFIN issues `/F CICSAWSA,'CEMT SET FIL(TRANSACT ) CLO'` and `/F CICSAWSA,'CEMT SET FIL(CXACAIX ) CLO'` (MVS MODIFY to CICS region CICSAWSA). Output ISFOUT/CMDOUT to SYSOUT.
2. STEP05 IDCAMS: DELETE TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS CLUSTER; IF MAXCC LE 08 SET 0; DELETE TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX ALTERNATEINDEX; same reset.
3. STEP10 IDCAMS: DEFINE CLUSTER TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS CYL(1 5) VOL AWSHJ1 KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(350 350) SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) ERASE INDEXED (.DATA/.INDEX).
4. STEP15 IDCAMS: `REPRO INFILE(TRANSACT) OUTFILE(TRANVSAM)`, TRANSACT DD = DALYTRAN.PS.INIT, TRANVSAM DD = TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS (both DISP=SHR).
5. STEP20 IDCAMS: DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX RELATE(TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) KEYS(26 304) NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE RECORDSIZE(350,350) VOL AWSHJ1 CYL(5,1). Offset 304 length 26 = TRAN-PROC-TS in CVTRA05Y.
6. STEP25 IDCAMS: DEFINE PATH TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH PATHENTRY(TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX).
7. STEP30 IDCAMS: BLDINDEX INDATASET(KSDS) OUTDATASET(AIX).
8. OPCIFIL SDSF: CEMT SET FIL(TRANSACT) OPE and FIL(CXACAIX) OPE.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TRANFILE] --> B[CLCIFIL SDSF CEMT close TRANSACT CXACAIX]
  B --> C[STEP05 DELETE KSDS and AIX]
  C --> D[STEP10 DEFINE CLUSTER key 16 rec 350]
  D --> E[STEP15 REPRO DALYTRAN.PS.INIT to KSDS]
  E --> F[STEP20 DEFINE AIX KEYS 26 304 NONUNIQUE UPGRADE]
  F --> G[STEP25 DEFINE PATH]
  G --> H[STEP30 BLDINDEX]
  H --> I[OPCIFIL SDSF CEMT open TRANSACT CXACAIX]
```

##### Data
Deletes/recreates TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS, .AIX, .AIX.PATH; loads from DALYTRAN.PS.INIT.

##### Outputs & side effects
Rebuilt transaction master with an alternate index on processing timestamp; CICS file state toggled.

##### External calls
SDSF (batch MVS console commands -> CICS CEMT), IDCAMS.

##### Migration notes
- No step has COND: every step runs even after failures (e.g. reopen happens after a failed load).
- SDSF RC does not reflect CEMT success; region name CICSAWSA is hardcoded.
- AIX is non-unique on TRAN-PROC-TS (byte offset 304, 0-based) with UPGRADE so writes maintain it.
- CICS file names TRANSACT/CXACAIX map to these datasets in the CSD (not in this batch).
recommendation: Fully documented.
note:
End-to-end: TRANFILE is submitted by remote_refresh.sh during the full master-data refresh. Upstream findings: sfind-89eccdc975c54f8c8f058e029a06ca5f.

title: READCUST / CBCUS01C - sequential dump of customer master to SYSOUT
description:
##### Entry point
Job `READCUST`, `STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C`.

##### Inputs
DD CUSTFILE -> `CUSTDATA.VSAM.KSDS`, 500-byte CVCUS01Y: CUST-ID 9(9) | FIRST/MIDDLE/LAST NAME X(25) each | ADDR-LINE-1..3 X(50) each | STATE X(2) | COUNTRY X(3) | ZIP X(10) | PHONE-1/2 X(15) | SSN 9(9) | GOVT-ID X(20) | DOB X(10) | EFT-ACCOUNT-ID X(10) | PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND X | FICO 9(3) | FILLER X(168).

##### Processing flow
Open, sequential read, DISPLAY CUSTOMER-RECORD twice per record, EOF '10', other status -> Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS + Z-ABEND-PROGRAM (CEE3ABD 999), close.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[READCUST CBCUS01C] --> B[OPEN CUSTFILE]
  B --> C{READ next}
  C -- 00 --> D[DISPLAY twice] --> C
  C -- 10 --> E[CLOSE GOBACK]
  C -- other --> F[Z-ABEND-PROGRAM]
```

##### Data
Read-only.

##### Outputs & side effects
SYSOUT listing including SSN and PII.

##### External calls
CEE3ABD.

##### Migration notes
Job card has `NOTIFY=&SYUID` (typo; not &SYSUID) - symbol is unresolved/ineffective. Paragraph names Z-* instead of 99xx. Otherwise same as CBACT03C.
recommendation: Fully documented.

         IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
         PROGRAM-ID.    CBCUS01C.
         AUTHOR.        AWS.
   
         ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
         INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
         FILE-CONTROL.
             SELECT CUSTFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO   CUSTFILE
                    ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED

        *
         DATA DIVISION.
         FILE SECTION.
         FD  CUSTFILE-FILE.
         01  FD-CUSTFILE-REC.
             05 FD-CUST-ID                        PIC 9(09).
             05 FD-CUST-DATA                      PIC X(491).
  
         WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
  
        *****************************************************************
         COPY CVCUS01Y.
         01  CUSTFILE-STATUS.
             05  CUSTFILE-STAT1      PIC X.
             05  CUSTFILE-STAT2      PIC X.
  
         01  IO-STATUS.
             05  IO-STAT1            PIC X.
             05  IO-STAT2            PIC X.
         01  TWO-BYTES-BINARY        PIC 9(4) BINARY.

             05  TWO-BYTES-LEFT      PIC X.
             05  TWO-BYTES-RIGHT     PIC X.
         01  IO-STATUS-04.
             05  IO-STATUS-0401      PIC 9   VALUE 0.
             05  IO-STATUS-0403      PIC 999 VALUE 0.
  
         01  APPL-RESULT             PIC S9(9)   COMP.
             88  APPL-AOK            VALUE 0.
             88  APPL-EOF            VALUE 16.
  
         01  END-OF-FILE             PIC X(01)    VALUE 'N'.
         01  ABCODE                  PIC S9(9) BINARY.
         01  TIMING                  PIC S9(9) BINARY. 
  
        *****************************************************************
         PROCEDURE DIVISION.
             DISPLAY 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C'.
             PERFORM 0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN.
  
             PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'
                 IF  END-OF-FILE = 'N'
                     PERFORM 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT
                     IF  END-OF-FILE = 'N'
                         DISPLAY CUSTOMER-RECORD 
                     END-IF
                 END-IF
             END-PERFORM.
  
             PERFORM 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE.
  
             DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBCUS01C'.
  
             GOBACK.

        *****************************************************************
         1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT.
             READ CUSTFILE-FILE INTO CUSTOMER-RECORD.
             IF  CUSTFILE-STATUS = '00'
                 MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT
                 DISPLAY CUSTOMER-RECORD 
             ELSE
                 IF  CUSTFILE-STATUS = '10'
                     MOVE 16 TO APPL-RESULT
                 ELSE
                     MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT
                 END-IF
             END-IF
             IF  APPL-AOK
                 CONTINUE
             ELSE
                 IF  APPL-EOF
                     MOVE 'Y' TO END-OF-FILE
                 ELSE
                     DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE'
                     MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS
                     PERFORM Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
                     PERFORM Z-ABEND-PROGRAM
                 END-IF
             END-IF
             EXIT.
        *---------------------------------------------------------------*
         0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN.
             MOVE 8 TO APPL-RESULT.
             OPEN INPUT CUSTFILE-FILE
             IF  CUSTFILE-STATUS = '00'
                 MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT
             ELSE
                 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT
             END-IF
             IF  APPL-AOK
                 CONTINUE
             ELSE
                 DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE'
                 MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS
                 PERFORM Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
                 PERFORM Z-ABEND-PROGRAM
             END-IF
             EXIT.
        *---------------------------------------------------------------*
         9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE.
             ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT.
             CLOSE CUSTFILE-FILE
             IF  CUSTFILE-STATUS = '00'
                 SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT
             ELSE
                 ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT
             END-IF
             IF  APPL-AOK
                 CONTINUE
             ELSE
                 DISPLAY 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE'
                 MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS
                 PERFORM Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
                 PERFORM Z-ABEND-PROGRAM
             END-IF
             EXIT.
  
         Z-ABEND-PROGRAM.
             DISPLAY 'ABENDING PROGRAM'
             MOVE 0 TO TIMING
             MOVE 999 TO ABCODE
             CALL 'CEE3ABD' USING ABCODE, TIMING.
  
        *****************************************************************
         Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS.
             IF  IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC
             OR  IO-STAT1 = '9'
                 MOVE IO-STAT1 TO IO-STATUS-04(1:1)
                 MOVE 0        TO TWO-BYTES-BINARY
                 MOVE IO-STAT2 TO TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
                 MOVE TWO-BYTES-BINARY TO IO-STATUS-0403
                 DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 
             ELSE
                 MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04
                 MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2)
                 DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 
             END-IF
             EXIT.

title: ESDSRRDS - load user security seed data into ESDS and RRDS variants
description:
##### Entry point
Job `ESDSRRDS` (demo/setup).

##### Inputs
Same 10 in-stream CSUSR01Y records as DUSRSECJ (passwords [REDACTED]).

##### Processing flow
1. PREDEL deletes `ESDSRRDS.PS`.
2. STEP01 IEBGENER in-stream -> `ESDSRRDS.PS` FB 80.
3. STEP02 DELETE USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS; SET MAXCC 0; DEFINE CLUSTER RECORDSIZE(80,80) REUSE NONINDEXED TRACKS(45,15) FREESPACE(10,15) CISZ(8192), DATA .DAT.
4. STEP03 REPRO ESDSRRDS.PS -> USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS (entry-sequenced, input order).
5. STEP04 DELETE USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS; SET MAXCC 0; DEFINE CLUSTER RECORDSIZE(80,80) REUSE NUMBERED ... DATA .DAT.
6. STEP05 REPRO ESDSRRDS.PS -> USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS (relative record numbers 1..10 in input order).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[ESDSRRDS] --> B[PREDEL] --> C[STEP01 IEBGENER to ESDSRRDS.PS]
  C --> D[STEP02 DEFINE ESDS] --> E[STEP03 REPRO to ESDS]
  E --> F[STEP04 DEFINE RRDS] --> G[STEP05 REPRO to RRDS]
```

##### Data
USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS, USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS, ESDSRRDS.PS. No consumer in this batch.

##### Outputs & side effects
Dataset creation only.

##### External calls
IEFBR14, IEBGENER, IDCAMS.

##### Migration notes
Diff vs DUSRSECJ: separate PS name, NONINDEXED/NUMBERED clusters, no key. Step comments are copy-pasted (STEP01 says user security PS; STEP05 comment says ESDS but loads RRDS). No COND.

title: PRTCATBL - unload TCATBALF KSDS to GDG backup and produce sorted, edited category-balance report file
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `PRTCATBL` (in CA-7 schedule). `//JOBLIB JCLLIB ORDER=('AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC')` resolves PROC REPROC.

##### Inputs
`AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.VSAM.KSDS` (CVTRA01Y 50-byte records).

##### Processing flow
1. DELDEF `EXEC PGM=IEFBR14`, THEFILE DD `TCATBALF.REPT` DISP=(MOD,DELETE) with UNIT/SPACE -> deletes prior report (allocates then deletes if absent).
2. STEP05R `PROC=REPROC,CNTLLIB=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL`: IDCAMS `REPRO INFILE(FILEIN) OUTFILE(FILEOUT)` from KSDS to `TCATBALF.BKUP(+1)` NEW,CATLG,DELETE FB LRECL 50.
3. STEP10R `PGM=SORT`: SORTIN = TCATBALF.BKUP(+1) (the generation just created). SYMNAMES: TRANCAT-ACCT-ID 1,11,ZD; TRANCAT-TYPE-CD 12,2,CH; TRANCAT-CD 14,4,ZD; TRAN-CAT-BAL 18,11,ZD. `SORT FIELDS=(ACCT-ID,A,TYPE-CD,A,CD,A)`; `OUTREC FIELDS=(ACCT-ID,X,TYPE-CD,X,CD,X,TRAN-CAT-BAL,EDIT=(TTTTTTTTT.TT),9X)`. SORTOUT = `TCATBALF.REPT` NEW,CATLG FB LRECL 40.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[PRTCATBL] --> B[DELDEF IEFBR14 delete TCATBALF.REPT]
  B --> C[STEP05R REPROC REPRO KSDS to TCATBALF.BKUP +1]
  C --> D[STEP10R SORT by acct,type,cat; OUTREC edit balance]
  D --> E[TCATBALF.REPT LRECL 40]
```

##### Data
Output record: acct(11) ' ' type(2) ' ' cat(4) ' ' balance edited 12 chars 'nnnnnnnnn.nn' + 9 blanks.

##### Outputs & side effects
New backup GDG generation + report dataset.

##### External calls
IDCAMS, DFSORT (PGM=SORT), IEFBR14.

##### Migration notes
- OUTREC builds 11+1+2+1+4+1+12+9 = 41 bytes but SORTOUT LRECL is 40; outcome (error vs truncation of the last blank) depends on DFSORT installation options - verify.
- EDIT mask has no sign position: negative balances print as positive.
- Comment says 'filter for parm date' but there is no INCLUDE; all records are output. Sort is effectively the KSDS key order.
- No COND on steps; TCATBALF.REPT is not a GDG (overwritten each run); GDG base TCATBALF.BKUP must pre-exist.
recommendation: Confirm the LRECL 40 vs 41-byte OUTREC behavior on the actual DFSORT configuration.
note:
End-to-end: PRTCATBL is the category-balance report job in the CA-7 network. Upstream findings: sfind-768eeaac8ac240da839e576915f7309d.

##### Inputs
- `STEP05R EXEC PROC=REPROC,CNTLLIB=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL`; overrides `PRC001.FILEIN` = `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS` (SHR).
- REPROC (app/proc/REPROC.prc): step PRC001 `EXEC PGM=IDCAMS`, FILEIN/FILEOUT default DSN=NULLFILE, SYSIN = `&CNTLLIB(REPROCT)`; member REPROCT contains `REPRO INFILE(FILEIN) OUTFILE(FILEOUT)`.

##### Processing flow
1. STEP05R (PRC001): IDCAMS REPRO of the whole TRANSACT KSDS (350-byte CVTRA05Y records in key order) to `PRC001.FILEOUT` = `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BKUP(+1)` NEW,CATLG,DELETE, RECFM=FB, LRECL=350, SPACE CYL(1,1).
2. STEP05 IDCAMS (no COND): `DELETE TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS CLUSTER`, `IF MAXCC LE 08 THEN SET MAXCC = 0`; `DELETE TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX ALTERNATEINDEX`, same reset (RC 8 = not found is tolerated).
3. STEP10 IDCAMS `COND=(4,LT)` (bypassed if any prior step RC > 4): DEFINE CLUSTER TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS CYLINDERS(1 5) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(350 350) SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) ERASE INDEXED, DATA .DATA, INDEX .INDEX.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TRANBKP] --> B[STEP05R REPROC PRC001 IDCAMS REPRO TRANSACT KSDS to TRANSACT.BKUP +1]
  B --> C[STEP05 IDCAMS DELETE cluster and AIX, MAXCC reset if <=8]
  C --> D{any prior RC > 4?}
  D -- no --> E[STEP10 DEFINE CLUSTER TRANSACT KSDS key 16 rec 350]
  D -- yes --> F[STEP10 bypassed]
```

##### Data
Read TRANSACT KSDS; write TRANSACT.BKUP(+1) GDG; delete and recreate TRANSACT KSDS (empty) and delete its AIX.

##### Outputs & side effects
A dated backup generation; empty transaction master ready for POSTTRAN; AIX/PATH (CXACAIX in CICS) no longer exists until TRANIDX/TRANFILE recreates it.

##### External calls
IDCAMS (REPRO, DELETE, DEFINE). No application programs.

##### Migration notes
- **STEP05 delete has no COND**: if the backup REPRO fails (RC 12), the KSDS is still deleted -> data loss; only STEP10 is protected by COND=(4,LT).
- The AIX is not redefined here (unlike TRANFILE), so online access via the AIX path fails until TRANIDX runs.
- Cluster is defined without REUSE; POSTTRAN opens it OUTPUT while empty.
- GDG base TRANSACT.BKUP must pre-exist (defined elsewhere).
- VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) and space are site-specific.
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm whether the unconditional delete after a failed backup should be guarded in the target pipeline.
note:
End-to-end: TRANBKP is submitted by run_posting.sh, run_interest_calc.sh, run_full_batch.sh and the Control-M DAILY-TransactionBackup folder; it backs up/empties TRANSACT before COMBTRAN/POSTTRAN reload it. title: INTRDRJ1 / INTRDRJ2 - copy FTP test file to backup, then submit INTRDRJ2 via internal reader
description:
##### Entry point
Job `INTRDRJ1` (demo of job chaining via internal reader).

##### Inputs
`AWS.M2.CARDEMO.FTP.TEST`; JCL member `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL(INTRDRJ2)`.

##### Processing flow
1. Step `IDCAMS EXEC PGM=IDCAMS,DYNAMNBR=200`: `REPRO IFILE(IN) OFILE(OUT)`, IN = FTP.TEST (SHR), OUT = FTP.TEST.BKUP (SHR, must pre-exist).
2. STEP01 IEBGENER: SYSUT1 = JCL(INTRDRJ2), SYSUT2 = `SYSOUT=(A,INTRDR)` LRECL/BLKSIZE 80 -> JES submits INTRDRJ2 as a new job.
3. INTRDRJ2 (see app/jcl/INTRDRJ2.JCL): IDCAMS REPRO FTP.TEST.BKUP -> FTP.TEST.BKUP.INTRDR.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[INTRDRJ1] --> B[IDCAMS REPRO FTP.TEST to FTP.TEST.BKUP]
  B --> C[STEP01 IEBGENER JCL INTRDRJ2 to INTRDR]
  C --> D[JES submits INTRDRJ2]
  D --> E[INTRDRJ2 IDCAMS REPRO BKUP to BKUP.INTRDR]
```

##### Data
Read FTP.TEST; write FTP.TEST.BKUP; (J2) write FTP.TEST.BKUP.INTRDR.

##### Outputs & side effects
Two copies of the FTP file and a new job submission.

##### External calls
IDCAMS, IEBGENER, JES internal reader.

##### Migration notes
No COND on STEP01: INTRDRJ2 is submitted even if the first REPRO fails. INTRDRJ2 runs asynchronously with no dependency tracking. Data DSNs use 'CARDEMO' while the JCL library uses 'CARDDEMO'. Related online pattern: CORPT00C SUBMIT-JOB-TO-INTRDR (outside batch).

title: READACCT / CBACT01C - dump account master and write fixed, array (COMP-3) and variable-length extract files
description:
##### Entry point
Job `READACCT`: PREDEL (IEFBR14) then `STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT01C`. CA-7 schedules READACCT, which triggers READCARD.

##### Inputs
DD ACCTFILE -> ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS (sequential read, CVACT01Y 300-byte layout).

##### Processing flow
1. PREDEL deletes ACCTDATA.PSCOMP, .ARRYPS, .VBPS (DISP=(MOD,DELETE,DELETE)).
2. CBACT01C opens ACCTFILE INPUT, OUTFILE/ARRYFILE/VBRCFILE OUTPUT (abend 999 on error).
3. Per record (1000-ACCTFILE-GET-NEXT, status '00'): INITIALIZE ARR-ARRAY-REC; 1100 DISPLAY each field; 1300-POPUL-ACCT-RECORD: copy fields to OUT-ACCT-REC; ACCT-REISSUE-DATE -> CODATECN-INP-DATE and WS-REISSUE-DATE, CODATECN-TYPE '2' (YYYY-MM-DD in), OUTTYPE '2' (YYYYMMDD out), `CALL 'COBDATFT' USING CODATECN-REC`, CODATECN-0UT-DATE -> OUT-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE; if ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT = 0 set OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT = 2525.00 (else NOT moved); 1350 WRITE (status other than '00'/'10' abends).
4. 1400 array: ARR-ACCT-ID; element(1) bal=ACCT-CURR-BAL, debit=1005.00; (2) bal=ACCT-CURR-BAL, debit=1525.00; (3) bal=-1025.00, debit=-2500.00; (4),(5) zero from INITIALIZE; 1450 WRITE.
5. 1500: VBRC-REC1 = ACCT-ID + ACTIVE-STATUS (12 bytes); VBRC-REC2 = ACCT-ID + CURR-BAL + CREDIT-LIMIT + reissue YYYY from WS-REISSUE-DATE (39 bytes); DISPLAY both; 1550 write 12-byte record, 1575 write 39-byte record (WS-RECD-LEN drives RECORD VARYING).
6. EOF ('10') ends loop; other status abends. Main loop also DISPLAYs ACCOUNT-RECORD. 9000 closes ACCTFILE only.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[READACCT PREDEL IEFBR14] --> B[STEP05 CBACT01C open files]
  B --> C{READ ACCTFILE}
  C -- 10 EOF --> Z[close ACCTFILE GOBACK]
  C -- 00 --> D[1100 DISPLAY fields]
  D --> E[1300 map + CALL COBDATFT reissue date; debit 0 -> 2525.00]
  E --> F[1350 WRITE OUTFILE]
  F --> G[1400/1450 array record WRITE ARRYFILE]
  G --> H[1500/1550/1575 two VB records WRITE VBRCFILE]
  H --> C
```

##### Data
- OUTFILE `ACCTDATA.PSCOMP` FB LRECL 107: OUT-ACCT-ID 9(11) | ACTIVE X | CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 | CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 | CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 | OPEN-DATE X(10) | EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) | REISSUE-DATE X(10) | CURR-CYC-CREDIT S9(10)V99 | CURR-CYC-DEBIT S9(10)V99 COMP-3 (7 bytes) | GROUP-ID X(10).
- ARRYFILE `ACCTDATA.ARRYPS` FB LRECL 110: ARR-ACCT-ID 9(11) + 5 x (CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 zoned + CYC-DEBIT S9(10)V99 COMP-3) + FILLER X(4).
- VBRCFILE `ACCTDATA.VBPS` RECFM=VB LRECL 84 (80 data + RDW).

##### Outputs & side effects
Three extract files; SYSOUT dump of every account (twice: field-by-field and whole record).

##### External calls
- `COBDATFT` (assembler, app/asm/COBDATFT.asm, 84 lines) passed CODATECN-REC (type X, input X(20), outtype X, output X(20)); returns converted date. Only skimmed: it tests input type '1'/'2', checks '-' at position 5, and branches on output type; exact error handling not traced (medium confidence).
- `CEE3ABD` abend 999.

##### Migration notes
- **OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT is only set when the source is zero (to 2525.00)**; otherwise it retains whatever is in the FD buffer (previous record/undefined). Test-data generator behavior, not a faithful copy.
- Array values are hardcoded test constants.
- WS-REISSUE-DATE is set in 1300 and reused in 1500 (order-dependent).
- Output files are never explicitly closed (implicit close at run end). Write status '10' accepted as success.
- UNIT=SYSAD is a site esoteric.
recommendation: COBDATFT assembler conversion not fully traced; confirm its output for invalid dates. Confirm whether the unset CYC-DEBIT behavior must be reproduced.
note: Duplicate of sfind-a67fbe5a171a4912927b7bc4e1a093b0 (CBACT01C account extract to PS/array/VB files (READACCT)); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: DISCGRP - (re)load disclosure group (interest rate) KSDS from flat file
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `DISCGRP`. Control-M folder `WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh`: MNTTRDB2 -> CLOSEFIL -> DISCGRP -> WAITSTEP -> OPENFIL.

##### Inputs
`AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS` (DD DISCGRP, SHR), 50-byte records, layout CVTRA02Y: DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) | DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD X(2) | DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD 9(4) | DIS-INT-RATE S9(4)V99 zoned | FILLER X(28). Must be sorted ascending by the 16-byte key with no duplicates.

##### Processing flow
1. STEP05 IDCAMS: DELETE DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS CLUSTER; `SET MAXCC = 0` (always clears errors).
2. STEP10 IDCAMS: DEFINE CLUSTER DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS CYLINDERS(1 5) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(50 50) SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) ERASE INDEXED; DATA .DATA, INDEX .INDEX.
3. STEP15 IDCAMS: REPRO INFILE(DISCGRP) OUTFILE(DISCVSAM), DISCVSAM DD = KSDS DISP=OLD.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[DISCGRP] --> B[STEP05 DELETE KSDS, SET MAXCC 0]
  B --> C[STEP10 DEFINE KSDS key 16 rec 50]
  C --> D[STEP15 REPRO DISCGRP.PS to KSDS]
```

##### Data
Writes `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS`, read by CBACT04C (INTCALC) via DD DISCGRP; the record keyed group 'DEFAULT' is required there as fallback.

##### Outputs & side effects
Full replace of rate table.

##### External calls
IDCAMS.

##### Migration notes
No COND on steps; a failed DEFINE still lets REPRO run (and fail). Rate S9(4)V99 is zoned with sign overpunch in the last byte. Shared pattern with TCATBALF.jcl and TRANCATG.jcl (differences: keys/record sizes/DSNs only).
recommendation: Fully documented. Ensure a 'DEFAULT' group row is migrated since INTCALC abends without it.
note:
End-to-end: DISCGRP is submitted by remote_refresh.sh/run_full_batch.sh and the Control-M WEEKLY DisclosureGroupsRefresh folder; feeds CBACT04C (INTCALC) interest rates. title: POSTTRAN / CBTRN02C - daily transaction validation and posting (TCATBAL, account, transaction master)
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `POSTTRAN`, step `STEP15 EXEC PGM=CBTRN02C` (STEPLIB AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB), no PARM. Listed in the CA-7 schedule (app/scheduler/CardDemo.ca7, triggered job POSTTRAN, SCHID 030).

##### Inputs
- DD `DALYTRAN` -> `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS` (sequential, 350-byte). Layout CVTRA06Y: DALYTRAN-ID X(16) | TYPE-CD X(2) | CAT-CD 9(4) | SOURCE X(10) | DESC X(100) | AMT S9(9)V99 | MERCHANT-ID 9(9) | MERCHANT-NAME X(50) | MERCHANT-CITY X(50) | MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) | CARD-NUM X(16) | ORIG-TS X(26) | PROC-TS X(26) | FILLER X(20).
- DD `XREFFILE` -> `CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS` (random by card number; CVACT03Y layout: card X(16), cust 9(9), acct 9(11), filler X(14)).
- DD `ACCTFILE` -> `ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS` (random, I-O; CVACT01Y 300-byte layout).
- DD `TCATBALF` -> `TCATBALF.VSAM.KSDS` (random, I-O; CVTRA01Y: acct 9(11), type X(2), cat 9(4), bal S9(9)V99, filler X(22)).

##### Processing flow
1. Open DALYTRAN INPUT, TRANFILE OUTPUT, XREFFILE INPUT, DALYREJS OUTPUT, ACCTFILE I-O, TCATBALF I-O; any non-'00' -> abend 999.
2. Loop until EOF: read DALYTRAN (status '10' = EOF; other errors abend). Count WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT; reset WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON=0, DESC=spaces.
3. 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN:
   - 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF: READ XREF by DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM; INVALID KEY -> reason 100 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND'.
   - Only if reason=0, 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT: READ ACCOUNT by XREF-ACCT-ID; INVALID KEY -> 101 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND'. Otherwise WS-TEMP-BAL = ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT - ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT + DALYTRAN-AMT; if ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT < WS-TEMP-BAL -> 102 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION'. Then independently if ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE < DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS(1:10) (string compare of YYYY-MM-DD) -> 103 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION' (overwrites 102).
4. Reason <> 0: WS-REJECT-COUNT+1; 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC writes DALYTRAN record (350) + trailer (reason 9(4) + desc X(76)) to DALYREJS; write error -> abend.
5. Reason = 0: 2000-POST-TRANSACTION copies all DALYTRAN fields to TRAN-RECORD, TRAN-PROC-TS = current timestamp 'YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000', then in order:
   - 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL: key XREF-ACCT-ID + DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD + DALYTRAN-CAT-CD; READ; '23' -> 2700-A-CREATE (INITIALIZE, set key, bal = amt, WRITE); '00' -> 2700-B-UPDATE (bal += amt, REWRITE); other status or write/rewrite error -> abend.
   - 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC: ACCT-CURR-BAL += amt; if amt >= 0 ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT += amt else ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT += amt (adds negative). REWRITE; INVALID KEY sets reason 109 but nothing acts on it.
   - 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE: WRITE TRANFILE keyed by TRAN-ID; non-'00' (e.g. duplicate '22') -> abend.
6. Close all files; DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED' and 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED'; if rejects > 0, RETURN-CODE = 4.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[POSTTRAN STEP15 CBTRN02C] --> B[Open DALYTRAN TRANFILE-OUT XREFFILE DALYREJS-OUT ACCTFILE-IO TCATBALF-IO]
  B --> C{1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT EOF?}
  C -- yes --> R[Close; display counts; RC=4 if rejects]
  C -- no --> D[1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF by card]
  D -- not found --> X[reason 100]
  D -- found --> E[1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT]
  E -- not found --> X1[reason 101]
  E -- found --> F{limit >= cyc credit - cyc debit + amt?}
  F -- no --> X2[reason 102]
  F --> G{expiry >= orig-ts date?}
  X2 --> G
  G -- no --> X3[reason 103]
  G -- yes and no reason --> P[2000-POST-TRANSACTION]
  X --> RJ[2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC DALYREJS]
  X1 --> RJ
  X3 --> RJ
  G -- yes but reason 102 --> RJ
  P --> T[2700 TCATBAL create/update]
  T --> U[2800 account bal + cycle credit/debit REWRITE]
  U --> W[2900 WRITE TRANSACT KSDS]
  W --> C
  RJ --> C
```

##### Data
- Read: DALYTRAN.PS, CARDXREF KSDS.
- Updated/created: TCATBALF KSDS (WRITE/REWRITE), ACCTDATA KSDS (REWRITE).
- Written: DD `TRANFILE` -> `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS` (opened OUTPUT, random WRITE by FD-TRANS-ID, 350-byte CVTRA05Y records = DALYTRAN fields + new PROC-TS); DD `DALYREJS` -> `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYREJS(+1)` new GDG, RECFM=F, LRECL=430 (350 reject data + 80 trailer: WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON 9(4), DESC X(76)).

##### Outputs & side effects
Posted transaction master records, updated balances, reject file, SYSOUT counts, job RC 0/4, abend U999 on I/O errors (no rollback of earlier updates).

##### External calls
`CEE3ABD` with ABCODE 999 / TIMING 0 on fatal errors. No other calls.

##### Migration notes
- Validation order matters: 103 overwrites 102; 101/100 short-circuit.
- Over-limit check uses only current-cycle credit/debit, not ACCT-CURR-BAL; debits are stored as negative amounts so `credit - debit` adds their magnitude.
- Expiry check is a lexical compare of X(10) dates.
- Reason 109 on account REWRITE failure is dead: the transaction is still written and not counted as rejected.
- Update order TCATBAL -> account -> transaction; an abend on transaction write leaves the first two updates applied.
- TRANFILE is opened OUTPUT on a KSDS; this requires the cluster to be empty (or REUSE) - in practice TRANBKP/TRANFILE redefine it beforehand. Behavior on a loaded non-REUSE cluster is environment-dependent; verify on target.
- Any duplicate TRAN-ID in DALYTRAN abends the job.
- DALYTRAN PROC-TS from input is discarded and replaced.
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm the intended precedence of rejection codes 102/103 and whether reason 109 should reject.

title: FTPJCL - FTP PUT of mainframe dataset to remote server
description:
##### Entry point
Job `FTPJCLS` (member FTPJCL), `STEP1 EXEC PGM=FTP,REGION=2048K`; job TIME=1440 (no CPU limit). A PARM with a different IP and EXIT TIMEOUT is commented out.

##### Inputs
SYSIN in-stream FTP script: server 172.31.21.124; user [REDACTED]; password [REDACTED]; `ASCII`; `pwd`; `dir`; `cd /ftpfolder`; `PUT 'AWS.M2.CARDEMO.FTP.TEST' welcome.txt`; `QUIT`.

##### Processing flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[FTPJCLS STEP1 PGM=FTP] --> B[connect 172.31.21.124, login]
  B --> C[ASCII mode, pwd, dir, cd /ftpfolder]
  C --> D[PUT AWS.M2.CARDEMO.FTP.TEST as welcome.txt]
  D --> E[QUIT]
```

##### Data
Reads `AWS.M2.CARDEMO.FTP.TEST` (note CARDEMO, single D).

##### Outputs & side effects
Remote file /ftpfolder/welcome.txt (EBCDIC->ASCII conversion by FTP client).

##### External calls
z/OS FTP client to external server.

##### Migration notes
Credentials hardcoded in JCL - must be externalized. Without EXIT parm, FTP command failures may not set a failing step RC. Comments say 'receive' but script sends (PUT).
recommendation: Fully documented; rotate/externalize embedded FTP credentials.

description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `TXT2PDF1` (accounting (T,TEST), MSGCLASS=X, CLASS=A). In CA-7 it is triggered by CREASTMT (SCHID 030) and triggers WAITSTEP → OPENFIL. Single step `TXT2PDF EXEC PGM=IKJEFT1B,DYNAMNBR=50,PARM=(''),COND=(0,NE)` (batch TMP / TSO).

##### Inputs
- `STEPLIB DD DISP=SHR,DSN=AWS.M2.LBD.TXT2PDF.LOAD` (external load library).
- `SYSEXEC DD DISP=SHR,DSN=AWS.M2.LBD.TXT2PDF.EXEC` (external REXX library).
- `INDD DD DISP=SHR,DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS` — account statement text produced by CREASTMT (CBSTM03A; FB LRECL 80, BLKSIZE 8000).

##### Processing flow
TMP executes REXX exec TXT2PDF with keywords BROWSE Y, IN DD:INDD, OUT 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS.PDF'. What TXT2PDF does internally is not in the repo (unresolved). COND=(0,NE) on the first and only step has no prior step RC to test, so it never bypasses the step.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TXT2PDF1 JOB] --> B[TXT2PDF EXEC PGM=IKJEFT1B]
  B --> C[SYSTSIN: %TXT2PDF BROWSE Y IN DD:INDD OUT STATEMNT.PS.PDF]
  C --> D[(external REXX AWS.M2.LBD.TXT2PDF.EXEC - not in repo)]
  D --> E[AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS.PDF]
```

##### Data
Read STATEMNT.PS; write dataset AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS.PDF, allocated dynamically by the exec (no DD; DYNAMNBR=50 permits dynamic allocation). Layout/DCB of the PDF dataset unknown.

##### Outputs & side effects
PDF dataset; SYSTSPRT/SYSPRINT messages.

##### External calls
IKJEFT1B (TSO TMP) → REXX TXT2PDF (third-party/external, unresolved).

##### Migration notes
- Depends on non-CardDemo libraries under HLQ AWS.M2.LBD; replace with a modern text-to-PDF step.
- IKJEFT1B (vs IKJEFT01) propagates the exec's return code / abends to the step.
- Behavior if STATEMNT.PS.PDF already exists is unknown (exec-controlled).
recommendation: The TXT2PDF REXX exec and load modules (AWS.M2.LBD.TXT2PDF.EXEC / .LOAD) are not in the repository; conversion behavior, output DCB and handling of an existing output dataset cannot be documented. Customer must supply the TXT2PDF package/version and its options.

title: TRANTYPE job: delete/define TRANTYPE KSDS and load it from TRANTYPE.PS
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `TRANTYPE` ('DEFINE TRAN TYPE', CLASS=A, MSGCLASS=0). Scheduled in CA-7 (triggered by CLOSEFIL SCHID 030, triggers WAITSTEP), listed in README setup and 'Running Batch Jobs' sequences, and uploaded by scripts/run_full_batch.sh and scripts/remote_refresh.sh.

##### Inputs
- STEP15 `TRANTYPE DD DISP=SHR,DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.PS` — sequential FB 60 (copybook CVTRA03Y: TRAN-TYPE X(2), TRAN-TYPE-DESC X(50), FILLER X(8)). Sample data app/data/ASCII/trantype.txt, e.g. `01Purchase`, `02Payment`, `03Credit`, `04Authorization`, `05Refund`, … (filler shows '00000000' in samples).

##### Processing flow
1. STEP05 IDCAMS: `DELETE AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS CLUSTER` then `SET MAXCC = 0` (unconditional — any delete failure, including not-found, is masked).
2. STEP10 IDCAMS: `DEFINE CLUSTER (NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS) CYLINDERS(1 5) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) KEYS(2 0) RECORDSIZE(60 60) SHAREOPTIONS(1 4) ERASE INDEXED) DATA(NAME(...KSDS.DATA)) INDEX(NAME(...KSDS.INDEX))`.
3. STEP15 IDCAMS: `REPRO INFILE(TRANTYPE) OUTFILE(TTYPVSAM)`; TTYPVSAM DD DISP=OLD (exclusive).
No COND parameters: STEP15 runs even if STEP10 failed.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TRANTYPE JOB] --> B[STEP05 IDCAMS DELETE TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS; SET MAXCC=0]
  B --> C[STEP10 IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER KEYS 2 0 RECSZ 60]
  C --> D[STEP15 IDCAMS REPRO TRANTYPE.PS -> TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS]
```

##### Data
Read TRANTYPE.PS (60-byte). Written/recreated KSDS TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS: key = bytes 1-2 (TRAN-TYPE), fixed 60-byte records, SHAREOPTIONS(1 4) (cross-region: one writer or many readers), ERASE (data overwritten on delete). Consumers include CBTRN03C (TRANTYPE DD) and CICS file definitions.

##### Outputs & side effects
Destroys and rebuilds the transaction type reference file. Must run while CICS has the file closed (CA-7 places it after CLOSEFIL).

##### External calls
IDCAMS (3 invocations).

##### Migration notes
- REPRO into a KSDS requires input sorted ascending by key with no duplicates; otherwise IDCAMS reports errors (RC 8/12) — the PS file must be in type-code order.
- Delete failure masked by unconditional SET MAXCC=0 (contrast XREFFILE, which masks only MAXCC ≤ 8).
- Hard-coded volume AWSHJ1 and space CYL(1 5).
recommendation: Fully documented.
note:
End-to-end: TRANTYPE is submitted by remote_refresh.sh, run_full_batch.sh and the CA-7 reference-refresh chain. Upstream findings: sfind-89eccdc975c54f8c8f058e029a06ca5f, sfind-574c7fefe140460688d7131108eb4d55, sfind-768eeaac8ac240da839e576915f7309d.

title: WAITSTEP job: COBSWAIT -> MVSWAIT -> ASMWAIT STIMER delay (centiseconds from SYSIN)
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `WAITSTEP` (CLASS=A, MSGCLASS=0). Used as a pacing job between file close/open jobs: CA-7 triggers it after POSTTRAN, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, TCATBALF, READXREF, TXT2PDF1, PRTCATBL (it then triggers OPENFIL/CLOSEFIL); Control-M runs it in DAILY-TransactionBackup (after TRANBKP), WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh (after DISCGRP) and MONTHLY-InterestCalculation (after COMBTRAN), each followed by OPENFIL. Single step `WAIT EXEC PGM=COBSWAIT`, STEPLIB AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB.

##### Inputs
`SYSIN DD *` line: `00003600      VALUE IN CENTISECONDS` — COBSWAIT ACCEPTs the first 8 bytes into PARM-VALUE PIC X(8) ('00003600').

##### Processing flow
1. COBSWAIT: `ACCEPT PARM-VALUE FROM SYSIN`; `MOVE PARM-VALUE TO MVSWAIT-TIME` (PIC 9(8) COMP — alphanumeric → binary numeric conversion); `CALL 'MVSWAIT' USING MVSWAIT-TIME` (by reference); `STOP RUN`.
2. MVSWAIT (app/asm/MVSWAIT.asm, `MVSWAIT START 0`, base R15): STM 14,12,12(13); L 5,0(1) (address of first parm); L 1,0(5) (fullword delay); ST 1,BINLBL; `ASMWAIT BINLBL`; LM 14,12,12(13); MVI 12(13),X'FF' (marks caller save area); SR 15,15 (RC 0); BR 14.
3. Macro ASMWAIT (app/maclib/ASMWAIT.mac): `&NAME ASMWAIT &B` expands to `STIMER WAIT,BINTVL=&B` — task waits for the binary interval in units of 0.01 s.
Default 3600 centiseconds = 36 seconds.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[WAITSTEP JOB] --> B[WAIT EXEC PGM=COBSWAIT]
  B --> C[ACCEPT PARM-VALUE X8 FROM SYSIN]
  C --> D[MOVE to MVSWAIT-TIME 9 8 COMP]
  D --> E[CALL MVSWAIT USING MVSWAIT-TIME]
  E --> F[ASMWAIT macro: STIMER WAIT,BINTVL=BINLBL]
  F --> G[RC 0, STOP RUN]
```

##### Data
No files other than SYSIN; SYSOUT allocated but nothing written by the code.

##### Outputs & side effects
Elapsed-time delay only; step RC 0.

##### External calls
MVSWAIT (assembler, parameter: one fullword binary centiseconds passed by reference); STIMER SVC via ASMWAIT macro.

##### Migration notes
- Unit is centiseconds (1/100 s); a re-implementation as sleep must divide by 100.
- No validation: non-numeric SYSIN content is moved into a COMP field (results compiler-dependent, typically garbage or 0); PIC 9(8) COMP holds up to 99,999,999 cs (~11.6 days).
- The wait exists to give CICS time after CEMT open/close commands (inferred from scheduler placement only).
- MVI 12(13),X'FF' sets the high byte of the caller's save-area return address word — conventional 'returned' flag; harmless but present.
- MVSWAIT saves registers into the caller's save area but does not chain its own save area (leaf routine).
recommendation: Fully documented. Note that the SYSIN value is moved alphanumeric-to-COMP without validation.
note:
Consolidated document for app/asm/MVSWAIT.asm, app/cbl/COBSWAIT.cbl, app/jcl/WAITSTEP.jcl, app/maclib/ASMWAIT.mac; merged duplicates: sfind-758d4fe75f8040bba19f611a2423e3e4, sfind-3703d3bad60b4b6d93f691f373effed2, sfind-10d1287a3fca445c93d1678862f81028.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- MVSWAIT does `MVI 12(13),X'FF'` on the caller save area before returning (flag marking save area; author comment questions its purpose).
- A value of 12000 means 120 s, because the unit is 1/100 s.
- MVSWAIT uses R15 as its base register without establishing a new save area, which is unusual.

End-to-end: WAITSTEP (COBSWAIT -> MVSWAIT -> ASMWAIT) is used as a timed delay step in the Control-M and CA-7 networks. Upstream findings: sfind-c0001c8086c54798b228ce1ea65e05ab, sfind-768eeaac8ac240da839e576915f7309d.

title: Control-M folders for CardDemo: daily transaction backup, weekly DB2 refresh/disclosure groups, monthly interest
description:
##### Entry point
Control-M DEFTABLE export (app/scheduler/CardDemo.controlm), APPLICATION=CARD-DEMO. Jobs are OS jobs (APPL_TYPE OS, USE_INSTREAM_JCL=N), MEMNAME = JCL member = JOBNAME, MAXWAIT=7, MAXRERUN=5 (regular folders), TIMETO=23:00.

##### Inputs
Folders/jobs and IN/OUT conditions (ODATE=ODAT; '+' add, '-' delete):
1. **DAILY-TransactionBackup** (regular folder, DAYS=ALL, all months):
   - CLOSEFIL: OUT +DAILY-TransactionBackup-CLOSEFIL
   - TRANBKP: IN CLOSEFIL cond; OUT -CLOSEFIL, +TRANBKP
   - WAITSTEP: IN TRANBKP; OUT -TRANBKP, +WAITSTEP
   - OPENFIL: IN WAITSTEP; OUT -WAITSTEP
2. **WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh** (regular folder): MNTTRDB2 — no DAYS attribute; OUT +WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2.
3. **WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh** (SMART folder, DAYS=SA, PRIORITY AA, PARENT_FOLDER WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh, DATACENTER PROD, PLATFORM UNIX):
   - CLOSEFIL: IN MNTTRDB2 cond; OUT +CLOSEFIL
   - DISCGRP: IN CLOSEFIL; OUT -CLOSEFIL, +DISCGRP
   - WAITSTEP: IN DISCGRP; OUT -DISCGRP, +WAITSTEP
   - OPENFIL: IN WAITSTEP; OUT -WAITSTEP
   - Folder OUT: -WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2
4. **SMART folder FOLDER_NAME=WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh** (JOBNAME TransactionTypesDBRefresh, DAYS=SA): TRANEXTR — IN MNTTRDB2 cond; folder OUT -MNTTRDB2.
5. **MONTHLY-InterestCalculation** (regular folder, no DAYS attribute on jobs): CLOSEFIL (+CLOSEFIL) → INTCALC (IN CLOSEFIL; -CLOSEFIL, +INTCALC) → COMBTRAN (IN INTCALC; -INTCALC, +COMBTRAN) → WAITSTEP (IN COMBTRAN; -COMBTRAN, +WAITSTEP) → OPENFIL (IN WAITSTEP; -WAITSTEP).

##### Processing flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph DAILY-TransactionBackup
    D1[CLOSEFIL] --> D2[TRANBKP] --> D3[WAITSTEP] --> D4[OPENFIL]
  end
  subgraph WEEKLY
    M[MNTTRDB2] -->|cond MNTTRDB2| S1[CLOSEFIL] --> S2[DISCGRP] --> S3[WAITSTEP] --> S4[OPENFIL]
    M -->|cond MNTTRDB2| T1[TRANEXTR]
  end
  subgraph MONTHLY-InterestCalculation
    I1[CLOSEFIL] --> I2[INTCALC] --> I3[COMBTRAN] --> I4[WAITSTEP] --> I5[OPENFIL]
  end
```
Each successor deletes its predecessor's condition after running, so a chain cannot be re-triggered for the same ODATE without re-adding conditions.

##### Data
None in scheduler; per-job data flows documented in respective JCL.

##### Outputs & side effects
Job ordering only; conditions added/removed in the Control-M condition table.

##### External calls
Submits JCL members CLOSEFIL, TRANBKP, WAITSTEP, OPENFIL, MNTTRDB2, DISCGRP, TRANEXTR, INTCALC, COMBTRAN.

##### Migration notes
- Folder name collision: regular folder and SMART folder both named WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh.
- Both weekly SMART folders wait on and then delete the same MNTTRDB2 condition; whichever completes first removes it — if the other has not yet started its first job, it will not run (race).
- MNTTRDB2 and the MONTHLY jobs have no DAYS/MONTHDAYS in this export, so their run calendar is undefined here (the 'MONTHLY' cadence is only in the folder name).
- Control-M and CA-7 definitions are not consistent with each other (e.g. TRANBKP/INTCALC/COMBTRAN only in Control-M; POSTTRAN/TRANTYPE/CREASTMT only in CA-7) — they are alternative samples, not one combined schedule.
- RUN_AS xuemingh; MAXRERUN=5 permits automatic reruns in regular folders; SMART folders have MAXRERUN=0.
recommendation: Fully documented from the XML. Customer should confirm intended schedule for MNTTRDB2 and the MONTHLY-InterestCalculation jobs, which carry no DAYS/MONTHDAYS attribute in this export, and the duplicate folder name WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh.

title: REPROC cataloged PROC: generic IDCAMS REPRO copy FILEIN -> FILEOUT
description:
##### Entry point
Cataloged PROC `REPROC` (app/proc/REPROC.prc), invoked as `EXEC PROC=REPROC,CNTLLIB=<pds>` by TRANREPT.jcl STEP05R and TRANREPT.prc STEP01R (and other jobs in the repo outside this batch). Single step `PRC001 EXEC PGM=IDCAMS`.

##### Inputs
- Symbolic parameter `&CNTLLIB` (no default; callers pass AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL).
- `FILEIN DD DISP=SHR,DSN=NULLFILE` and `FILEOUT DD DISP=SHR,DSN=NULLFILE` — dummy placeholders that callers must override as `PRC001.FILEIN` / `PRC001.FILEOUT`.
- `SYSIN DD DISP=SHR,DSN=&CNTLLIB(REPROCT)`; member REPROCT (app/ctl/REPROCT.ctl) contains only `REPRO INFILE(FILEIN) OUTFILE(FILEOUT)`.

##### Processing flow
IDCAMS reads every record of FILEIN in its native order and writes it to FILEOUT (load or unload of VSAM / sequential). No record selection, no REPLACE/REUSE options.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[Caller EXEC PROC=REPROC,CNTLLIB=...] --> P[PRC001 IDCAMS]
  P --> S[SYSIN &CNTLLIB REPROCT: REPRO INFILE FILEIN OUTFILE FILEOUT]
  S --> O[FILEOUT = caller override]
```

##### Data
Whatever the caller overrides: for TRANREPT, TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS (350-byte) → TRANSACT.BKUP(+1).

##### Outputs & side effects
FILEOUT populated; IDCAMS messages to SYSPRINT. RC from IDCAMS (0 ok, 12 typical failure).

##### External calls
IDCAMS only.

##### Migration notes
- If a caller forgets an override, NULLFILE (DUMMY) is used: input yields zero records and REPRO into NULLFILE discards data, with no failure.
- Behavior depends on an external control-card member REPROCT; app/app-transaction-type-db2/ctl/REPROCT.ctl is another copy of the same name in the optional DB2 module.
recommendation: Fully documented.
note: Owners from git history (no CODEOWNERS file in repo).

title: TRANREPT cataloged PROC: CICS-submitted variant of the transaction report (via CORPT00C internal reader)
description:
##### Entry point
Cataloged procedure member `TRANREPT` in AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC (app/proc/TRANREPT.prc). Its PROC statement is labeled `//REPROC PROC` (not TRANREPT) and it ends with `// PEND`. It is invoked by job `TRNRPT00`, which CICS program CORPT00C (transaction report screen) builds in working storage (JOB-DATA) and writes line-by-line (80-byte records) to extrapartition TD queue `JOBS` (internal reader) until a line equal to '/*EOF' or spaces/low-values:
```
//TRNRPT00 JOB 'TRAN REPORT',CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=0,
// NOTIFY=&SYSUID
//JOBLIB JCLLIB ORDER=('AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC')
//STEP10 EXEC PROC=TRANREPT
//STEP05R.SYMNAMES DD *
TRAN-CARD-NUM,263,16,ZD
TRAN-PROC-DT,305,10,CH
PARM-START-DATE,C'<start>'
PARM-END-DATE,C'<end>'
/*
//STEP10R.DATEPARM DD *
<start> <end>
/*
```
(start/end are the 10-char dates CORPT00C computed — PARM-START-DATE-1/2, PARM-END-DATE-1/2 get the same values.)

##### Inputs
Same DD/dataset set as app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl: STEP01R (nested PROC REPROC, CNTLLIB=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL) PRC001.FILEIN=TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS, PRC001.FILEOUT=TRANSACT.BKUP(+1) (FB 350); STEP05R SORT SORTIN=TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), default SYMNAMES dates 2022-01-01/2022-07-06 (overridden by caller), SORTOUT=TRANSACT.DALY(+1); STEP10R CBTRN03C TRANFILE=TRANSACT.DALY(+1), CARDXREF, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG KSDSs, DATEPARM=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DATEPARM (overridden by caller with instream `YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD`), TRANREPT=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANREPT(+1) FB 133. Record layouts: see TRANREPT.jcl finding (CVTRA05Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA03Y, CVTRA04Y, CVTRA07Y).

##### Processing flow
Identical three-step pipeline to TRANREPT.jcl (diffed: only differences are step 1 named STEP01R instead of STEP05R, and `// PEND` instead of null `//` terminator). Because the caller overrides both SYMNAMES and DATEPARM with the same dates, the SORT INCLUDE range and CBTRN03C's DATEPARM range agree in this path, so the NEXT SENTENCE early-exit in CBTRN03C is not triggered by range mismatch here.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  U[CICS CORPT00C report screen] -->|WRITEQ TD QUEUE JOBS, 80-byte JCL lines| R[Internal reader: job TRNRPT00]
  R --> P[STEP10 EXEC PROC=TRANREPT]
  P --> S1[STEP01R PROC=REPROC IDCAMS REPRO TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS -> TRANSACT.BKUP+1]
  S1 --> S2[STEP05R SORT, SYMNAMES overridden with user dates -> TRANSACT.DALY+1]
  S2 --> S3[STEP10R CBTRN03C, DATEPARM overridden instream]
  S3 --> O[AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANREPT +1 report]
```

##### Data
As TRANREPT.jcl: reads TRANSACT KSDS, CARDXREF/TRANTYPE/TRANCATG KSDS; writes new generations of TRANSACT.BKUP, TRANSACT.DALY, TRANREPT (GDG LIMIT 5 SCRATCH, DEFGDGB.jcl).

##### Outputs & side effects
Report generation TRANREPT(+1); two intermediate GDG generations; SYSOUT displays from CBTRN03C. Job runs asynchronously from the CICS user; CORPT00C gets no completion feedback.

##### External calls
Nested PROC REPROC (IDCAMS with REPROCT control card), SORT, CBTRN03C (CEE3ABD on error).

##### Migration notes
- PROC label `REPROC` equals the name of the nested PROC it calls; resolution works by member name (TRANREPT) but a re-implementation must not rely on the label.
- Override step names `STEP05R.SYMNAMES` and `STEP10R.DATEPARM` from CORPT00C are a contract with this PROC; renaming steps breaks the CICS report submission.
- Concurrent submissions each create +1 generations of the same GDGs; with LIMIT(5) a burst of submissions rolls off earlier reports.
- All CBTRN03C quirks (double-counted final amount, missing last account total, page-break rule) apply — see TRANREPT.jcl finding.
recommendation: Fully traced; behavior of CBTRN03C is documented in the TRANREPT.jcl finding. Confirm with the customer whether the PROC statement label REPROC (instead of TRANREPT) is intentional.
note:
End-to-end: TRANREPT PROC is invoked by the JCL CORPT00C builds (//STEP10 EXEC PROC=TRANREPT) and writes to TDQ JOBS (internal reader); runs CBTRN03C, the same report documented for batch TRANREPT. Upstream findings: sfind-47410982987d4cc78d6efd7d871e30aa.

title: TRANREPT batch job: unload TRANSACT KSDS, date-filter/sort, CBTRN03C daily transaction report
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `TRANREPT` (app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl), job card `//TRANREPT JOB 'TRANSACTION REPORT',CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=0,NOTIFY=&SYSUID`. Manually submitted (it is not in the CA-7 or Control-M definitions; README lists TRANREPT as 'Transaction Report - Submitted from CICS', which is actually done via the PROC variant app/proc/TRANREPT.prc from CICS program CORPT00C — see that finding). `//JOBLIB JCLLIB ORDER=('AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC')` makes the cataloged PROC library searchable for `REPROC`.

Steps in order (no COND parameters on any step, so each step runs regardless of prior return codes unless a JCL/allocation error ends the job):
1. `STEP05R EXEC PROC=REPROC,CNTLLIB=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL` — IDCAMS REPRO unload.
2. `STEP05R EXEC PGM=SORT` — (duplicate step name) filter + sort.
3. `STEP10R EXEC PGM=CBTRN03C` (STEPLIB AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB) — report writer.

##### Inputs
| Step | DD | DSN | DISP | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|STEP05R(PROC)|PRC001.FILEIN|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS|SHR|override of REPROC FILEIN; transaction master KSDS, 350-byte records|
|STEP05R(PROC)|SYSIN (in proc)|&CNTLLIB(REPROCT) = AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL(REPROCT)|SHR|contains `REPRO INFILE(FILEIN) OUTFILE(FILEOUT)` (app/ctl/REPROCT.ctl)|
|STEP05R(SORT)|SORTIN|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BKUP(+1)|SHR|generation created by step 1|
|STEP05R(SORT)|SYMNAMES|instream|—|`TRAN-CARD-NUM,263,16,ZD`; `TRAN-PROC-DT,305,10,CH`; `PARM-START-DATE,C'2022-01-01'`; `PARM-END-DATE,C'2022-07-06'`|
|STEP10R|TRANFILE|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.DALY(+1)|SHR|sequential, read by CBTRN03C TRANSACT-FILE|
|STEP10R|CARDXREF|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS|SHR|indexed random, key card number|
|STEP10R|TRANTYPE|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.VSAM.KSDS|SHR|indexed random, key 2-byte type|
|STEP10R|TRANCATG|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANCATG.VSAM.KSDS|SHR|indexed random, key type(2)+cat(4)|
|STEP10R|DATEPARM|AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DATEPARM|SHR|80-byte record; contents not in repo|

Transaction record (copybook CVTRA05Y, 350 bytes, all DISPLAY): TRAN-ID X(16) pos1; TRAN-TYPE-CD X(2) pos17; TRAN-CAT-CD 9(4) pos19; TRAN-SOURCE X(10) pos23; TRAN-DESC X(100) pos33; TRAN-AMT S9(9)V99 zoned pos133 (11 bytes); TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(9) pos144; TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) pos153; TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) pos203; TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) pos253; TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) pos263; TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) pos279; TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) pos305; FILLER X(20) pos331. (SORT symbol positions 263 and 305 match.) CBTRN03C's FD view is FD-TRANS-DATA X(304)/FD-TRAN-PROC-TS X(26)/FILLER X(20) and it reads INTO TRAN-RECORD.

DATEPARM record as consumed (WS-DATEPARM-RECORD): WS-START-DATE X(10) pos1-10, FILLER X(1) pos11, WS-END-DATE X(10) pos12-21; rest of 80 bytes ignored. Format expected `YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD` (compared as text).

XREF (CVACT03Y, 50 bytes): XREF-CARD-NUM X(16), XREF-CUST-ID 9(9), XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11), FILLER X(14). TRAN-TYPE (CVTRA03Y, 60): TRAN-TYPE X(2), TRAN-TYPE-DESC X(50), FILLER X(8). TRAN-CAT (CVTRA04Y, 60): TRAN-TYPE-CD X(2), TRAN-CAT-CD 9(4), TRAN-CAT-TYPE-DESC X(50), FILLER X(4).

##### Processing flow
**Step 1 (REPROC/IDCAMS)**: REPRO full copy of the TRANSACT KSDS into a new GDG generation TRANSACT.BKUP(+1) (RECFM=FB, LRECL=350, SPACE CYL(1,1) RLSE, DISP NEW,CATLG,DELETE). Output is in KSDS key order (TRAN-ID).

**Step 2 (SORT)**: `INCLUDE COND=(TRAN-PROC-DT,GE,C'2022-01-01',AND,TRAN-PROC-DT,LE,C'2022-07-06')` — character compare of the first 10 bytes of TRAN-PROC-TS; `SORT FIELDS=(TRAN-CARD-NUM,A)` with ZD (zoned decimal) format on the 16-byte card number. Output TRANSACT.DALY(+1), DCB copied from SORTIN.

**Step 3 (CBTRN03C)**:
1. DISPLAY 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN03C'.
2. Open in order TRANFILE(input), TRANREPT(output), CARDXREF, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, DATEPARM (input). Any status ≠ '00' → DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING …', display file status, 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.
3. 0550-DATEPARM-READ: status '00' → DISPLAY 'Reporting from <start> to <end>'; '10' (empty) → END-OF-FILE='Y' (no transactions processed, report empty, normal end); other → abend.
4. Main loop `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE='Y'`:
   - 1000-TRANFILE-GET-NEXT: READ INTO TRAN-RECORD; '00' ok; '10' → END-OF-FILE='Y' (TRAN-RECORD keeps the previous record's data); other → abend.
   - Date filter: if TRAN-PROC-TS(1:10) ≥ WS-START-DATE and ≤ WS-END-DATE → CONTINUE; **else NEXT SENTENCE**, which transfers control past the period after END-PERFORM, i.e. the loop is abandoned and the program goes straight to closing files — no further records, no page/grand totals written. This check also runs on the EOF iteration against the stale last record.
   - If not EOF: DISPLAY TRAN-RECORD (to SYSOUT); if TRAN-CARD-NUM ≠ WS-CURR-CARD-NUM: if WS-FIRST-TIME='N' write account totals (1120-WRITE-ACCOUNT-TOTALS); save card; 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF (random READ CARDXREF; INVALID KEY → DISPLAY 'INVALID CARD NUMBER : '…, abend). Then 1500-B-LOOKUP-TRANTYPE (key TRAN-TYPE-CD; INVALID KEY → abend), 1500-C-LOOKUP-TRANCATG (key type+cat; INVALID KEY → abend), then 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT.
   - If EOF: DISPLAY 'TRAN-AMT ' and 'WS-PAGE-TOTAL'; ADD TRAN-AMT (the last record's amount, again) to WS-PAGE-TOTAL and WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL; 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS; 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS.
5. 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT: on first call set WS-FIRST-TIME='N', move dates into header, write headers (4 lines). If MOD(WS-LINE-COUNTER,20)=0 → write page totals then headers. Add TRAN-AMT to page & account totals; write detail line (+1 line).
6. 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS: write 'Page Total' line, add page total to grand total, zero page total, write dash line (+2 lines). 1120-WRITE-ACCOUNT-TOTALS: write 'Account Total' line, zero account total, dash line (+2). 1120-WRITE-HEADERS: name header, blank, header-1, dash line (+4). 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS: 'Grand Total' line (counter not incremented).
7. Close all six files (errors → abend), DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN03C', GOBACK.

All write errors in 1111-WRITE-REPORT-REC (status ≠ '00') → abend. 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM calls CEE3ABD with ABCODE 999, TIMING 0 (user abend U999). 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS prints 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' + 4-digit status (binary second byte decoded when stat1='9' or non-numeric).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[TRANREPT JOB] --> B[STEP05R PROC=REPROC IDCAMS REPRO\nTRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS -> TRANSACT.BKUP+1]
  B --> C[STEP05R SORT INCLUDE PROC-DT 2022-01-01..2022-07-06\nSORT TRAN-CARD-NUM A -> TRANSACT.DALY+1]
  C --> D[STEP10R CBTRN03C]
  D --> E[0000..0500 OPEN 6 files]
  E -->|open fail| Z[9999-ABEND-PROGRAM CEE3ABD 999]
  E --> F[0550-DATEPARM-READ]
  F -->|status 10| X[close files, GOBACK - empty report]
  F -->|other err| Z
  F --> G[1000-TRANFILE-GET-NEXT]
  G -->|read err| Z
  G --> H{PROC-TS 1:10 within WS-START..WS-END?}
  H -->|no: NEXT SENTENCE| X2[exit loop, close files, no totals]
  H -->|yes| I{END-OF-FILE?}
  I -->|N| J{card changed?}
  J -->|yes, not first| K[1120-WRITE-ACCOUNT-TOTALS]
  J -->|yes| L[1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF CARDXREF]
  K --> L
  L -->|INVALID KEY| Z
  J -->|no| M
  L --> M[1500-B-LOOKUP-TRANTYPE / 1500-C-LOOKUP-TRANCATG]
  M -->|INVALID KEY| Z
  M --> N[1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT headers/page break/detail]
  N --> G
  I -->|Y| O[ADD last TRAN-AMT again; 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS; 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS]
  O --> X3[9000-9500 CLOSE, GOBACK]
```

##### Data
Read: TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS (full), TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), TRANSACT.DALY(+1), CARDXREF KSDS (key 16), TRANTYPE KSDS (key 2), TRANCATG KSDS (key 6), DATEPARM. Written: TRANSACT.BKUP(+1) (LRECL 350), TRANSACT.DALY(+1) (LRECL 350), TRANREPT(+1) (FB 133). GDG bases defined by DEFGDGB.jcl: TRANSACT.BKUP, TRANSACT.DALY, TRANREPT each LIMIT(5) SCRATCH (oldest generation scratched after 5).

Report line layouts (CVTRA07Y, padded with spaces to 133):
- REPORT-NAME-HEADER: 'DALYREPT' X(38), 'Daily Transaction Report' X(41), 'Date Range: ' X(12), start X(10), ' to ' X(4), end X(10).
- TRANSACTION-HEADER-1: 'Transaction ID' X(17), 'Account ID' X(12), 'Transaction Type' X(19), 'Tran Category' X(35), 'Tran Source' X(14), space, '        Amount' X(16).
- TRANSACTION-HEADER-2: 133 × '-'.
- TRANSACTION-DETAIL-REPORT: TRAN-ID X(16), sp, XREF-ACCT-ID X(11), sp, type cd X(2), '-', TRAN-TYPE-DESC X(15) (truncated from 50), sp, cat cd 9(4), '-', TRAN-CAT-TYPE-DESC X(29) (truncated from 50), sp, TRAN-SOURCE X(10), 4 sp, amount `-ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.ZZ`, 2 sp.
- REPORT-PAGE-TOTALS: 'Page Total' X(11), 86 '.', `+ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.ZZ`. REPORT-ACCOUNT-TOTALS: 'Account Total' X(13), 84 '.', same edit. REPORT-GRAND-TOTALS: 'Grand Total' X(11), 86 '.', same edit.

##### Outputs & side effects
New generations of TRANSACT.BKUP, TRANSACT.DALY, TRANREPT; SYSOUT DISPLAYs (start/end messages, date range, every in-range TRAN-RECORD in full, final TRAN-AMT/page total). Abend U999 on any I/O error or missing reference record. No master files updated.

##### External calls
IDCAMS (via PROC REPROC, control card REPROCT); DFSORT/SORT (SYMNAMES, INCLUDE, SORT); CBTRN03C (no CALLs except LE service CEE3ABD(ABCODE=999, TIMING=0) to abend).

##### Migration notes
- **Date range is defined twice**: hard-coded in SORT SYMNAMES (2022-01-01..2022-07-06) and separately in DATEPARM dataset. If DATEPARM's range is narrower, the first out-of-range record (anywhere, because the file is sorted by card not date) makes CBTRN03C silently stop: NEXT SENTENCE inside the inline PERFORM exits the loop; no account/page/grand totals are written and RC is 0.
- **Final amount double-counted**: on EOF the last record's TRAN-AMT is added again to page and account totals before writing the last page total and the grand total, so the final Page Total and Grand Total are overstated by the last transaction amount.
- **Last account total never written**: account totals are emitted only on card-number change; after the final card only page and grand totals are written.
- Account breaks are on card number (sort key), not account id; an account with several cards gets several 'Account Total' lines.
- Page break test MOD(line counter,20)=0 is only evaluated before a detail line; the counter includes header (4), total (2) and detail (1) lines, so account-total lines can skip past a multiple of 20 and pages have variable length. First page has no page-break check effect (counter=4 after first header).
- Grand total = sum of page totals at the time each page total is written.
- Descriptions truncated (type 15 chars, category 29); account id 9(11) moved into X(11); totals S9(9)V99 truncate silently on overflow.
- Empty DATEPARM → normal end, empty report. Empty TRANFILE → filter compares uninitialized TRAN-RECORD (content compiler-dependent); output almost certainly empty with no totals.
- READ ... INVALID KEY handles only not-found; other non-'00' statuses on the random lookups are not checked.
- SORT uses ZD format for card number (16 digits); non-numeric card numbers would sort per ZD rules, not character order.
- Two steps share the name STEP05R (PROC step and SORT step); overrides by step name are ambiguous in this member. The PROC version (app/proc/TRANREPT.prc) uses STEP01R for the unload.
- All datasets are hard-coded with HLQ AWS.M2.CARDDEMO; GDG relative (+1) references in later steps resolve to the generation created earlier in the same job.
recommendation: Fully traced. Unresolved only: contents of dataset AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DATEPARM (not in repo) and the initial contents of the uninitialized TRAN-RECORD working storage on an empty input (compiler/runtime dependent). Customer should confirm whether the double-counted final amount, the missing last account total and the NEXT SENTENCE early-exit are behaviors to preserve.
note:
Consolidated document for app/cbl/CBTRN03C.cbl, app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl; merged duplicates: sfind-07276fc47cfb4ea584ad364e22921f15, sfind-bdd161f090414d368e006e9a9667ea5b, sfind-ab9fd62ab3df4e27a0be972f630bcd08.

- Bug-compatible behaviours: (a) last transaction's amount is added twice to page/account totals at EOF (then grand total includes it twice); (b) the final account's ACCOUNT TOTAL line is never written (only page + grand totals at EOF); (c) grand total only accumulates at page-total time; (d) page break test happens BEFORE the detail line and header lines also increment the counter, so pages are not
- The page-total line written at a page break is followed by headers but page total resets; account totals are not reset at page breaks.
- TRAN-REPORT-ACCOUNT-ID is X(11) moved from 9(11).

title: XREFFILE job: rebuild card/account cross-reference KSDS with account-id alternate index and path
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `XREFFILE` ('Delete define cross ref file', CLASS=A, MSGCLASS=0). Listed in README setup/run sequences; uploaded by scripts/run_full_batch.sh and remote_refresh.sh. Not present in the CA-7 or Control-M definitions in this repo.

##### Inputs
STEP15 `XREFDATA DD DISP=SHR,DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.PS` — FB 50, copybook CVACT03Y: XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) pos1-16, XREF-CUST-ID 9(9) pos17-25, XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) pos26-36, FILLER X(14). Sample app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt (e.g. `0500024453765740` card, `000000050` cust, `00000000050` acct).

##### Processing flow
1. STEP05 IDCAMS: DELETE CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS CLUSTER; `IF MAXCC LE 08 THEN SET MAXCC = 0`; DELETE CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX ALTERNATEINDEX; same reset. (Deleting the base cluster also deletes its related AIX/path, so the second delete normally gets not-found, which is masked.)
2. STEP10 IDCAMS: DEFINE CLUSTER NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS) CYLINDERS(1 5) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(50 50) SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) ERASE INDEXED; DATA ...KSDS.DATA; INDEX ...KSDS.INDEX.
3. STEP15 IDCAMS: REPRO INFILE(XREFDATA) OUTFILE(XREFVSAM) (XREFVSAM DISP=SHR).
4. STEP20 IDCAMS: DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX) RELATE(base) KEYS(11,25) (account id, offset 25 = bytes 26-36) NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE RECORDSIZE(50,50) FREESPACE(10,20) VOLUMES(AWSHJ1) CYLINDERS(5,1); DATA ...AIX.DATA; INDEX ...AIX.INDEX.
5. STEP25 IDCAMS: DEFINE PATH NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH) PATHENTRY(...AIX).
6. STEP30 IDCAMS: BLDINDEX INDATASET(base KSDS) OUTDATASET(AIX).
No COND parameters; every step runs regardless of prior RC.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[XREFFILE JOB] --> B[STEP05 DELETE KSDS + AIX, mask MAXCC<=8]
  B --> C[STEP10 DEFINE CLUSTER CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS KEYS 16 0]
  C --> D[STEP15 REPRO CARDXREF.PS -> KSDS]
  D --> E[STEP20 DEFINE AIX KEYS 11,25 NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE]
  E --> F[STEP25 DEFINE PATH CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH]
  F --> G[STEP30 BLDINDEX KSDS -> AIX]
```

##### Data
Creates base KSDS keyed by card number (16), AIX keyed by account id (11, non-unique: one account → many cards), and PATH. Consumers: CBTRN03C/other batch via CARDXREF DD (base, card key); INTCALC.jcl and CICS file CXACAIX (CSD, DSNAME ...CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH) for account-to-card lookup.

##### Outputs & side effects
Destroys and rebuilds the xref dataset, AIX and path. UPGRADE means later base-cluster updates through opened upgrade set maintain the AIX. Should run with CICS files CXACAIX/xref closed (CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL jobs close/open CXACAIX).

##### External calls
IDCAMS (6 invocations).

##### Migration notes
- Order matters: the AIX is built after the load (BLDINDEX), so the REPRO does not maintain it; a re-implementation must index after loading.
- Account-id index is non-unique; the base key (card) is unique — REPRO requires input sorted by card number without duplicates.
- Delete masking only resets MAXCC ≤ 8; an RC 12 delete failure would remain, but subsequent steps still run (no COND).
- SHAREOPTIONS(2 3) on base vs (1 4) on TRANTYPE: different concurrency semantics.
- AIX RECORDSIZE(50,50) is fixed-length; with NONUNIQUEKEY an AIX record holds key+pointers to multiple primary keys, so many cards per account could overflow a 50-byte AIX record (each primary key pointer is 16 bytes plus header) — capacity limit inherited by the design (IDCAMS behavior, not verified at runtime).
- Hard-coded volume AWSHJ1.
recommendation: Fully documented.
note:
End-to-end: XREFFILE is submitted by remote_refresh.sh and run_full_batch.sh. Upstream findings: sfind-89eccdc975c54f8c8f058e029a06ca5f, sfind-574c7fefe140460688d7131108eb4d55.

title: ASMWAIT macro: STIMER WAIT with binary interval (used by MVSWAIT)
description:
##### Entry point
Assembler macro `ASMWAIT` in app/maclib/ASMWAIT.mac, prototype `&NAME ASMWAIT &B`. Only user in repo: MVSWAIT.asm (`ASMWAIT BINLBL`), called by COBOL COBSWAIT (WAITSTEP job).

##### Inputs
`&B` — label of a fullword (DS F) containing the interval in hundredths of a second (BINTVL format).

##### Processing flow
Expands to one instruction: `STIMER WAIT,BINTVL=&B`. `&NAME` is accepted but not placed on the generated statement (label dropped).
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[MVSWAIT: ASMWAIT BINLBL] --> X[STIMER WAIT,BINTVL=BINLBL]
  X --> R[task resumes after interval]
```

##### Data
Reads the fullword at &B.

##### Outputs & side effects
Suspends the task for the interval.

##### External calls
z/OS STIMER service.

##### Migration notes
The `&NAME` label is ignored by the expansion, so a label coded on ASMWAIT would not be defined. Interval unit is 0.01 s.
recommendation: Fully documented; see WAITSTEP flow for the full call chain.
