title: CA-7 job network for CardDemo (CLOSEFIL-triggered chains: posting, reference loads, reads, statements, reports)
description:
##### Entry point
CA-7 `LJOB,JOB=…,LIST=ALL` listing (app/scheduler/CardDemo.ca7, date 06.198). All jobs: SYSTEM CARDDEMO, JCL ID 255, member = job name (except CLOSEFIL1/CLOSEFIL2 which run member CLOSEFIL), JCLLIB=&CARDDEMOPRODJCL, MSGCLASS=A, REGION=4096K, CPUTM 00023, ELAPTM 2359, flags 'JOB MARKED AS MAINT ONLY'=Y, 'COMP TRIGGERS OTHER JOBS'=Y, 'DONT SCHEDULE BEFORE 03237'. Sequencing is by job-completion triggers (QTM=0100, LEADTM=0000).

##### Inputs
Trigger records (job → triggered job, SCHID):
- CLOSEFIL → CBPAUP0J (030) → POSTTRAN (030) → WAITSTEP (030) → OPENFIL (030)
- CLOSEFIL → TRANTYPE (030) → WAITSTEP (030) → CLOSEFIL1 (031) and CLOSEFIL2 (032)
- CLOSEFIL1 (member CLOSEFIL) → TRANCATG (031) → WAITSTEP (031) → CLOSEFIL (030)
- CLOSEFIL2 (member CLOSEFIL) → TCATBALF (032) → WAITSTEP (032) → CLOSEFIL (030)
- CLOSEFIL → READACCT (030) → READCARD (030) → READCUST (030) → READXREF (030) → WAITSTEP (030) → OPENFIL (030)
- CLOSEFIL → CREASTMT (030) → TXT2PDF1 (030) → WAITSTEP (030) → OPENFIL (030); also TXT2PDF1 → CLOSEFIL (031)
- CLOSEFIL (031) → PRTCATBL (031) → WAITSTEP (031) → OPENFIL (031)

##### Processing flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CF[CLOSEFIL] --> PA[CBPAUP0J] --> PT[POSTTRAN] --> W1[WAITSTEP] --> OF1[OPENFIL]
  CF --> TT[TRANTYPE] --> W2[WAITSTEP] --> C1[CLOSEFIL1] & C2[CLOSEFIL2]
  C1 --> TC[TRANCATG] --> W3[WAITSTEP 031] --> CF
  C2 --> TB[TCATBALF] --> W4[WAITSTEP 032] --> CF
  CF --> RA[READACCT] --> RC[READCARD] --> RU[READCUST] --> RX[READXREF] --> W5[WAITSTEP] --> OF2[OPENFIL]
  CF --> CS[CREASTMT] --> TP[TXT2PDF1] --> W6[WAITSTEP] --> OF3[OPENFIL]
  TP --> CF31[CLOSEFIL 031] --> PR[PRTCATBL] --> W7[WAITSTEP 031] --> OF4[OPENFIL 031]
```
Pattern: every update chain is bracketed by CLOSEFIL (CICS file close via console CEMT) and OPENFIL, with WAITSTEP (36 s) before reopening/next close.

##### Data
No datasets defined in the scheduler; data flow comes from the jobs (e.g. TRANTYPE rebuilds TRANTYPE KSDS; TXT2PDF1 converts CREASTMT's STATEMNT.PS).

##### Outputs & side effects
Job submission order only.

##### External calls
Submits JCL members from &CARDDEMOPRODJCL.

##### Migration notes
- Trigger graph contains cycles (CLOSEFIL → TRANTYPE → … → CLOSEFIL1 → TRANCATG → WAITSTEP → CLOSEFIL); in CA-7 triggers fire per completion, so a naive DAG scheduler cannot represent it as-is and could loop. SCHID values (030/031/032) distinguish the branches.
- CLOSEFIL1/CLOSEFIL2 are aliases for the same JCL member CLOSEFIL allowing parallel branches.
- WAITSTEP is reused by many branches with different SCHIDs.
- XREFFILE, TRANREPT, INTCALC, COMBTRAN, TRANBKP are not in this CA-7 listing (TRANBKP/INTCALC/COMBTRAN appear only in Control-M).
- 'MAINT ONLY' flag set on all jobs (CA-7 treats as maintenance jobs — no dataset requirement tracking).
recommendation: The listing is an LJOB report export, not CA-7 database definitions: trigger lists for CLOSEFIL are split across several listing fragments and some entries are listed without job-detail blocks. Calendar/schedule IDs (SCHID 030/031/032) meanings and time-of-day are not defined in the file; customer must provide CA-7 schedule (SCHD) definitions to confirm run frequency.

title: Ad-hoc single JCL submission via FTP/JES (remote_submit.sh)
description:
##### Entry point
Bash script `scripts/remote_submit.sh <file_name> <file_extension>`; no caller exists in the repo.

##### Inputs
- `$1` file_name: path of a local JCL file.
- `$2` file_extension: must equal `.jcl` exactly.

##### Processing flow
1. Tunnel check `ps f | grep -c "2121:"` == 1 → echo 'FTP Tunnel to Ensono not running.' and exit.
2. Echo the two args.
3. If `$file_extension != ".jcl"` → echo 'Only files with jcl extension can be submitted on mainframe', exit.
4. `tnftp localhost 2121`: `pwd`, `quote site filetype=JES`, `put $file_name`, `bye` — submits the file as a JES job.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[remote_submit.sh file ext] --> B{tunnel on 2121?}
  B -->|no| X1[echo; exit]
  B -->|yes| C{ext == .jcl?}
  C -->|no| X2[echo only jcl; exit]
  C -->|yes| D[tnftp localhost 2121; site filetype=JES; put file; bye]
```

##### Data
Reads the local JCL file only.

##### Outputs & side effects
One JES job submission; FTP dialogue on stdout.

##### External calls
`tnftp` FTP/JES at localhost:2121 (tunnelled); auth via tnftp auto-login, not in script.

##### Migration notes
- Extension test is case-sensitive: upper-case members such as `CREASTMT.JCL`, `TXT2PDF1.JCL` in app/jcl are rejected.
- `$file_extension` is unquoted; an empty `$2` makes `[` error out (non-zero), so the reject branch is skipped and the script proceeds to submit.
- No job completion or RC check; exit status 0 on early exits.
recommendation: Fully documented. No caller is in the repo (likely an IDE task passing file/extension arguments); confirm invocation.

title: Shell-driven interest calculation cycle via FTP/JES submit (CLOSEFIL, INTCALC, TRANBKP, COMBTRAN, TRANIDX, OPENFIL)
description:
##### Entry point
Bash script `scripts/run_interest_calc.sh`, run manually by an operator on a workstation with an FTP tunnel to the mainframe (message text: 'Ensono') on localhost:2121. No arguments.

##### Inputs
- Local files `jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl`, `jcl/INTCALC.jcl`, `jcl/TRANBKP.jcl`, `jcl/COMBTRAN.jcl`, `jcl/TRANIDX.jcl`, `jcl/OPENFIL.jcl`, relative to the current directory (repo has them in `app/jcl`, so it must be run from `app/`).
- Process list (`ps f`) to detect the tunnel.

##### Processing flow
1. Tunnel check: `ps f | grep -c "2121:"`; if the count is 1 (only the grep itself) print 'FTP Tunnel to Ensono not running.' and exit (status 0).
2. Echo 'Running Interest Calculation Cycle'.
3. Open `tnftp localhost 2121` with a here-doc: `pwd`, `quote site filetype=JES` (FTP server in JES mode: each `put` submits the file as a batch job).
4. Submit in order: CLOSEFIL → sleep 5 → INTCALC → sleep 5 → TRANBKP (no sleep) → COMBTRAN → sleep 5 → TRANIDX → sleep 5 → OPENFIL; `bye`. The `!echo`/`!sleep` lines are local shell escapes from tnftp.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[run_interest_calc.sh] --> C{ps f grep -c 2121: == 1?}
  C -->|yes| E[echo tunnel not running; exit]
  C -->|no| F[tnftp localhost 2121; quote site filetype=JES]
  F --> J1[put jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl] --> W1[sleep 5] --> J2[put jcl/INTCALC.jcl] --> W2[sleep 5] --> J3[put jcl/TRANBKP.jcl] --> J4[put jcl/COMBTRAN.jcl] --> W3[sleep 5] --> J5[put jcl/TRANIDX.jcl] --> W4[sleep 5] --> J6[put jcl/OPENFIL.jcl] --> B[bye]
```

##### Data
No local data written. Submitted jobs: CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL (CEMT close/open TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, USRSEC in CICSAWSA); INTCALC (CBACT04C PARM='2022071800', writes SYSTRAN(+1)); TRANBKP (backup TRANSACT KSDS to TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), delete/redefine KSDS, delete AIX); COMBTRAN (sort BKUP(0)+SYSTRAN(0) by TRAN-ID into TRANSACT.COMBINED(+1), REPRO to KSDS); TRANIDX (define AIX KEYS(26 304) NONUNIQUEKEY UPGRADE, PATH, BLDINDEX).

##### Outputs & side effects
Six JES job submissions; console echoes; FTP replies (job IDs) to stdout only.

##### External calls
`tnftp` to the FTP/JES interface at localhost:2121 (tunnelled). Credentials come from tnftp auto-login (e.g. ~/.netrc) — not in the script.

##### Migration notes
- Fire-and-forget: `put` returns once JES accepts the job, not when it ends; 5-second sleeps do not guarantee ordering and there is no return-code check — a failing INTCALC still lets TRANBKP/COMBTRAN run. Jobs may overlap unless JES serializes them.
- Order differs from Control-M MONTHLY-InterestCalculation: this script runs TRANBKP between INTCALC and COMBTRAN and adds TRANIDX, but has no WAITSTEP. TRANBKP must finish before COMBTRAN reads BKUP(0), yet no sleep separates them.
- Tunnel detection depends on `ps f` (current-terminal processes only) showing a process with '2121:' in its command line (e.g. `ssh -L 2121:...`) — environment-dependent.
- Exits status 0 even on the failure path.
- Same pattern as run_full_batch.sh and run_posting.sh (outside this batch), which add data-refresh and POSTTRAN steps.
recommendation: Fully documented. Re-implementation should replace fixed sleeps with completion/return-code checks; customer should confirm whether this order (TRANBKP inside the cycle, TRANIDX after COMBTRAN) or the Control-M MONTHLY-InterestCalculation order is authoritative.
note: Owners from git history (no CODEOWNERS file in repo).

title: Remote COBOL batch compile/link via templated JCL submitted to JES (remote_compile.sh + compile_batch.jcl.template)
description:
##### Entry point
Bash script `scripts/remote_compile.sh <file_name> <file_extension> <basename_no_ext>` (developer tooling; no caller in repo).

##### Inputs
- `$1` file_name (echoed only), `$2` file_extension (must be `.cbl`), `$3` member base name.
- `./compile_batch.jcl.template` (relative to cwd; exists at scripts/compile_batch.jcl.template).
- `Makefile` in cwd (not present in the repo).

##### Processing flow
1. Tunnel check (`ps f | grep -c "2121:"` == 1 → message, exit).
2. `pwd`; `make -f Makefile` — comment says it uploads latest modules to the mainframe; result not checked.
3. Echo args; if ext != `.cbl` → 'Only files with cbl extension can be compiled on mainframe', exit.
4. `sed s/ZZZZZZZZ/<basename>/g template > <basename>.tmp`; if sed rc≠0 → 'JCL template substition failed rc = …', exit.
5. `tnftp localhost 2121`: `quote site filetype=JES`, `put <basename>.tmp` (submit), `bye`.
6. `rm <basename>.tmp`.

Submitted JCL (job COMPILEC, CLASS=A, MSGCLASS=0, REGION=0M, TIME=1440) runs in-stream PROC BLDBAT with MEM=<basename>:
- COMPILE: IGYCRCTL (STEPLIB IGY.SIGYCOMP.V63, PARM APOST,LIST,MAP,NUMBER), SYSIN AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL(&MEM), SYSLIB AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY, SYSPRINT AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LISTING(&MEM), object to &&LOADSET.
- CBLPRINT: IEBGENER copies LISTING(&MEM) to SYSOUT.
- LKED: HEWL PARM LIST,XREF; SYSLIB SYS1.LINKLIB, CSF.SCSFMOD0, CEE.SCEELKED, CEE.SCEELKEX, AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB; SYSLMOD AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(&MEM).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[remote_compile.sh] --> B{tunnel?}
  B -->|no| X[exit]
  B -->|yes| M[make -f Makefile]
  M --> C{ext == .cbl?}
  C -->|no| X2[exit]
  C -->|yes| S[sed ZZZZZZZZ to member > member.tmp]
  S --> R{sed rc 0?}
  R -->|no| X3[exit]
  R -->|yes| F[tnftp JES put member.tmp] --> D[rm member.tmp]
  F -.JES.-> J[COMPILEC: COMPILE IGYCRCTL -> CBLPRINT IEBGENER -> LKED HEWL -> LOADLIB member]
```

##### Data
Writes/deletes local temp `<basename>.tmp`. Mainframe: reads CBL/CPY PDS, writes LISTING and LOADLIB members.

##### Outputs & side effects
JES compile job; updated load module in AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB.

##### External calls
`make` (Makefile not in repo — unresolved), `sed`, `tnftp` FTP/JES at localhost:2121.

##### Migration notes
- No COND= on CBLPRINT/LKED: link-edit is attempted even if compile fails.
- Member names >8 chars break the JCL; extension check is case-sensitive (`.CBL` rejected).
- Compiles the mainframe PDS copy, not the local file — local edits must be uploaded first (presumably by the missing Makefile).
- Temp file deleted even if FTP submit fails; exit status 0 on early exits.
recommendation: Fully documented except the 'make -f Makefile' step: no Makefile exists in the repo, so module-upload behavior is unresolved; customer should supply it if relevant.

title: CA-7 job-trigger network: posting, transaction-type/category refresh, file reads, statement generation, category-balance print
description:
##### Entry point
`app/scheduler/CardDemo.ca7` — output of CA-7 `LJOB,JOB=xxx,LIST=ALL` commands (DATE=06.198). Execution enters by CA-7 job-completion triggers: when a listed job completes normally, each job in its `TRIGGERED JOBS` section is brought into the request queue with the given SCHID. The head jobs (CLOSEFIL at lines 18, 159, 337, 465) have no visible predecessor; how they are scheduled is not in this file.

##### Inputs
Per-job attributes (identical for every listed job): JCL ID 255, SYSTEM=CARDDEMO, MAIN=ALL, SCHED DSNBR 000652, JCLLIB=&CARDDEMOPRODJCL, OWNER *NONE*, CLASS blank, MSGCLASS=A, REGION=4096K, PRTY=000, CPUTM=00023, ELAPTM=2359, 'JOB MARKED AS MAINT ONLY'=Y, 'COMP TRIGGERS OTHER JOBS'=Y (except OPENFIL at line 138 =N), DONT SCHEDULE BEFORE 03237. Trigger entries: QTM=0100 (1h queue time), LEADTM=0000, SUBMTM blank or 0000. JCL member equals job name except CLOSEFIL1 and CLOSEFIL2, whose MEMBER is `CLOSEFIL`.

##### Processing flow
Reading the listing segment by segment (each segment starts at an `LJOB,JOB=CLOSEFIL`):

1. Segment A (lines 18-157) – transaction posting, SCHID 030: CLOSEFIL → CBPAUP0J (`app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl/CBPAUP0J.jcl`) → POSTTRAN → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL (end).
2. Segment B (lines 159-335) – reference-data refresh with fan-out/fan-in: CLOSEFIL → TRANTYPE(030) → WAITSTEP(030) → {CLOSEFIL1 SCHID 031, CLOSEFIL2 SCHID 032} in parallel; CLOSEFIL1 → TRANCATG(031) → WAITSTEP(031) → CLOSEFIL(030); CLOSEFIL2 → TCATBALF(032) → WAITSTEP(032) → CLOSEFIL(030).
3. Segment C (lines 337-463) – CLOSEFIL → READACCT → READCARD → READCUST → READXREF → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL (all SCHID 030).
4. Segment D (lines 465-570) – statement and report: CLOSEFIL → CREASTMT → TXT2PDF1 → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL(030) → CLOSEFIL(031) → PRTCATBL(031) → WAITSTEP(031) → OPENFIL(031).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph A[Segment A SCHID 030]
    A1[CLOSEFIL] --> A2[CBPAUP0J] --> A3[POSTTRAN] --> A4[WAITSTEP] --> A5[OPENFIL]
  end
  subgraph B[Segment B]
    B1[CLOSEFIL] --> B2[TRANTYPE 030] --> B3[WAITSTEP 030]
    B3 --> B4[CLOSEFIL1 031 member CLOSEFIL] --> B5[TRANCATG 031] --> B6[WAITSTEP 031] --> B9[CLOSEFIL 030]
    B3 --> B7[CLOSEFIL2 032 member CLOSEFIL] --> B8[TCATBALF 032] --> B10[WAITSTEP 032] --> B9
  end
  subgraph C[Segment C SCHID 030]
    C1[CLOSEFIL] --> C2[READACCT] --> C3[READCARD] --> C4[READCUST] --> C5[READXREF] --> C6[WAITSTEP] --> C7[OPENFIL]
  end
  subgraph D[Segment D]
    D1[CLOSEFIL] --> D2[CREASTMT] --> D3[TXT2PDF1] --> D4[WAITSTEP] --> D5[OPENFIL 030] --> D6[CLOSEFIL 031] --> D7[PRTCATBL 031] --> D8[WAITSTEP 031] --> D9[OPENFIL 031]
  end
  B9 -.continues as.-> C1
```

Branches: CA-7 triggers fire only on normal completion; there are no conditional or abnormal-completion triggers in the file. Segment B's CLOSEFIL(030) at the fan-in is listed again at line 337 with READACCT as its trigger, so Segment B plausibly flows into Segment C (inference from listing order, not explicit).

##### Data
No datasets listed (requirements sections not printed). Jobs invoked act on CardDemo VSAM and CICS files (CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL: CEMT SET FIL TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, USRSEC CLO/OPE in CICSAWSA; WAITSTEP: COBSWAIT 36 s).

##### Outputs & side effects
Job submissions from &CARDDEMOPRODJCL; CICS file closures during each segment.

##### External calls
JCL members CLOSEFIL, CBPAUP0J, POSTTRAN, WAITSTEP, OPENFIL, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, TCATBALF, READACCT, READCARD, READCUST, READXREF, CREASTMT (.JCL), TXT2PDF1 (.JCL), PRTCATBL — all present under app/jcl except CBPAUP0J (app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl). No members CLOSEFIL1/CLOSEFIL2 exist; they run member CLOSEFIL.

##### Migration notes
- In a real CA-7 database a job name is unique, so the trigger lists for CLOSEFIL (CBPAUP0J, TRANTYPE, READACCT, CREASTMT, PRTCATBL), WAITSTEP (OPENFIL, CLOSEFIL1, CLOSEFIL2, CLOSEFIL) and OPENFIL (CLOSEFIL 031) would be merged and fire together, possibly qualified by the triggering job's SCHID (not shown). Taken literally this creates cycles (WAITSTEP→CLOSEFIL→…→WAITSTEP). Decide whether to model these as four separate chains (as the listing segments suggest) or reproduce SCHID-qualified triggers.
- Fan-in at Segment B: CLOSEFIL(030) is triggered by both WAITSTEP(031) and WAITSTEP(032); CA-7 triggers do not AND by themselves, so without a requirement definition CLOSEFIL could run twice. Model an explicit join.
- Segment D runs OPENFIL then immediately CLOSEFIL again for PRTCATBL — online availability window is brief.
- OPENFIL in segment A has 'COMP TRIGGERS OTHER JOBS'=N, but OPENFIL in segment D lists a trigger (CLOSEFIL 031): inconsistent listings.
- Line 423 is `LJOB,JOB=READXREF,LIST=` (truncated) yet output is LIST=ALL — cosmetic.
- QTM=0100 means the triggered job is due-out 1h after queueing; ELAPTM=2359 / CPUTM=00023 are limits to preserve if SLAs matter.

title: Control-M batch schedule: DAILY-TransactionBackup, WEEKLY DB2 refresh / DisclosureGroupsRefresh, MONTHLY-InterestCalculation
description:
##### Entry point
Control-M Desktop export `app/scheduler/CardDemo.controlm` (`<DEFTABLE>` with `Folder.xsd` schema). Execution enters when Control-M orders a folder at New Day per its scheduling criteria; each `<JOB>` submits the JCL member named in `MEMNAME` (APPL_TYPE=OS, i.e. z/OS JCL) from the job library. All jobs: APPLICATION=CARD-DEMO, SUB_APPLICATION=CTRLM, TASKTYPE=Job, MAXWAIT=7 (days to stay in AJF waiting), MAXRERUN=5, TIMETO=23:00 (no TIMEFROM), RULE_BASED_CALENDARS NAME="*", CYCLIC=0, CONFIRM=0, CRITICAL=0, AUTOARCH=1.

##### Inputs
No data inputs of its own. Inputs are Control-M *conditions* (name + ODATE=ODAT, the order date) and scheduling criteria:

| Folder (type) | Ordering criteria |
|---|---|
| DAILY-TransactionBackup (regular, id 1) | each job DAYS=ALL, all 12 months =1 |
| WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh (regular, id 2) | MNTTRDB2 has **no DAYS attribute** |
| WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh (SMART folder `DisclosureGroupsRefresh`, id 3) | folder DAYS=SA (Saturday), PRIORITY=AA, DATACENTER=PROD, SHIFT=Ignore Job, MAXRERUN=0, MAXWAIT=0, DAYSKEEPINNOTOK=1 |
| WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh (SMART folder `TransactionTypesDBRefresh`, id 4) | folder DAYS=SA, same attributes as id 3 |
| MONTHLY-InterestCalculation (regular, id 5) | **no DAYS attribute on any job** |

##### Processing flow
Each folder is a linear chain: job N adds condition `<folder>-<JOB>` (SIGN=+) on success; job N+1 waits for it (INCOND AND_OR=A) and on its own success deletes it (SIGN=-) and adds its own. The last job only deletes its predecessor's condition (no OUTCOND +).

1. **DAILY-TransactionBackup** (every day, by 23:00): CLOSEFIL → TRANBKP → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL.
   - CLOSEFIL (`app/jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl`): SDSF step issues `/F CICSAWSA,'CEMT SET FIL(x) CLO'` for TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, USRSEC.
   - TRANBKP: REPROC backs up AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS to GDG TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), IDCAMS deletes the KSDS and AIX (MAXCC≤8 reset to 0), redefines KSDS (KEYS(16 0), RECORDSIZE(350 350)).
   - WAITSTEP: PGM=COBSWAIT, SYSIN `00003600` centiseconds = 36 s pause.
   - OPENFIL: same SDSF/CEMT commands with OPE.
2. **WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh** regular folder: MNTTRDB2 (`app/app-transaction-type-db2/jcl/MNTTRDB2.jcl`) runs and adds `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2`.
3. **SMART DisclosureGroupsRefresh** (Saturday): CLOSEFIL waits for `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2` → DISCGRP → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL. At SMART-folder end, folder-level OUTCOND deletes `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2`.
4. **SMART TransactionTypesDBRefresh** (Saturday): single job TRANEXTR (`app/app-transaction-type-db2/jcl/TRANEXTR.jcl`) waits for `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2`; it has no OUTCOND of its own; folder end deletes the MNTTRDB2 condition.
5. **MONTHLY-InterestCalculation**: CLOSEFIL → INTCALC → COMBTRAN → WAITSTEP → OPENFIL.
   - INTCALC: PGM=CBACT04C PARM='2022071800' reading TCATBALF, CARDXREF (+AIX path), ACCTDATA, DISCGRP KSDSs and writing SYSTRAN(+1).
   - COMBTRAN: SORT TRANSACT.BKUP(0)+SYSTRAN(0) by TRAN-ID ascending into TRANSACT.COMBINED(+1), then IDCAMS REPRO into TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph DAILY[DAILY-TransactionBackup DAYS=ALL]
    D1[CLOSEFIL] -->|+CLOSEFIL cond| D2[TRANBKP] -->|+TRANBKP| D3[WAITSTEP] -->|+WAITSTEP| D4[OPENFIL]
  end
  subgraph WK[WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh regular]
    M[MNTTRDB2]
  end
  M -->|+WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2| S1
  M -->|same cond| T1
  subgraph SDG[SMART DisclosureGroupsRefresh DAYS=SA]
    S1[CLOSEFIL] --> S2[DISCGRP] --> S3[WAITSTEP] --> S4[OPENFIL]
    S4 -.folder end: -MNTTRDB2 cond.-> X1((del))
  end
  subgraph STT[SMART TransactionTypesDBRefresh DAYS=SA]
    T1[TRANEXTR] -.folder end: -MNTTRDB2 cond.-> X2((del))
  end
  subgraph MON[MONTHLY-InterestCalculation no DAYS]
    I1[CLOSEFIL] --> I2[INTCALC CBACT04C] --> I3[COMBTRAN] --> I4[WAITSTEP] --> I5[OPENFIL]
  end
  D2 -.TRANSACT.BKUP GDG consumed by.-> I3
```

Branches: no ON/DO actions other than conditions exist; a failing job does not add its condition, so successors stay waiting (up to MAXWAIT=7 days) and the job may be rerun up to MAXRERUN=5 times. No failure paths are defined.

##### Data
Condition names (all ODATE=ODAT): DAILY-TransactionBackup-{CLOSEFIL,TRANBKP,WAITSTEP}; WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2; WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh-{CLOSEFIL,DISCGRP,WAITSTEP}; MONTHLY-InterestCalculation-{CLOSEFIL,INTCALC,COMBTRAN,WAITSTEP}. Datasets touched by called JCL: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS/.AIX, TRANSACT.BKUP GDG, SYSTRAN GDG, TRANSACT.COMBINED GDG, TCATBALF/CARDXREF/ACCTDATA/DISCGRP KSDS; CICS files TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, USRSEC.

##### Outputs & side effects
Submits JCL jobs; adds/deletes Control-M conditions; via CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL makes CICS files unavailable to online users between close and open.

##### External calls
JCL members CLOSEFIL, TRANBKP, WAITSTEP, OPENFIL, MNTTRDB2, DISCGRP, TRANEXTR, INTCALC, COMBTRAN (documented by other batches). CICS region CICSAWSA via SDSF MODIFY/CEMT.

##### Migration notes
- 'MONTHLY' and 'WEEKLY' are names only: MONTHLY-InterestCalculation and MNTTRDB2 carry no DAYS/MONTHDAYS/calendar, so they are not auto-ordered by these definitions; only the two SMART folders (DAYS=SA) and DAILY (DAYS=ALL) are.
- Both SMART folders depend on MNTTRDB2's condition and **both delete it** at folder end — whichever finishes first can remove the condition before the other folder's job starts (race). The condition is date-qualified (ODAT), so MNTTRDB2 must run on the same order date (Saturday) for either to start.
- FOLDER_NAME `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh` is used twice (regular id 2 and SMART id 4) — a target scheduler with unique folder names must rename one.
- Monthly chain does not run TRANBKP itself; COMBTRAN consumes TRANSACT.BKUP(0) from the latest daily TRANBKP, and SYSTRAN(0) from INTCALC. The monthly chain also omits TRANIDX (rebuild of the TRANSACT AIX) that scripts/run_interest_calc.sh runs after COMBTRAN; TRANBKP deletes the AIX daily.
- INTCALC passes hard-coded PARM '2022071800' (processing date), not the order date.
- Same JCL members (CLOSEFIL, WAITSTEP, OPENFIL) are reused in several folders; WAITSTEP is a fixed 36-second sleep.
- TIMETO=23:00 with no TIMEFROM: jobs may start any time after ordering until 23:00.
recommendation: Fully documented from the XML. Customer input needed: (1) MNTTRDB2 and the whole MONTHLY-InterestCalculation folder have no DAYS/calendar criteria, so it is unclear how/when they are ordered (manual order or an external rule?); (2) confirm the intended relationship between the duplicate FOLDER_NAME 'WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh' (regular folder id 2 and SMART folder id 4); (3) confirm whether TRANIDX should follow COMBTRAN in the monthly cycle as it does in scripts/run_interest_calc.sh.
note: Duplicate of sfind-c0001c8086c54798b228ce1ea65e05ab (Control-M schedule); unique migration notes folded into that finding.

title: CREADB2 job - create CARDDEMO DB2 database/tables and seed transaction types/categories
description:
##### Entry point
JCL job `CREADB2` (member CREADB21.jcl), CLASS=A, `TYPRUN=SCAN` on the job card (as shipped it only syntax-checks; must be removed to run). Symbols CODER=AWS, LBNM=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO, DB2S=DAZ1. JOBLIB OEM.DB2.DAZ1.SDSNLOAD (twice), CEE.SCEERUN.

##### Inputs
Control members in &LBNM..CNTL: DB2FREE, DB2TIAD1, DB2CREAT, DB2TEP41, DB2LTTYP, DB2LTCAT (sources in app/app-transaction-type-db2/ctl).

##### Processing flow
1. FREEPLN: IKJEFT01, SYSTSIN=DB2FREE: `DSN SYSTEM(DAZ1)`, FREE PLAN(CARDDEMO), FREE PLAN(COTRTLIC), FREE PACKAGE(COTRTLIC.*). Ends RC 8 if not existing (comment says skip for new DB).
2. CRCRDDB: IKJEFT01, SYSTSIN=DB2TIAD1 (`RUN PROGRAM(DSNTIAD) PARMS('RC0')`), SYSIN=DB2CREAT: SET CURRENT SQLID='SYSADM'; CREATE DATABASE CARDDEMO STOGROUP AWST1STG BP0 CCSID EBCDIC; TABLESPACE CARDSPC1 (SEGSIZE 4, LOCKSIZE TABLE); TABLE CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE (TR_TYPE CHAR(2) NOT NULL PK, TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL); UNIQUE INDEX XTRAN_TYPE(TR_TYPE); GRANT DBADM/USE/DML TO PUBLIC; TABLESPACE CARDSTTC; TABLE CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY (TRC_TYPE_CODE CHAR(2), TRC_TYPE_CATEGORY CHAR(4), TRC_CAT_DATA VARCHAR(50), PK(code,category)); UNIQUE INDEX X_TRAN_TYPE_CATG; ALTER ADD FOREIGN KEY (TRC_TYPE_CODE) REFERENCES TRANSACTION_TYPE(TR_TYPE) ON DELETE RESTRICT; GRANT DML TO PUBLIC. (ddl/*.ddl hold equivalent standalone DDL.)
3. LDTTYPE: IEFBR14 COND=(0,NE) (no-op marker), then RUNTEP2: IKJEFT01 (no COND) DB2TEP41 (`RUN PROGRAM(DSNTEP4) PLAN(DSNTEP4) PARMS('/ALIGN(LHS) MIXED')`) with SYSIN DB2LTTYP: inserts 01 PURCHASE, 02 PAYMENT, 03 CREDIT, 04 AUTHORIZATION, 05 REFUND, 06 REVERAL, 07 ADJUSTMENT.
4. LDTCCAT: IKJEFT01 COND=(0,NE) DSNTEP4 SYSIN DB2LTCAT: 18 category rows (01/0001 REGULAR SALES DRAFT, 01/0002 REGULAR CASH ADVANCE, 01/0003 CONVENIENCE CHECK DEBIT, 01/0004 ATM CASH ADVANCE, 01/0005 INTEREST AMOUNT, 02/0001 CASH PAYMENT, 02/0002 ELECTRONIC PAYMENT, 02/0003 CHECK PAYMENT, 03/0001 CREDIT TO ACCOUNT, 03/0002 CREDIT TO PURCHASE BALANCE, 03/0003 CREDIT TO CASH BALANCE, 04/0001 ZERO DOLLAR AUTHORIZATION, 04/0002 ONLINE PURCHASE AUTHORIZATION, 04/0003 TRAVEL BOOKING AUTHORIZATION, 05/0001 REFUND CREDIT, 06/0001 FRAUD REVERSAL, 06/0002 NON FRAUD REVERSAL, 07/0001 SALES DRAFT CREDIT ADJUSTMENT).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[CREADB2 TYPRUN=SCAN] --> B[FREEPLN IKJEFT01 DB2FREE]
B --> C[CRCRDDB DSNTIAD DB2CREAT]
C --> D[LDTTYPE IEFBR14]
D --> E[RUNTEP2 DSNTEP4 DB2LTTYP]
E --> F[LDTCCAT DSNTEP4 DB2LTCAT COND 0,NE]
```

##### Data
Creates/loads CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE and CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY (layouts above; DCLGEN in dcl/DCLTRTYP.dcl and dcl/DCLTRCAT.dcl).

##### Outputs & side effects
DB2 objects in subsystem DAZ1; SYSOUT reports.

##### External calls
IKJEFT01 TSO batch -> DSN; DSNTIAD (dynamic DDL), DSNTEP4 (dynamic SQL); IEFBR14.

##### Migration notes
- COND=(0,NE) means a step is bypassed if any prior step RC<>0; FREEPLN RC 8 on new install will bypass LDTCCAT (and LDTTYPE's IEFBR14) - but RUNTEP2 has no COND so types load while categories do not.
- Seed data has typo 'REVERAL' for 06; keep or fix explicitly.
- GRANTs to PUBLIC; CCSID EBCDIC; LOCKSIZE TABLE.
- STEPLIB uses mixed OEM.DB2.DAZ1 and OEMA.DB2.VERSIONA libraries.
- REPROCT.ctl (`REPRO INFILE(FILEIN) OUTFILE(FILEOUT)`) is the IDCAMS card used by proc/REPROC.prc, not by this job.
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm intended step-condition behaviour on fresh installs and the REVERAL typo.

title: CODATE01 - MQ-triggered system date/time request-reply service
description:
##### Entry point
CICS program `CODATE01` (IS INITIAL) started by the MQ trigger monitor; `EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(MQTM)` obtains the trigger message (CMQTML). Transaction ID not defined in this batch.

##### Inputs
- MQTM trigger message: MQTM-QNAME = input queue name.
- Request messages (MQGET, buffer 1000): copied to REQUEST-MSG-COPY {WS-FUNC X(4), WS-KEY 9(11), filler X(985)} - content is not used.

##### Processing flow
1. 1000-CONTROL: blank names; 2100-OPEN-ERROR-QUEUE opens 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' (MQOO-OUTPUT+PASS-ALL-CONTEXT+FAIL-IF-QUIESCING); failure -> DISPLAY MQ-ERR-DISPLAY and terminate.
2. RETRIEVE: NORMAL -> input queue = MQTM-QNAME, reply queue = 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'; else 9000-ERROR (message 'RESP: '+resp1+resp2+'END') and terminate.
3. 2300 open input (INPUT-SHARED+SAVE-ALL-CONTEXT+FAIL-IF-QUIESCING); 2400 open reply queue (OUTPUT). Errors -> 9000-ERROR + 8000-TERMINATION.
4. 3000-GET-REQUEST: MQGET with SYNCPOINT+FAIL-IF-QUIESCING+CONVERT+WAIT 5000 ms. OK -> save MSGID/CORRELID/REPLYTOQ, 4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY, count+1. MQRC-NO-MSG-AVAILABLE -> NO-MORE-MSGS. Other -> 'INP MQGET ERR:' error and terminate.
5. Loop 4000-MAIN-PROCESS until NO-MORE-MSGS: CICS SYNCPOINT, then 3000-GET-REQUEST.
6. 4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY: ASKTIME, FORMATTIME MMDDYYYY with '-' and TIME with ':'; reply = 'SYSTEM DATE : '+MM-DD-YYYY+'SYSTEM TIME : '+HH:MM:SS (no separator between); 4100-PUT-REPLY: MQPUT to reply handle, MSGID/CORRELID = request's, FORMAT MQSTR, CCSID Q-MGR, SYNCPOINT+DEFAULT-CONTEXT; error -> 9000/8000.
7. 9000-ERROR: MQPUT MQ-ERR-DISPLAY (para X25, message X25, CC 9(2), RC 9(5), queue X48) to error queue; failure -> DISPLAY and terminate.
8. 8000-TERMINATION: close input (flag REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN), reply (RESP-QUEUE-OPEN), error queue; `EXEC CICS RETURN`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[CODATE01 1000-CONTROL] --> B[2100-OPEN-ERROR-QUEUE CARD.DEMO.ERROR]
B --> C[CICS RETRIEVE MQTM]
C -->|fail| E[9000-ERROR] --> T
C --> D[2300 open input / 2400 open CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE]
D --> G[3000-GET-REQUEST MQGET wait 5s]
G -->|msg| H[4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY ASKTIME FORMATTIME]
H --> I[4100-PUT-REPLY MQPUT]
I --> J[4000-MAIN-PROCESS SYNCPOINT]
J --> G
G -->|no msg| T[8000-TERMINATION MQCLOSE x3 RETURN]
```

##### Data
No files/DB. LIT-ACCTFILENAME 'ACCTDAT' declared but unused.

##### Outputs & side effects
Reply messages on CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE; error records on CARD.DEMO.ERROR; MQ units of work committed by CICS SYNCPOINT each loop iteration (last message committed at task end).

##### External calls
MQOPEN/MQGET/MQPUT/MQCLOSE (IBM MQ CICS adapter) with hconn 0; CICS RETRIEVE, ASKTIME, FORMATTIME, SYNCPOINT, RETURN.

##### Migration notes
- Reply goes to fixed queue, NOT MQMD-REPLYTOQ (saved but unused); request payload ignored.
- Correlation: reply MSGID and CORRELID copied from request.
- Flag names are swapped (input open sets REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN, output sets RESP-QUEUE-OPEN) but used consistently in termination.
- RESP2 display bug: WS-CICS-RESP2-CD moved to itself, so RESP2 shown as 0.
- MQ-MSG-COUNT has no VALUE (uninitialised display numeric) and is never output.
- Close failures recursively call 8000-TERMINATION (and 5200 calls 9000-ERROR on the queue being closed) - potential loop.
- 9000-ERROR reuses MQMD from last GET (message id may carry over).
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm transaction/trigger process definitions (outside batch) and whether replies should honour ReplyToQ.

title: CTTU / COTRTUPC - Transaction Type single-record maintain (lookup, add, update, delete)
description:
##### Entry point
CICS transaction `CTTU` -> `COTRTUPC` (CSD CRDDEMOD, DB2TRAN CTTUTRAN). Reached from COADM01C menu or PF02 on COTRTLIC. `HANDLE ABEND LABEL(ABEND-ROUTINE)` set first. Each turn returns `RETURN TRANSID('CTTU') COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA 2000 bytes)`.

##### Inputs
- Commarea: CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (COCOM01Y) + WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA: TTUP-CHANGE-ACTION X(1) state, TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE X(2)/DESC X(50) (values fetched from DB), TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE X(2)/DESC X(50) (values keyed).
- State codes: LOW-VALUES/space=details not fetched, 'K' invalid search key, 'X' not found, 'S' show details, 'R' create new, 'V' review new (never set), '9' confirm delete, '8' start delete, '7' delete done, '6' delete failed, 'E' changes not ok, 'N' changes ok not confirmed, 'L' lock error, 'F' update failed, 'C' done, 'B' backed out.
- Map `CTRTUPA`/mapset `COTRTUP`: TRTYPCDI X(2) type code, TRTYDSCI X(50) description; FKEYS/FKEY04/FKEY05/FKEY12 labels, INFOMSG, ERRMSG.

##### Processing flow
1. Init: EIBCALEN=0 or entered fresh from COADM01C/COTRTLIC (not reenter) -> clear commarea, PGM-ENTER, not-fetched. Else restore.
2. 0001-CHECK-PFKEYS valid: PF03; ENTER unless confirm-delete; PF04 in S or 9; PF05 in N, X or delete-in-progress; PF12 in N,S,X,9,R. Otherwise 'Invalid key pressed'.
3. Reset to not-fetched when: PF12 in S/R/X; state C; state F/L; B with no old details; 7; 6.
4. Main EVALUATE:
   - PF03: target caller (default CA00/COADM01C), SYNCPOINT, XCTL.
   - Fresh entry from admin/list or PGM-ENTER+not-fetched: send blank map, set REENTER.
   - PF04 + '9': state '8', 9800-DELETE-PROCESSING, send.
   - PF04 + 'S': state '9' (ask 'Delete this record ? Press F4 to confirm').
   - PF05 + 'X': state 'R' (enter new details).
   - PF05 + 'N': 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING.
   - PF12 + N/9/S: FOUND flag on, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION (cancel).
   - Invalid key: resend.
   - OTHER: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION, send.
5. 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS: RECEIVE MAP; 1150 stores input in NEW (skip if state X, not PF05 and same code; '*' or spaces -> LOW-VALUES; else TRIM); 1200 edits: state X with same code -> back to not-fetched unless PF05; unless R/N: 1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE (1245 numeric-required len 2: blank -> 'Tran Type code must be supplied.', TEST-NUMVAL fail -> 'must be numeric.', zero -> 'must not be zero.'; valid -> NUMVAL to 9(2), zero-padded e.g. '5 '->'05'); blank -> 'No input received'; invalid -> 'K'. Then 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW (upper-case trimmed compare) -> no change: 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' Changes -> state 'E', 1230 alnum-required desc edit (same rules as COTRTLIC); OK -> 'N' ('Changes validated.Press F5 to save').
6. 2000-DECIDE-ACTION: not-fetched or PF12 -> if key valid 9000-READ-TRANTYPE (`SELECT TR_TYPE,TR_DESCRIPTION ... WHERE TR_TYPE=:code`; 0 found -> 'S'; +100 -> 'No record found for this key in database', state 'X' with prompt 'Press F05 to add. F12 to cancel'; <0 -> 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:..'); else PF12 in '9' -> 'Delete was cancelled', in 'N' -> 'Update was cancelled' + 'B'. '9'+PF12 stays; 'S' -> 'N' unless error/no change/invalid key; 'E' stays; 'B' -> 'E'; 'K' stays; PF05+'X' -> 'R'; 'N' stays; 'C' -> 'S' (if FROM-TRANID blank zero ACCT-ID/CARD-NUM); OTHER -> ABEND-ROUTINE code '0001' 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'.
7. 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING (upsert): `UPDATE ... SET TR_DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE`; 0 -> SYNCPOINT; +100 -> 9700-INSERT-RECORD `INSERT (TR_TYPE,TR_DESCRIPTION)` (0 -> SYNCPOINT, else 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table...'); -911 -> 'Could not lock record for update' -> 'L'; <0 -> 'Update of record failed' message replaced by 'Error updating:...' -> 'F'; otherwise 'C' ('Changes committed to database').
8. 9800-DELETE-PROCESSING: `DELETE ... WHERE TR_TYPE = old code`; 0 -> '7' + SYNCPOINT ('Delete successful.'); -532 -> message 'Please delete associated child records first:SQLCODE :..' (state stays '8'); other -> '6' 'Delete failed with message:...'.
9. 3000-SEND-MAP: header, values (old vs new by state), info message (centred 40), attributes (code field unprotected in not-fetched/K/X; desc unprotected in S/E/R/B; red on invalid key, '*' on blank), PF-key label brightness per state, SEND MAP ERASE CURSOR FREEKB.
10. ABEND-ROUTINE: SEND ABEND-DATA, HANDLE ABEND CANCEL, ABEND ABCODE (code '9999' overwrites).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[CTTU COTRTUPC 0000-MAIN] --> B[HANDLE ABEND]
B --> C[restore/init commarea]
C --> D[0001-CHECK-PFKEYS]
D --> E{EVALUATE}
E -->|PF03| F[SYNCPOINT XCTL caller/COADM01C]
E -->|PF04 state 9| G[9800-DELETE-PROCESSING DELETE]
E -->|PF04 state S| H[state 9 confirm]
E -->|PF05 state X| I[state R new]
E -->|PF05 state N| J[9600-WRITE-PROCESSING UPDATE]
J -->|+100| K[9700-INSERT-RECORD INSERT]
E -->|other| L[1000-PROCESS-INPUTS edits]
L --> M[2000-DECIDE-ACTION]
M --> N[9000-READ-TRANTYPE SELECT]
G --> O[3000-SEND-MAP]
H --> O
I --> O
J --> O
K --> O
M --> O
O --> P[RETURN TRANSID CTTU]
```

##### Data
DB2 `CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE` (TR_TYPE CHAR(2) PK, TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50)): SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE. DCLTRCAT (TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY) is included but not referenced in SQL.

##### Outputs & side effects
Map CTRTUPA; DB2 changes committed by SYNCPOINT; XCTL to caller on PF03; abend with screen dump on unexpected state.

##### External calls
CICS RECEIVE/SEND MAP, SYNCPOINT, XCTL (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), ABEND. No DSNTIAC; SQLERRM used directly in messages.

##### Migration notes
- Add is implicit: PF05 on not-found goes to 'R'; save does UPDATE then INSERT on +100 (upsert).
- Type code normalised via NUMVAL so ' 5'/'5 ' becomes '05'; zero rejected.
- In 9800 the -532 branch does not set TTUP-DELETE-FAILED (state remains '8'), unlike other errors.
- -532 message concatenates SQLERRM twice. 9600: 'Update of record failed' 88 set but overwritten by STRING; DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE is never set (dead branch); there is no optimistic concurrency check despite the message.
- DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN = length of untrimmed 50-byte field (always 50).
- 9500 moves DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT(1:LEN) - relies on DB2 length.
- 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES moves LOW-VALUES to TRTYPCDO twice (desc not cleared).
- State 'V' TTUP-REVIEW-NEW-RECORD and CODING-TO-BE-DONE are never set (dead).
- 9100 +100 sets INPUT-ERROR; DECIDE-ACTION then branches on FOUND flag.
recommendation: Fully documented. Customer should confirm upsert semantics and whether optimistic-locking message should be implemented.

Additional migration notes folded from duplicates:
- Duplicate inserts**: the INSERT error path does not handle −803.
- Stored description length**: the length is set from the untrimmed field (50), so the stored VARCHAR is space-padded to 50.
- Abend code**: the '0001' set in 2000 is overwritten by '9999' in ABEND-ROUTINE.

- Unresolved**: the details of the screen-attribute paragraphs (3000–3400) were not traced line by line. They set field protection, colors, and the info message for each state.

title: CTLI / COTRTLIC - Transaction Type list, filter, page, inline update and delete (DB2 CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE)
description:
##### Entry point
CICS transaction `CTLI` -> program `COTRTLIC` (CSD `CRDDEMOD.csd`, DB2TRAN CTLITRAN -> DB2ENTRY CARDDEMO, PLAN CARDDEMO). Reached by XCTL from admin menu `COADM01C` (option listed in `COADM02Y` as COTRTLIC) or from `COTRTUPC` on PF03. Pseudo-conversational: every turn ends with `EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CTLI') COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA) LENGTH(2000)`.

##### Inputs
- DFHCOMMAREA = `CARDDEMO-COMMAREA` (COCOM01Y) followed by `WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA`: WS-CA-TYPE-CD X(2) (last type filter), WS-CA-TYPE-DESC X(50) (last desc filter), WS-CA-ALL-ROWS-OUT X(364) = 7 x {TR-CODE X(2), TR-DESC X(50)} (rows currently on screen), WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED S9(4) COMP, WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE X(2), WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE X(2), WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM 9(1) (1=first page), WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED 9(1) (0 shown / 9 not shown), WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND X ('Y' exists / LOW-VALUES not), WS-CA-DELETE-FLAG X ('Y' requested, LOW-VALUES = not requested = succeeded), WS-CA-UPDATE-FLAG X (same convention).
- Map `CTRTLIA` of mapset `COTRTLI` (symbolic map COTRTLI.cpy, redefined in-program as 7 rows): header filters TRTYPEI X(2) (type code), TRDESCI X(50) (description); per row TRTSELI X(1) (action D/U), TRTTYPI X(2), TRTYPDI X(50) (editable description).
- AID key via `YYYY-STORE-PFKEY` (CSSTRPFY): PF13-24 fold onto PF1-12.

##### Processing flow
1. 0000-MAIN: INITIALIZE work areas. If EIBCALEN=0: fresh commarea, FROM-TRANID/PROGRAM=CTLI/COTRTLIC, USRTYP admin, PGM-ENTER, first page. Else split DFHCOMMAREA into CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + program area.
2. If (PGM-ENTER and FROM-PROGRAM<>COTRTLIC) or (PF03 and FROM-TRANID=CTTU): reset program area, force ENTER, first page.
3. If EIBCALEN>0 and FROM-PROGRAM=COTRTLIC: 1000-RECEIVE-MAP = 1100-RECEIVE-SCREEN (rows: description '*' or spaces -> LOW-VALUES, else TRIM) then 1200-EDIT-INPUTS: 1210-EDIT-ARRAY, 1230-EDIT-DESC, 1220-EDIT-TYPECD, 1290-CROSS-EDITS.
   - 1210: if either filter changed, clear selections and exit. Else tally blanks/'D'/'U' across 7 select flags; ACTIONS-REQUESTED = 7 - blanks; loop rows 7..1: D/U -> remember I-SELECTED (ends as lowest selected row), if >1 action mark row error; U -> 1211 (compare trimmed upper-case desc vs commarea row; equal => 'No change detected with respect to database values.'; else 1240 alnum-required edit of 50 chars: blank -> 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.', non alnum (anything other than A-Z a-z 0-9, spaces allowed after convert) -> 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.'). Other non-blank code -> INPUT-ERROR 'Action code selected is invalid'. Row selection changed if I-SELECTED<>WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED. >1 action -> 'Please select only 1 action'.
   - 1220: blank/spaces/zeros -> filter blank (WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER='00'); non-numeric -> error 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', protect rows; else filter valid. Exit logic: if value differs from commarea value -> reset paging, store, CHANGED-YES.
   - 1230: non-blank -> filter valid, WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER = '%'||TRIM(desc)||'%'; changed detection same pattern.
   - 1290: if any filter valid -> 9100-CHECK-FILTERS `SELECT COUNT(1)` with same predicates; count 0 -> INPUT-ERROR, filters NOT-OK, protect rows, 'No Records found for these filter conditions'. SQL error -> INPUT-ERROR + DSNTIAC message.
4. PF validity: valid = ENTER, PF02, PF03, PF07, PF08, PF10 when delete/update requested; else treated as ENTER.
5. PF03: target = FROM-TRANID/PROGRAM unless blank or self -> CA00/COADM01C; SYNCPOINT; XCTL with CARDDEMO-COMMAREA.
6. PF02 with FROM-PROGRAM=self: set USRTYP-USER (note: not admin), PGM-ENTER, XCTL to `COTRTUPC` (add/maintain screen).
7. Non-PF08 -> last-page-not-shown. PF10 is downgraded to ENTER unless a delete/update is pending and neither filters nor row selection changed.
8. 9998-PRIMING-QUERY (`SELECT 1 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1`); failure -> SEND TEXT of WS-LONG-MSG (800) and plain `CICS RETURN` (ends conversation).
9. EVALUATE (first match wins):
   - INPUT-ERROR: re-read forward from first code (only if no filter NOT-OK), send map.
   - PF07 and first page: read forward from first code, send (message 'No previous pages to display').
   - PF03 / reentry from other program: reset and show page 1.
   - PF08 and next page exists: start key = last code, screen-num+1, read forward, clear selections.
   - PF07 not first page: screen-num-1, 8100-READ-BACKWARDS from first code, clear selections.
   - ENTER with deletes>0: redisplay (row highlighted, 'Delete HIGHLIGHTED row ? Press F10 to confirm').
   - PF10 with deletes>0: 9300-DELETE-RECORD; on success reset commarea after sending map.
   - ENTER with updates>0: redisplay ('Update HIGHLIGHTED row. Press F10 to save').
   - PF10 with updates>0: 9200-UPDATE-RECORD, re-read forward, send.
   - OTHER: read forward from first code, send.
10. COMMON-RETURN: write back commarea and RETURN TRANSID CTLI.

8000-READ-FORWARD: clear rows, OPEN C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD, FETCH up to 7 rows; row 1 sets FIRST-TR-CODE (screen-num 0->1); after 7th row does one look-ahead FETCH: found -> next page exists, LAST-TR-CODE = look-ahead code (so next page starts at >= the 8th row); +100 -> no next page. +100 before 7 rows -> no next page; page 1 with 0 rows -> 'No records found for this search condition.'. CLOSE cursor.
8100-READ-BACKWARDS: OPEN C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD (TR_TYPE < first code ORDER BY DESC) and fill rows 7 down to 1; row 1 sets FIRST-TR-CODE. Any non-zero SQLCODE (incl. +100) ends loop and sets WS-DB2-ERROR.
9200-UPDATE-RECORD: `UPDATE CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE SET TR_DESCRIPTION=:desc WHERE TR_TYPE=:code` for row I-SELECTED; 0 -> SYNCPOINT, success; +100 -> 'Record not found. Deleted by others ?'; -911 -> 'Deadlock. Someone else updating ?' + INPUT-ERROR; <0 -> 'Update failed with'.
9300-DELETE-RECORD: `DELETE ... WHERE TR_TYPE=:code`; 0 -> SYNCPOINT; -532 (RI restrict from TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY) -> 'Please delete associated child records first:'; other -> 'Delete failed with message:'.
2000-SEND-MAP: 2100 header (titles, CTLI, COTRTLIC, date MM/DD/YY, time, PAGENO), 2200 row attributes (empty rows or protect flag -> select protected; error rows red + cursor; selected delete row neutral; selected update row desc unprotected, red if invalid), 2300 move rows to screen (desc shows input when changed, '*' if blank), 2400 filter field attrs, 2500 info/error messages (info centred in 45 chars), 2600 SEND MAP ERASE CURSOR FREEKB.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[CTLI COTRTLIC 0000-MAIN] --> B{EIBCALEN=0?}
B -->|yes| C[Init commarea first page]
B -->|no| D[Restore commarea]
```

##### Data
- DB2 `CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE` (DCLTRTYP): TR_TYPE CHAR(2) PK, TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50) (host vars DCL-TR-TYPE X(2), DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN S9(4) COMP + TEXT X(50)). Read via cursors C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD (`TR_TYPE >= :WS-START-KEY` + optional `TR_TYPE = :filter` when WS-EDIT-TYPE-FLAG='1' + optional `TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE TRIM(:desc-filter)` when WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAG='1', ORDER BY TR_TYPE) and C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD (`<`, DESC); COUNT(1) check; UPDATE; DELETE. `SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1` priming.
- Implicit child `CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY` via FK ON DELETE RESTRICT.

##### Outputs & side effects
Map CTRTLIA sends; DB2 update/delete committed with `EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT`; XCTL to COADM01C/COTRTUPC/caller; SEND TEXT on DB2 connectivity failure.

##### External calls
- `DSNTIAC` (via 9999-FORMAT-DB2-MESSAGE in CSDB2RPY): CALL USING DFHEIBLK, DFHCOMMAREA, SQLCA, WS-DSNTIAC-FORMATTED (len 720 + 10x72 text), LRECL 72; returns formatted SQLCA text; message = action + ' SQLCODE:' + edited SQLCODE (----9) + text into WS-LONG-MSG and WS-RETURN-MSG (truncated to 75).
- XCTL COADM01C / COTRTUPC / CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM with CARDDEMO-COMMAREA only (program area not passed).

##### Migration notes
- Page size 7 (WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES); WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM is PIC 9(1) so page counter wraps after 9.
- Paging key semantics: next page starts at the look-ahead (8th) row code, not after last displayed row. Backward read treats +100 as DB2 error (WS-DB2-ERROR) - fewer than 7 previous rows leaves leading rows LOW-VALUES and flags error.
- Description filter is substring LIKE '%x%' case-sensitive; type filter of '00' treated as blank.
- CA-DELETE-SUCCEEDED and CA-DELETE-NOT-REQUESTED share LOW-VALUES (same for update) - success and 'not requested' are indistinguishable.
- Only lowest-numbered selected row is acted on (loop runs 7->1).
- The alnum edit rejects punctuation and the description update stores TRIM(text) but sets LEN = FUNCTION LENGTH of the untrimmed 50-byte field, so DB2 VARCHAR gets 50 bytes (trailing spaces padded).
- In 9300 'other' branch neither delete flag nor error flag is set.
- PF02 sets CDEMO-USRTYP-USER before XCTL to COTRTUPC (inconsistent with admin flows).
- Error after delete SQL uses WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard: only first message wins. 1220 exit paragraph contains logic (code after the -EXIT label executes).
- Priming-query failure ends the task without TRANSID (conversation lost).
recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm whether the PIC 9(1) page counter wrap and the VARCHAR length padding are acceptable to replicate.

title: Control-M schedule: DAILY transaction backup, WEEKLY DB2 type/disclosure refresh, MONTHLY interest calculation sequences
description:
##### Entry point
Control-M definition table `app/scheduler/CardDemo.controlm` (XML DEFTABLE, Folder.xsd). It defines three regular folders and two SMART folders (TYPE=2). Every job is TASKTYPE=Job and APPL_TYPE=OS, and MEMNAME names the JCL member that gets submitted. Common attributes on all jobs: APPLICATION=CARD-DEMO, MAXWAIT=7 days, MAXRERUN=5, TIMETO=23:00 (no TIMEFROM), CYCLIC=0, RULE_BASED_CALENDARS NAME="*", ODATE=ODAT on all conditions.

##### Inputs
The only inputs are Control-M conditions and calendars. No data parameters are passed. The scheduling inputs are:
- `DAILY-TransactionBackup` folder: each job has DAYS="ALL".
- `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh` folder (job MNTTRDB2): no DAYS attribute on the job.
- SMART folders `WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh` and `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh`: DAYS="SA" (Saturday), INTERVAL=00005M, SHIFT="Ignore Job", DATACENTER=PROD, PLATFORM=UNIX, SITE_STANDARD_NAME=CARD-DEMO-STANDARD. The jobs inside them have no DAYS.
- `MONTHLY-InterestCalculation` folder: no DAYS or MONTHDAYS attribute on any job.

##### Processing flow
In the tables below, an OUTCOND with + adds a condition and one with - deletes it. The `|` separates a condition name from its sign.

**DAILY-TransactionBackup** (runs every day):
| # | JOB/MEMNAME | INCOND | OUTCOND |
|---|---|---|---|
|1|CLOSEFIL|-|+DAILY-TransactionBackup-CLOSEFIL|
|2|TRANBKP|CLOSEFIL|-CLOSEFIL, +TRANBKP|
|3|WAITSTEP|TRANBKP|-TRANBKP, +WAITSTEP|
|4|OPENFIL|WAITSTEP|-WAITSTEP|

What each member does (from app/jcl):
- CLOSEFIL: runs PGM=SDSF to issue `/F CICSAWSA,'CEMT SET FIL(x) CLO'` for TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX and USRSEC.
- TRANBKP:
  - STEP05R runs PROC REPROC (IDCAMS with SYSIN from AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL(REPROCT)). It copies AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS to the new GDG generation TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), defined with LRECL=350 and RECFM=FB.
  - STEP05 deletes the TRANSACT KSDS cluster and the TRANSACT AIX. `IF MAXCC LE 08 THEN SET MAXCC=0` follows each delete.
  - STEP10 runs with COND=(4,LT). It redefines an empty KSDS with KEYS(16 0), RECORDSIZE(350 350) and SHAREOPTIONS(2 3).
- WAITSTEP: runs PGM=COBSWAIT with SYSIN `00003600`, which is centiseconds (36 seconds). COBSWAIT moves the value to MVSWAIT-TIME and calls MVSWAIT.
- OPENFIL: issues CEMT OPE for the same 5 files.

**WEEKLY**:
- Folder `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh` contains one job, MNTTRDB2. It sets +WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2. MNTTRDB2.jcl (app/app-transaction-type-db2/jcl) runs IKJEFT01 with `DSN SYSTEM(DAZ1) RUN PROGRAM(COBTUPDT) PLAN(CARDDEMO)` and DD INPFILE.
- SMART folder `WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh` (DAYS=SA) runs this chain:
  - CLOSEFIL waits on INCOND MNTTRDB2 and sets +DisclosureGroupsRefresh-CLOSEFIL.
  - DISCGRP waits on CLOSEFIL, then deletes CLOSEFIL and sets +DISCGRP. DISCGRP.jcl uses IDCAMS to DELETE and DEFINE AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS, then REPRO from DISCGRP.PS.
  - WAITSTEP waits on DISCGRP, then deletes DISCGRP and sets +WAITSTEP.
  - OPENFIL waits on WAITSTEP, then deletes WAITSTEP.
  - When the folder ends, it deletes the MNTTRDB2 condition (line 55).
- SMART folder `WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh` (DAYS=SA) runs TRANEXTR, which waits on INCOND MNTTRDB2. When the folder ends, it also deletes the MNTTRDB2 condition (line 62). TRANEXTR.jcl steps:
  - IEBGENER backs up &HLQ..TRANTYPE.PS to BKUP(+1).
  - IEBGENER backs up TRANCATG.PS to PS.BKUP(+1), with COND=(0,NE).
  - IEFBR14 deletes both PS files.
  - IKJEFT01 runs DSNTIAUL to unload DB2 into a new TRANTYPE.PS. A STEP50 follows with COND=(4,LT).

**MONTHLY-InterestCalculation**:
| # | JOB | INCOND | OUTCOND |
|---|---|---|---|
|1|CLOSEFIL|-|+CLOSEFIL|
|2|INTCALC|CLOSEFIL|-CLOSEFIL, +INTCALC|
|3|COMBTRAN|INTCALC|-INTCALC, +COMBTRAN|
|4|WAITSTEP|COMBTRAN|-COMBTRAN, +WAITSTEP|
|4 (dup JOBISN)|OPENFIL|WAITSTEP|-WAITSTEP|

What each member does:
- INTCALC: runs CBACT04C with PARM='2022071800'. It reads TCATBALF, CARDXREF (KSDS and AIX PATH), ACCTDATA and DISCGRP, and writes SYSTRAN(+1).
- COMBTRAN:
  - STEP05R runs SORT on TRANSACT.BKUP(0) plus SYSTRAN(0), `SORT FIELDS=(TRAN-ID,A)`, and writes TRANSACT.COMBINED(+1).
  - STEP10 runs IDCAMS `REPRO INFILE(TRANSACT) OUTFILE(TRANVSAM)` to load COMBINED(+1) into TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph DAILY[DAILY-TransactionBackup DAYS=ALL]
    D1[CLOSEFIL SDSF CEMT CLO] -->|DAILY-TransactionBackup-CLOSEFIL| D2[TRANBKP REPROC->TRANSACT.BKUP+1; delete/redefine TRANSACT KSDS]
    D2 -->|-TRANBKP| D3[WAITSTEP COBSWAIT 3600cs]
    D3 -->|-WAITSTEP| D4[OPENFIL SDSF CEMT OPE]
  end
  subgraph WEEKLY
    W0[MNTTRDB2 IKJEFT01 COBTUPDT PLAN CARDDEMO] -->|WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh-MNTTRDB2| W1[SMART WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh DAYS=SA]
    W0 -->|same cond| W5[SMART WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh DAYS=SA: TRANEXTR]
    W1 --> C1[CLOSEFIL] --> C2[DISCGRP] --> C3[WAITSTEP] --> C4[OPENFIL]
    C4 --> X1[folder end: -MNTTRDB2]
    W5 --> X2[folder end: -MNTTRDB2]
  end
  subgraph MONTHLY[MONTHLY-InterestCalculation]
    M1[CLOSEFIL] --> M2[INTCALC CBACT04C PARM 2022071800] --> M3[COMBTRAN SORT BKUP0+SYSTRAN0 -> REPRO TRANSACT KSDS] --> M4[WAITSTEP] --> M5[OPENFIL]
  end
```

##### Data
The scheduler table itself reads and writes no data. Its members touch these datasets:
- AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS: key at offset 0, length 16; record length 350.
- AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.
- GDGs TRANSACT.BKUP, SYSTRAN and TRANSACT.COMBINED.
- DISCGRP.PS and DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS.
- TCATBALF, CARDXREF and ACCTDATA VSAM files.
- &HLQ..TRANTYPE.PS and TRANCATG.PS, plus their BKUP GDGs.
- The DB2 subsystem DAZ1, plan CARDDEMO.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Control-M conditions are added and deleted, as listed in the tables above.
- CICS region CICSAWSA has its files closed and later reopened.
- The transaction master is backed up and then emptied every day.
- Each month, system interest transactions are appended into the transaction master.

##### External calls
- SDSF operator commands (CEMT) against CICS region CICSAWSA.
- IDCAMS, SORT, IEBGENER and IEFBR14.
- COBSWAIT, which calls MVSWAIT.
- CBACT04C.
- The DB2 programs COBTUPDT and DSNTIAUL, run via IKJEFT01.

##### Migration notes
- Daily, TRANBKP deletes and redefines TRANSACT as an empty file, and nothing in the daily folder reloads it or rebuilds the TRANSACT AIX (TRANIDX is not scheduled anywhere). The online system therefore reopens an empty TRANSACT file. The monthly COMBTRAN reloads it from BKUP(0) plus SYSTRAN(0), but the monthly folder also has no TRANIDX step, so the AIX is never rebuilt.
- The monthly folder has no TRANBKP step. COMBTRAN reads BKUP(0), which is whatever the last daily run produced. Whether that is correct depends on the daily and monthly runs happening in the right order on the same day; no cross-folder condition enforces that.
- The MONTHLY folder jobs, the WEEKLY regular-folder job MNTTRDB2, and the jobs inside the SMART folders have no DAYS/MONTHDAYS. When MONTHLY and MNTTRDB2 actually run is not defined in this file; it must come from external ordering. Only the SMART folders (DAYS=SA) and the DAILY jobs (DAYS=ALL) have explicit days.
- Two folders have the same name, WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh: the regular folder at line 26 and the SMART folder at line 57 (FOLDER_NAME). Both SMART folders also give PARENT_FOLDER=WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh. TRANEXTR's PARENT_FOLDER is WEEKLY-DisclosureGroupsRefresh, which does not match its enclosing folder. The import behavior is ambiguous.
- Both SMART folders wait on the same INCOND (MNTTRDB2) and both delete it when they end. They run in parallel, not in sequence.
- In MONTHLY, JOBISN=4 is used twice (WAITSTEP and OPENFIL).
- TIMETO=23:00 has no TIMEFROM, so a job may start any time from ordering until 23:00. MAXRERUN=5 allows automatic reruns: a rerun of TRANBKP creates another BKUP(+1) generation, and a rerun of COMBTRAN re-REPROs into a non-empty KSDS, which can give duplicate-key errors.
- INTCALC's processing date is hard-coded as PARM '2022071800'. It is not derived from ODATE.
- CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL handle only 5 CICS files (TRANSACT, CCXREF, ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, USRSEC). Other files, such as card or customer data or DISCGRP, are not closed, even in the DISCGRP refresh.
- The ODATE=ODAT conditions are date-scoped, so dependencies do not carry across order dates.
recommendation: Fully documented. Customer input needed: the actual run calendar for MONTHLY and MNTTRDB2 (no DAYS defined), whether the duplicate folder name WEEKLY-TransactionTypesDBRefresh is intended, and whether the daily emptying of TRANSACT without a reload or TRANIDX is the intended production behavior.

title: remote_refresh.sh: FTP/JES-submitted full master-data refresh (11 reload jobs bracketed by CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL)
description:
##### Entry point
The operator runs `scripts/remote_refresh.sh` manually, with no arguments.

##### Inputs
- JCL is read from the relative path `jcl/`.
- An FTP tunnel must be listening on localhost:2121.

##### Processing flow
1. Tunnel guard (the same as in the other scripts).
2. It runs tnftp, then `pwd`, then `quote site filetype=JES`.
3. Jobs are submitted in this order:
   - Job 1 CLOSEFIL, followed by sleep 5.
   - Job 2 ACCTFILE.
   - Job 3 CARDFILE.
   - Job 4 XREFFILE.
   - Job 5 CUSTFILE.
   - Job 6 TRANFILE. Its own SDSF step closes the CICS files. It then deletes and defines the TRANSACT KSDS, REPROs AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT into it, and defines and builds the AIX and PATH.
   - Job 7 DISCGRP.
   - Job 8 TCATBALF.
   - Job 9 TRANCATG.
   - Job 10 TRANTYPE.
   - Job 11 DUSRSECJ: IEFBR14 deletes USRSEC.PS, IEBGENER writes it from instream data, and IDCAMS deletes, defines and REPROs the USRSEC KSDS.
   - The script echoes "Data Refresh Complete" and sleeps 5.
   - "Job 11" again (duplicate label): OPENFIL.
4. `bye`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[remote_refresh.sh] --> G{tunnel 2121?}
  G -- no --> X[exit]
  G -- yes --> F[tnftp JES mode]
  F --> C[CLOSEFIL] --> S[sleep 5] --> R1[ACCTFILE] --> R2[CARDFILE] --> R3[XREFFILE] --> R4[CUSTFILE] --> R5[TRANFILE] --> R6[DISCGRP] --> R7[TCATBALF] --> R8[TRANCATG] --> R9[TRANTYPE] --> R10[DUSRSECJ] --> S2[sleep 5] --> O[OPENFIL] --> B[bye]
```

##### Data
Every seed PS file is loaded into its corresponding VSAM KSDS under AWS.M2.CARDDEMO:
- ACCTDATA, CARDDATA, CARDXREF and CUSTDATA.
- TRANSACT, loaded from DALYTRAN.PS.INIT.
- DISCGRP, TCATBALF, TRANCATG, TRANTYPE and USRSEC.

##### Outputs & side effects
All master files are reset to seed data, and CICS files are closed and then reopened.

##### External calls
- tnftp JES submission.
- ps, grep and sleep.

##### Migration notes
- This differs from run_full_batch.sh: it uses TRANFILE (reload from DALYTRAN.PS.INIT, including the AIX) instead of TRANBKP, and it includes TRANCATG.
- After CLOSEFIL there is only one 5-second sleep. The reload jobs are queued back to back, and OPENFIL is queued only 5 seconds after the last submission. OPENFIL can therefore run before the reloads finish.
- No RC checking is done.
- The "Job 11" label is used twice.
recommendation: Fully documented.

title: run_posting.sh: FTP/JES-submitted daily posting cycle (ACCTFILE, TCATBALF, TRANBKP, POSTTRAN, TRANIDX)
description:
##### Entry point
The operator runs `scripts/run_posting.sh` manually, with no arguments.

##### Inputs
Same as run_full_batch.sh:
- JCL is read from the relative path `jcl/`.
- An FTP tunnel must be listening on localhost:2121.
- tnftp supplies the credentials.

##### Processing flow
1. Tunnel guard, identical to the other scripts: if `ps f | grep -c "2121:"` returns 1, it prints a message and exits with status 0.
2. It runs `tnftp localhost 2121`, then `pwd`, then `quote site filetype=JES`.
3. Jobs are submitted in this order:
   - Job 1 CLOSEFIL, followed by sleep 5.
   - Job 2 ACCTFILE: reloads the account master from ACCTDATA.PS, resetting balances to the seed data.
   - Job 3 TCATBALF: reloads the category-balance file.
   - Job 4 "Refresh Transaction Master", which actually runs TRANBKP. It backs up TRANSACT to BKUP(+1), then deletes and redefines it empty and deletes the AIX.
   - Job 5 POSTTRAN (CBTRN02C), followed by sleep 10.
   - Job 6 TRANIDX: defines the AIX (KEYS 26 304) and the PATH, then runs BLDINDEX. Followed by sleep 5.
   - Job 7 OPENFIL.
4. `bye`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[run_posting.sh] --> G{tunnel 2121 running?}
  G -- no --> X[echo; exit]
  G -- yes --> F[tnftp; quote site filetype=JES]
  F --> J1[CLOSEFIL] --> S1[sleep 5] --> J2[ACCTFILE] --> J3[TCATBALF] --> J4[TRANBKP] --> J5[POSTTRAN CBTRN02C] --> S2[sleep 10] --> J6[TRANIDX] --> S3[sleep 5] --> J7[OPENFIL] --> B[bye]
```

##### Data
- ACCTDATA.PS loaded into the ACCTDATA KSDS.
- The TCATBALF file.
- The TRANSACT KSDS, its AIX and PATH, and the BKUP GDG.
- DALYTRAN.PS, read by POSTTRAN.
- CARDXREF, read by POSTTRAN.
- DALYREJS(+1), written by POSTTRAN.

##### Outputs & side effects
The account and category-balance masters are reset to seed data, and the daily transactions are posted into an emptied TRANSACT file. Its alternate index is then rebuilt.

##### External calls
- tnftp JES submission.
- ps, grep and sleep.

##### Migration notes
- Like the full batch, this script is not a pure posting step. It first resets ACCTDATA and TCATBALF from their PS seeds and empties TRANSACT, so every run starts from seed balances. Card, xref and customer files are not refreshed.
- Ordering depends only on sleeps, and no RC is checked. If ACCTFILE, TCATBALF or TRANBKP are still running when POSTTRAN starts, POSTTRAN may fail or post against partially loaded files.
- The step label "Refresh Transaction Master" does not match the member it runs (TRANBKP).
- Compared with run_full_batch.sh, this script adds no INTCALC, COMBTRAN or second TRANBKP.
- The guard exits with code 0 when the tunnel is absent.
recommendation: Fully documented. Customer should confirm whether the master-file resets before posting are intended outside demo use.

title: run_full_batch.sh: FTP/JES-submitted full batch cycle (refresh, POSTTRAN, INTCALC, backup, combine, AIX rebuild)
description:
##### Entry point
The operator runs the bash script `scripts/run_full_batch.sh` manually, with no arguments. This is an alternative to Control-M sequencing.

##### Inputs
- JCL members are read from the relative path `jcl/*.jcl`. Because of that relative path, the script must be run from a directory that has a `jcl/` subfolder, such as `app/`.
- An FTP tunnel must be listening on localhost:2121. The comments say it reaches the "Ensono" mainframe.
- FTP credentials come from tnftp's own mechanism (~/.netrc or autologin). The script does not set them.

##### Processing flow
1. Guard: `ps f | grep -c "2121:"`. A count of 1 means only the grep process itself matched. In that case the script prints "FTP Tunnel to Ensono not running." and exits with status 0.
2. It opens `tnftp localhost 2121` with a here-doc, runs `pwd`, then `quote site filetype=JES`. That switches FTP into JES mode: every `put` submits the file as a batch job.
3. Jobs are submitted in this order. The echoed label is shown, followed by the actual member and what it does:
   - Job 1 CLOSEFIL: CEMT closes 5 CICS files. The script then sleeps 5 seconds.
   - Job 2 ACCTFILE: delete, define and REPRO ACCTDATA.PS into ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS.
   - Job 3 CARDFILE.
   - Job 4 XREFFILE.
   - Job 5 CUSTFILE.
   - Job 6 "Refresh Transaction Data", which actually submits TRANBKP.jcl, not TRANFILE. It backs up TRANSACT to BKUP(+1), then deletes and redefines an empty TRANSACT KSDS and deletes the AIX.
   - Job 7 DISCGRP.
   - Job 8 TCATBALF.
   - Job 9 TRANTYPE.
   - Job 11 DUSRSECJ (user security PS and VSAM rebuild). There is no Job 10, and TRANCATG is not submitted.
   - The script echoes "Data Refresh Complete" and sleeps 5 seconds.
   - Job 12 POSTTRAN: CBTRN02C posts DALYTRAN.PS into TRANSACT, ACCTDATA and TCATBALF, and writes rejects to DALYREJS(+1). The script sleeps 10 seconds.
   - Job 13 INTCALC: CBACT04C with PARM 2022071800 writes SYSTRAN(+1). The script sleeps 5 seconds.
   - Job 14 TRANBKP again: the posted transactions go to BKUP(+1) and TRANSACT is emptied.
   - Job 15 COMBTRAN: SORT BKUP(0) plus SYSTRAN(0) by TRAN-ID, write COMBINED(+1), then REPRO it into TRANSACT KSDS. The script sleeps 5 seconds.
   - "Job 15" again (duplicate label) TRANIDX: DEFINE AIX TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX with KEYS(26 304), NONUNIQUEKEY and UPGRADE; DEFINE PATH; then BLDINDEX. The script sleeps 5 seconds.
   - Job 16 OPENFIL: CEMT reopens the files.
4. `bye`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[run_full_batch.sh] --> G{ps f grep -c 2121: == 1?}
  G -- yes --> X[echo tunnel not running; exit]
  G -- no --> F[tnftp localhost 2121; quote site filetype=JES]
  F --> J1[put CLOSEFIL] --> S1[sleep 5] --> J2[ACCTFILE] --> J3[CARDFILE] --> J4[XREFFILE] --> J5[CUSTFILE] --> J6[TRANBKP] --> J7[DISCGRP] --> J8[TCATBALF] --> J9[TRANTYPE] --> J11[DUSRSECJ]
  J11 --> S2[sleep 5] --> J12[POSTTRAN CBTRN02C] --> S3[sleep 10] --> J13[INTCALC CBACT04C] --> S4[sleep 5] --> J14[TRANBKP] --> J15[COMBTRAN] --> S5[sleep 5] --> J15b[TRANIDX] --> S6[sleep 5] --> J16[OPENFIL] --> B[bye]
```

##### Data
The script reads only the local JCL files. The submitted jobs touch these datasets:
- AWS.M2.CARDDEMO ACCTDATA, CARDDATA, CARDXREF, CUSTDATA, TRANSACT (KSDS 350-byte records, key 16 at offset 0; AIX key 26 at offset 304), DISCGRP, TCATBALF, TRANTYPE and USRSEC.
- DALYTRAN.PS and the DALYREJS GDG.
- The SYSTRAN, TRANSACT.BKUP and TRANSACT.COMBINED GDGs.

##### Outputs & side effects
- Echo text goes to the terminal.
- 15 job submissions are made to JES. The mainframe master files are rebuilt, transactions are posted, and interest transactions are generated and merged.
- The script does not capture any job output or return code.

##### External calls
- `tnftp` FTP client to localhost:2121, using JES submission (`quote site filetype=JES`, then `put`).
- `ps` and `grep`.
- Shell `sleep`, run through FTP's `!` escape.

##### Migration notes
- JES FTP submission is asynchronous. `put` returns once the job is queued, not when it completes. The only ordering controls are the fixed sleeps (5 or 10 seconds) and JES initiator/class serialization. Every job name is different, so jobs can overlap. Nothing checks return codes; a failed POSTTRAN does not stop INTCALC or TRANBKP.
- The step labelled "Refresh Transaction Data" actually runs TRANBKP, not TRANFILE. It backs up the current TRANSACT and empties it before posting. remote_refresh.sh uses TRANFILE (reload from DALYTRAN.PS.INIT) at the same position.
- TRANCATG is not run (Job 10 is skipped), unlike remote_refresh.sh. Two different steps are both labelled Job 15.
- The GDG relative generations (+1)/(0) depend on job completion order. TRANBKP runs twice, so COMBTRAN's BKUP(0) is the second generation, which holds the posted transactions, only if Job 14 finishes before COMBTRAN starts.
- The tunnel check is fragile. It counts `ps f` lines containing "2121:", which works only if the tunnel command line contains that text. When the tunnel is down, the script exits with code 0, which looks like success.
- The INTCALC date is fixed at 2022071800.
recommendation: Fully documented. In the migrated system, replace the fixed sleeps with explicit job-completion and RC dependencies. Confirm with the customer whether TRANBKP at Job 6 (rather than TRANFILE) and omitting TRANCATG are intended.

title: compile_batch.jcl.template + remote_compile.sh: batch COBOL compile/link job (IGYCRCTL -> IEBGENER -> HEWL)
description:
##### Entry point
- JCL job `COMPILEC`. It has an in-stream PROC `BLDBAT` that is invoked by `//STEP1 EXEC BLDBAT,MEM=ZZZZZZZZ`.
- The template is used by `scripts/remote_compile.sh <file_name> <ext> <basename>`. That script:
  1. Runs the tunnel guard.
  2. Runs `make -f Makefile`. No Makefile exists in the repo root or in scripts/.
  3. Rejects any extension other than `.cbl`.
  4. Runs `sed s/ZZZZZZZZ/<basename>/g` to produce `<basename>.tmp`.
  5. Submits the .tmp file via tnftp JES mode, then deletes it.

##### Inputs
- MEM: the program member name (8 characters or fewer).
- Source: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL(&MEM).
- Copybooks: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY.
- Job card: 'M2APP', CLASS=A, MSGCLASS=0, REGION=0M, NOTIFY=&SYSUID, TIME=1440.

##### Processing flow
1. COMPILE step: `PGM=IGYCRCTL` with PARM=(APOST,LIST,MAP,NUMBER) and STEPLIB IGY.SIGYCOMP.V63 (Enterprise COBOL 6.3).
   - SYSIN is the source member and SYSLIB is the copybook PDS.
   - SYSPRINT goes to AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LISTING(&MEM), DISP=SHR.
   - SYSLIN writes the object deck to &&LOADSET (MOD,PASS).
   - SYSUT1 through SYSUT15 and SYSMDECK are 3390 work files.
2. CBLPRINT step: `PGM=IEBGENER` copies the LISTING member to SYSOUT. It has no COND.
3. LKED step: `PGM=HEWL` with PARM='LIST,XREF'.
   - SYSLIB concatenates SYS1.LINKLIB, CSF.SCSFMOD0, CEE.SCEELKED, CEE.SCEELKEX and AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB.
   - SYSLIN is &&LOADSET (OLD,DELETE).
   - SYSLMOD is AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(&MEM).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[remote_compile.sh] --> M[make -f Makefile] --> E{ext == .cbl?}
  E -- no --> X[exit]
  E -- yes --> T[sed ZZZZZZZZ->basename > basename.tmp] --> R{rc==0?}
  R -- no --> X2[exit]
  R -- yes --> P[tnftp JES put basename.tmp] --> D[rm tmp]
  P --> J[COMPILEC STEP1 EXEC BLDBAT]
  J --> C1[COMPILE IGYCRCTL] --> C2[CBLPRINT IEBGENER] --> C3[LKED HEWL -> LOADLIB MEM]
```

##### Data
DD-to-DSN mapping:
| Step | DD | DSN | DISP |
|---|---|---|---|
| COMPILE | STEPLIB | IGY.SIGYCOMP.V63 | SHR |
| COMPILE | SYSIN | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL(&MEM) | SHR |
| COMPILE | SYSLIB | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY | SHR |
| COMPILE | SYSPRINT | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LISTING(&MEM) | SHR |
| COMPILE | SYSLIN | &&LOADSET | MOD,PASS |
| CBLPRINT | SYSUT1 | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LISTING(&MEM) | SHR |
| LKED | SYSLIB | SYS1.LINKLIB, CSF.SCSFMOD0, CEE.SCEELKED, CEE.SCEELKEX, AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB | SHR |
| LKED | SYSLIN | &&LOADSET | OLD,DELETE |
| LKED | SYSLMOD | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(&MEM) | SHR |

##### Outputs & side effects
- A load module is written to LOADLIB(&MEM).
- The compile listing is written to the LISTING PDS member and also copied to SYSOUT.

##### External calls
- IGYCRCTL (COBOL compiler), IEBGENER and HEWL (binder).
- From the shell side: make, sed and tnftp.

##### Migration notes
- LKED has no COND parameter, so it runs even if the compile failed (RC 12 or higher). It may then link a partial object or fail on an empty &&LOADSET.
- The template only suits batch programs that use no CICS or DB2 translator; there are no precompile steps.
- The literal placeholder ZZZZZZZZ is replaced everywhere, including the job body.
- remote_compile.sh calls `make -f Makefile`, but no Makefile exists, so that step fails and the script continues regardless. It also uses `[[ rc -ne 0 ]]`, where the variable is written without `$`; in bash arithmetic context this still evaluates the variable rc.
- CSF.SCSFMOD0 (ICSF) is in the link libraries.
recommendation: Fully documented. Build tooling only; replace it with the target build pipeline.

- Compiles the mainframe PDS copy, not the local file — local edits must be uploaded first (presumably by the missing Makefile).
- Temp file deleted even if FTP submit fails; exit status 0 on early exits.
